elitenet-archimedes-econet.title: !EliteNet
elitenet-archimedes-econet.upstream_name: !EliteNet: Elite over Econet for the Acorn Archimedes

runtime_profiles.name: !EliteNet application
runtime_profiles.notes: Requires Econet and Archimedes Elite version 1.14; the README states no minimum ARM model or RAM requirement.

source_language: original BBC BASIC and ARM assembly sources
elitenet-archimedes-econet.notes: Original MIT-licensed RISC OS application and module that add Econet multiplayer scoreboards to Archimedes Elite 1.14 while leaving the game itself untouched. The cross-host build assembles the ARM module, provides Archimedes tokenisation steps, and compares compiled binaries against the released originals.

dec0de-atari-st-deprotection.title: $DEC0DE — Atari ST deprotection
dec0de-atari-st-deprotection.notes: C tool removes documented protection schemes from ST programs, including Rob Northen Copylock series 1/2, Anti-bitos and several packers. Source and prebuilt binaries for ST and hosts are provided; each supported protection is listed in the README.

c64-15-second-format-disassembly.title: 15 Second Format
c64-15-second-format-disassembly.display_title: 15 Second Format — C64 and 1541 utility disassembly
c64-15-second-format-disassembly.notes: Dave McMurtrie disassembled a historical C64/1541 fast-format utility; 64tass source separates host and drive code. The README names a historical PRG and assembly command, without claiming byte-identical output or a verified run.

180-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

25vibe128-raycasting-sdk.title: 2.5vibe128
25vibe128-raycasting-sdk.notes: Standalone native Commodore 128 VIC-IIe 2.5D SDK derived solely from the 3Dvibe64 2.5D pipeline, not its polygon engine. Python builder, native assembly, border FAST acceleration, bitmap/double buffering and four original/optimized automatic/interactive demos. Assembly guide describes 6502-compatible instructions; exact native CPU variant merits follow-up. Upstream documents VICE x128 testing; physical hardware has not been tested. Code/data are PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. The project is original Commodore 128 / VIC-IIe SDK/homebrew work, so source CPU is not applicable; its checked-in 6502-compatible assembly and 64tass build establish 6502 output without implying a narrower chip variant or RAM minimum.

25vibeplus4-raycasting-sdk.title: 2.5vibePlus4
25vibeplus4-raycasting-sdk.notes: Standalone native Plus/4 TED 2.5D SDK derived solely from the 3Dvibe64 2.5D pipeline, not its polygon engine. Python builder, native assembly, bitmap/double buffering and four original/optimized automatic/interactive demos. Assembly guide describes 6502-compatible instructions; exact native CPU variant merits follow-up. Upstream documents VICE xplus4 testing; physical hardware has not been tested. Code/data are PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. The project is original Commodore Plus/4 / TED SDK/homebrew work, so source CPU is not applicable; its checked-in 6502-compatible assembly and 64tass build establish 6502 output without implying a narrower chip variant or RAM minimum.

25vibevic-vic20-raycasting-sdk.title: 2.5vibeVic

runtime_profiles.notes: Requires 24 KB RAM expansion in blocks 1/2/3; unexpanded VIC-20 unsupported. Upstream tests use VICE xvic, not physical hardware.

25vibevic-vic20-raycasting-sdk.notes: Standalone native VIC-20 DDA raycaster derived from the qualified 3Dvibe64 raycast-stock experiment, not its polygon engine. Python builder, 6502 assembly runtime, maps and four generated demo PRGs cover monochrome and multicolor character-glyph framebuffers. Requires 24 KB RAM expansion in blocks 1/2/3; unexpanded VIC-20 is unsupported. Upstream reports VICE xvic measurements; real hardware has not been tested. Code/data are PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0.

runtime_profiles.notes: Runs as a normal Atari cartridge ROM in Stella or on real hardware using a Harmony cartridge; PAL mode is selected with the TV TYPE switch.

2048-atari-2600.notes: Atari 2600 port of the 2048 puzzle game with one- and two-player modes. Primary source documents the DASM build and declares PROCESSOR 6502. This is an original homebrew port, not reverse-engineered software.

c64-rohingosling-3d-cube-commodore.title: 3D Cube
c64-rohingosling-3d-cube-commodore.notes: Author disassembled surviving VIC-20 and C64 PRGs of a historical personal 3D cube demo and recast them as modifiable Kick Assembler projects. Both computer builds and running instructions are documented; provenance is recovered own binary, not an original source archive.

deathchase-spectrum.title: 3D Deathchase
deathchase-spectrum.notes: Disassembly and annotation of the 1983 ZX Spectrum game Deathchase by Ritchie Swann.

3dvibe64-c64-graphics-sdk.title: 3Dvibe64
3dvibe64-c64-graphics-sdk.notes: Source SDK for eight C64 graphics modes: polygon rendering and a distinct Mode 8 2.5D DDA bitmap renderer. PowerShell/Python scene builder emits 6510/6502 assembly for 64tass; example JSON and guides are included. Mode 8 has no wall UV textures or room-over-room, and is not the historical character-cell renderer. Upstream qualifies stock VICE x64sc; real hardware has not been tested. Code/data are PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. The repository documents Codex-assisted use of the SDK, not independently verified AI authorship of the engine.

4-to-4-back-to-the-future-amstrad-cpc.title: 4 to 4 Back to the Future — Amstrad CPC native game source
4-to-4-back-to-the-future-amstrad-cpc.display_title: 4 to 4 Back to the Future — Amstrad CPC native game source
types: native BASIC and assembly homebrew source release
4-to-4-back-to-the-future-amstrad-cpc.status: Original native source release; no independent compilation or execution in this review.
4-to-4-back-to-the-future-amstrad-cpc.notes: Original September 2015 CPC game by the cpc-power.com team, released as BASIC listings, Z80 components and explanatory source notes. Upstream reports fourth place in CPCRetroDev 2015 and credits Bruno Kukulcan, Tom & Jerry/GPA, CED and testers. Original competition game with a Back to the Future theme. Interpreted Locomotive BASIC is part of the native CPC program; no host game-specific guest CPU wrapper is included in this classification. README requires manual WinAPE assembly and BASIC autotype, plus separate image conversion, compression and DSK preparation tools. An automated complete reconstruction of the distributable was not established; no build/run/play/byte-exact result is asserted. Reviewed on 2026-10-05; no independent build or execution was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/CPCRetroDev/4to4BackToTheFuture/blob/master/README.md https://github.com/CPCRetroDev/4to4BackToTheFuture/blob/master/src/files_source_code_and_explanation.txt https://github.com/CPCRetroDev/4to4BackToTheFuture/blob/master/src/ingame-RSX.asm. Latest upstream commit: https://github.com/CPCRetroDev/4to4BackToTheFuture/commit/47ac20e09c5d2d5c4fa5a9726347a64ae680508f

multiply-test-6502-benchmarks.title: 6502 Integer Multiplication
multiply-test-6502-benchmarks.notes: Research and reproducible cycle/memory comparisons of more than 120 credited 6502 multiplication routines; useful developer reference, not a game disassembly.

6502net-cross-assembler.title: 6502.Net — multi-CPU cross assembler
6502net-cross-assembler.notes: .NET macro assembler with 6502 family, 6800/6809, Z80/8080 and 8086 targets, documentation, a disassembler and tests; representative systems listed, not a claim of an analyzed CPC binary.

sourcegen-6502bench.title: 6502bench

runtime_profiles.name: SourceGen desktop application
runtime_profiles.os: Windows 7 SP1 or later with Microsoft .NET Framework 4.8.1
runtime_profiles.notes: README also reports Wine 9+ operation; no minimum CPU or RAM is stated.

sourcegen-6502bench.notes: Interactive SourceGen workbench for 6502-family binaries. It traces reachable code and processor flags, handles undocumented opcodes and 65816 register widths, emits source for multiple assemblers, invokes them for verification and stores shareable JSON project metadata without embedding original binary contents.

6502life-acorn-simulation.title: 6502Life
6502life-acorn-simulation.display_title: 6502Life — native Acorn Game of Life implementations
6502life-acorn-simulation.notes: Native 6502 implementations compare dense/list-based Game of Life algorithms, pan/zoom UI and banked-memory coprocessor variants. BeebAsm script assembles top-level variants and builds SSD. ALIFE and Apple Life historical sources are credited separately. No independent compile/run. Not a game disassembly; one coherent native-retro development/simulation repository. Variant memory requirements differ. README documents runnable Life variants and controls; build.sh assembles and creates an SSD using BeebAsm and mmb_utils. No independent build or coprocessor test.

8bit-analysers.title: 8-Bit Analysers
8bit-analysers.notes: Multi-platform analysis/annotation toolkit for 8-bit games. Includes Spectrum, C64 and CPC analysers, assembler export support and MCP analysis tooling; tracked as adjacent reverse-engineering infrastructure.

c64-mist64-80columns.title: 80columns
c64-mist64-80columns.notes: Reconstructed and optimized historical 80COLUMNS.PRG, whose original author is unidentified. cc65/exomizer build emits a 2.2 KB runnable C64 80x25 screen utility, with alternate character sets.

8192-c64-homebrew.notes: Original 2048-style C64 puzzle game. Upstream marks version 0.3 alpha playable with music and sound effects while menu, persistence and other features remain incomplete. ca65/ld65 Makefile builds a D64 using exomizer/mkd64 and provides a VICE run target; main.s implements native game flow.

8bit-unity-native-6502-game-sdk.title: 8bit-Unity — cross-platform 6502 game SDK
8bit-unity-native-6502-game-sdk.status: Original native source release; no independent compilation or execution in this review.
8bit-unity-native-6502-game-sdk.notes: Anthony Beaucamp’s original cross-development SDK combines CC65 target drivers, game projects and a script-generating builder. The C64 VIC-II driver directly configures target hardware. README lists the 6502-based output families and Windows/Linux builder workflows; these host environments are not claims of native Windows/Linux game ports. SDK and bundled sample projects form one coherent development-tool root. CC65 is a dependency, not a reconstructed historical subject. README documents loading .builder projects and generating disk/ROM scripts, with releases hosting additional tools. No successful current source build or SDK execution was established, so compilation and run flags remain null. Playability and original-binary matching do not apply to the SDK as a whole. Reviewed on 2026-10-05; no independent build or execution was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/8bit-Dude/8bit-Unity/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/8bit-Dude/8bit-Unity/blob/main/unity/targets/c64/VIC2.c https://github.com/8bit-Dude/8bit-Unity/blob/main/build/_readme_.txt. Latest upstream commit: https://github.com/8bit-Dude/8bit-Unity/commit/8776333e16c7bfd18e39b0d78dfc3f4601626ddc

8bitworkshop-retro-browser-ide.title: 8bitworkshop
source_language: 6502, Z80 and other platform development toolchains
8bitworkshop-retro-browser-ide.notes: Browser IDE compiles or assembles source locally in the browser and runs it in bundled emulators, with breakpoints, disassembly, memory inspection, probes and replay. README names C64, CPC, Spectrum, Apple II and Atari 8-bit among many targets; supports code creation and analysis, not binary-derived restoration of any one game.

kastely-c64-reconstruction-web.title: A Kastély — C64 reverse-engineering toolkit and browser game
kastely-c64-reconstruction-web.display_title: A Kastély — C64 reverse-engineering toolkit and browser game
types: Game-specific reverse engineering and data-driven game reimplementation
kastely-c64-reconstruction-web.status: Java 17 reverse-engineering/export toolkit plus an upstream-described playable browser reconstruction; partial metadata decoding remains.
kastely-c64-reconstruction-web.notes: Java decoders/exporter extract a structured Kastély model from original D64 images. GameModelBuilder consumes disk-derived room, combat and conversation structures; TypeScript implements combat/state/verbs directly. This is substantive reconstructed game logic, not merely a C64-emulator wrapper. GameModelBuilder retains a partial decode of sprite/enemy-seed metadata. jsidplay2 supports Java runtime tracing; jsSID supplies browser audio. Neither replaces the direct reconstructed browser game rules. Artifact-host compatibility is not proof of AI-assisted authorship. Single coherent toolkit plus reconstructed web-game project for Mantis Software's 1993 Hungarian adventure. Original D64 disk images are not included and are required locally for extraction/verification. README calls the project a non-clean-room tribute; no blanket license for original game assets or repository-wide license was established. Reviewed 2026-10-05 by primary documentation, source, build-file and tree inspection. All local build, test, emulation and runtime checks remain unperformed. Positive flags are evidence-scoped upstream reports only; byte_exact remains unknown. Last activity is the latest default-branch commit date, not repository creation or pushed_at. Evidence: https://github.com/virtualparadox/a-kastely/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/virtualparadox/a-kastely/blob/main/src/main/java/eu/virtualparadox/castle/export/GameModelBuilder.java https://github.com/virtualparadox/a-kastely/blob/main/src-web/src/engine/combat.ts https://github.com/virtualparadox/a-kastely/blob/main/src-web/README.md https://github.com/virtualparadox/a-kastely/blob/main/pom.xml https://github.com/virtualparadox/a-kastely/blob/main/src-web/package.json https://github.com/virtualparadox/a-kastely/commit/c8915f69f9b7f2745fea0d34acc643efda292f07

avtak-c64-unorig.title: A View to a Kill
avtak-c64-unorig.display_title: A View to a Kill — C64 reverse-engineered source
avtak-c64-unorig.notes: Slowly progressing reverse-engineering/decompilation of the C64 game. The repository keeps 6502bench analysis projects and assembly exported for 64tass, with game/map observations intended to support bug understanding and eventual fixes.

a2-hires-lab-apple2-lode-runner.title: a2-hires-lab
a2-hires-lab-apple2-lode-runner.display_title: a2-hires-lab — Apple II Lode Runner graphics workbench

runtime_profiles.notes: Excel for Microsoft 365 or Excel 2024 with macros enabled; web Excel cannot run VBA. Author tested on Windows 11.

source_language: Apple II Lode Runner 6502 disassembly and sprite tables
a2-hires-lab-apple2-lode-runner.notes: Excel/VBA workbench exploring the original Apple II Lode Runner sprite bytes, two-stage shift tables and HGR memory/NTSC color behavior using data from XekriRedmane's disassembly. The author quantifies a possible direct-table optimization; this is an analysis experiment, not a patch to the original game. VBA source is exported in src/bas. README documents Windows Excel 365/2024 and manual workbook checks; Python shift-table tests exist. HISTORY explicitly describes LLM sessions and corrected Gemini-authored assembly explanations. The author's separate a2-lode-runner work is already tracked; this workbook is distinct.

a2scsi-rom-gorlik.title: a2scsi-rom
a2scsi-rom-gorlik.display_title: Apple II SCSI Card ROM — annotated disassembly
a2scsi-rom-gorlik.notes: Commented disassembly of Apple II SCSI Card ROM revision 341-0437-A (rev. c), with sixteen 1 KiB banks and SourceGen project files. Its Makefile reassembles the complete ROM for EPROM programming or MAME; the README also documents driver interactions and firmware behavior. Byte-exact output is not asserted.

abadia-cpc-web-reimplementation.title: abadia
abadia-cpc-web-reimplementation.display_title: La Abadía del Crimen — CPC-derived Web reimplementation
source_language: CPC game assets and credited prior disassembly
abadia-cpc-web-reimplementation.notes: Authored browser game logic and scenes using assets from the CPC version and explicitly crediting Giner/Pazos disassembly/SDL work; README calls it playable with known bugs. Distinct Web implementation, not an independently recovered CPC disassembly.

abm-apple2-6502disassembly.title: ABM
abm-apple2-6502disassembly.display_title: ABM — Apple II game disassembly & engine analysis
abm-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Apple II ABM disassembly covering the game, paddle-read routine and Applesoft loader/configuration programs. The SourceGen project uses an extension script to format heavy inline data and documents self-modifying code, floating-point use, collision behavior and incremental explosion rendering.

acebasic-amiga-compiler.title: ACE - Amiga BASIC Compiler - Enhanced
acebasic-amiga-compiler.display_title: ACE BASIC — enhanced native Amiga compiler
acebasic-amiga-compiler.notes: Historical ACE BASIC compiler continued with a modern VBCC build, 68020-native output (optional 68000 mode), classes/generic methods, closures and Amiga graphics/UI/network libraries. Actual parser/code generator, assembly runtime and ARexx tests are present. Original-source continuation/restoration, not binary-derived reconstruction. AI guidance is explicit; byte matching is not.

ace-amiga-c-engine.title: ACE - Amiga C Engine
ace-amiga-c-engine.display_title: ACE — Amiga C game engine and asset tools

runtime_profiles.name: ACE library baseline
runtime_profiles.notes: Root README explicitly states Kickstart 1.3 requirement. OCS-oriented implementation and experimental AGA extensions do not prove an exact minimum CPU/RAM for every dependent game.

ace-amiga-c-engine.notes: Thin C framework that directly manages classic Amiga hardware, temporarily disables/restores the OS, and supplies audio, blitter, copper, input, view, tilemap and asset-conversion support. The repository includes a showcase and host-side converters. The documentation targets 68000 and Kickstart 1.3; no executable minimum RAM is asserted.

aces-pacific-kylofon-sdl3.title: Aces of the Pacific — native SDL3 reconstruction
aces-pacific-kylofon-sdl3.display_title: Aces of the Pacific — native SDL3 reconstruction

execution_paths.name: Native reconstructed output
execution_paths.notes: Historical behavior is implemented in maintained host code; reference emulators or audio-chip models do not execute the game CPU in this play path.

aces-pacific-kylofon-sdl3.status: Author-reported playable port; catalogue review did not build or run it.
aces-pacific-kylofon-sdl3.notes: Native C reconstruction of INTRO.EXE, PS.EXE and AP.EXE in one process, based on CD version 1.2. VGA/AdLib gameplay is reported working; other sound devices and reported carrier-deck rendering issues remain. Original executable/data resources are required. Reviewed on 2026-10-05; build/playability claims are upstream reports, not independent execution. Evidence: https://github.com/kylofon/aces-of-the-pacific-sdl3/blob/master/README.md https://github.com/kylofon/aces-of-the-pacific-sdl3/blob/master/aotpport/PORTING.md https://github.com/kylofon/aces-of-the-pacific-sdl3/blob/master/aotpport/src/sim_flow/flight_loop.c https://github.com/kylofon/aces-of-the-pacific-sdl3/commit/689914f7ede0e3ebe8ab44ea0d537025122217d2 Published build: https://github.com/kylofon/aces-of-the-pacific-sdl3/releases/tag/v0.1.0

acorn-6502-copro-os-seddon.title: Acorn 6502 Second Processor OS
acorn-6502-copro-os-seddon.display_title: Acorn 6502 Second Processor OS — buildable ROM disassembly
acorn-6502-copro-os-seddon.notes: Buildable disassembly of Acorn's 6502 second-processor and Master Turbo OS ROMs. It builds 4 KiB ROM images on modern Windows/macOS/Linux systems and verifies supported 1.10/1.20 outputs against reference ROMs.

acorn-tube-client-acornaeology.title: Acorn 6502 Tube Client — ROM reconstruction
acorn-tube-client-acornaeology.notes: Annotated disassembly of external and Master Turbo internal v1.10 Tube Client ROM variants, generated from original bytes and reassembled with beebasm in CI.

acorn-adfs-acornaeology.title: Acorn ADFS 1.30 — ROM reconstruction
acorn-adfs-acornaeology.notes: Annotated ADFS 1.30 filing-system ROM disassembly, including disc and SCSI paths; README documents beebasm byte-for-byte reassembly and CI verification.

acorn-econet-bridge-acornaeology.title: Acorn Econet Bridge — firmware reconstruction
acorn-econet-bridge-acornaeology.notes: Annotated variant 1 bridge firmware disassembly from the standalone 6502-based network device; README documents beebasm byte-for-byte reassembly and CI verification.

electron-speed-tricks.title: Acorn Electron speed tricks
electron-speed-tricks.notes: Annotated BASIC and inline assembly SPEED.txt demonstrates and times Electron screen mode, keyboard and MOS speed techniques. Contains source; CLK limitations documented.

acorn-mos-disassembly-seddon.title: Acorn MOS
acorn-mos-disassembly-seddon.display_title: Acorn MOS — Master-series ROM disassembly & reconstruction
acorn-mos-disassembly-seddon.notes: Work-in-progress disassembly of multiple released and unreleased Acorn MOS versions for the 8-bit Master family and derivatives. The shared source is intended to be modifiable and builds original ROM variants that are checked against the reference ROMs; the project also produces experimental refreshed MOS variants.

acorn-nfs-anfs-disassembly.title: Acorn NFS and ANFS — BBC Micro ROM disassemblies
acorn-nfs-anfs-disassembly.upstream_name: Acorn NFS and ANFS — BBC Micro ROM disassemblies
acorn-nfs-anfs-disassembly.display_title: Acorn NFS and ANFS — BBC Micro ROM disassemblies
acorn-nfs-anfs-disassembly.notes: Annotated Acorn Network Filing System and Advanced NFS ROMs across multiple 3.x and 4.x versions. The project documents label/comment cross-references, version comparisons and dasmos/fantasm generation; CI reassembles with BeebAsm and compares each supported ROM byte for byte. README documents an 8 KB NFS and 16 KB ANFS successor.

acornaeology-disassembly-site-generator.title: Acornaeology disassembly site generator
source_language: annotated disassembly JSON and version metadata
acornaeology-disassembly-site-generator.notes: Python generator consumes version manifests and disassembly JSON from individual Acornaeology repositories, renders formatted source and resolves cross-version address links. Its data/sources.json lists six source repositories; five were already tracked before this batch and acorn-nfs is reviewed here. The generator itself is a distinct publication tool, not another ROM disassembly.

iso-pascal-bbc-electron-zornslemma.title: Acornsoft ISO Pascal ROM disassembly
iso-pascal-bbc-electron-zornslemma.notes: ISO Pascal v1.10 ROM analysis for a possible combined 32K ROM, with two ROM-specific Python disassembly passes, CPU interpreter and source. Goal and provenance described in README; combined ROM not established.

action-replay-5-amiga.title: Action Replay 5
action-replay-5-amiga.notes: Builds an expanded Amiga Action Replay debugger from Action Replay III and reverse-engineered ARIV/Action Replay IV material, combining original and newly authored code. README documents DeMoN cartridge, WinUAE, original cartridge and software modes; makefile assembles 68000 sources with vasm. A vasm build recipe is present, but a successful current build, output/runtime variants and binary equality have not been verified.

adf-opus-2025.title: ADF Opus 2025
adf-opus-2025.display_title: ADF Opus 2025 — Amiga disk image workbench
source_language: Amiga ADF and OFS/FFS disk structures
adf-opus-2025.notes: 2025 revival of the original 2003 ADF Opus source; offers disk-image browsing, raw bootblock inspection and Greaseweazle support for physical floppy reads/writes. Based on preserved source, not a claim to have reconstructed the old binary.

adf-reader-writer-js.title: ADF reader/writer
adf-reader-writer-js.display_title: ADF reader/writer — Amiga OFS/FFS image inspector
source_language: Amiga OFS/FFS filesystem and ADF/HDF images
adf-reader-writer-js.notes: Plain JavaScript OFS/FFS reader/writer for ADF and HDF images, with extraction and raw-sector access useful for recovering files from damaged images. Multi-partition HDFs are not supported.

adf7z-amiga-filesystem.title: Adf7z
adf7z-amiga-filesystem.notes: 7-Zip format plugin for extracting Amiga OFS/FFS files from ADF images. README limits it to read/extract operations: links and attributes are not supported, and ADF creation or modification is unavailable.

adfexplorer-r-amiga-disk-analysis.title: adfExplorer
adfexplorer-r-amiga-disk-analysis.display_title: adfExplorer — R analysis of Amiga ADF files
source_language: Amiga OFS/FFS ADF and ADZ disk files
adfexplorer-r-amiga-disk-analysis.notes: R package for programmatic inspection and writing of Amiga ADF images, including batch file transfer. README explicitly limits it to older AmigaOS media and excludes extended ADF flux/MFM information used for some protected disks. Separate R interface and analytics from ADFlib's C implementation.

adfinder-amiga-disk-manager-ginnov.title: ADFinder
adfinder-amiga-disk-manager-ginnov.display_title: ADFinder — Amiga ADF/HDF manager for macOS
adfinder-amiga-disk-manager-ginnov.notes: Native macOS manager to create, inspect, compare and modify Amiga ADF/HDF media. Its own README identifies ADFlib as the shared C library dependency and says public downloads are disabled pending provenance/compliance checks. This is an application consumer with distinct disk-image workflows, not an independent reimplementation of ADFlib.

adflib-amiga-filesystem.title: ADFlib
adflib-amiga-filesystem.notes: Portable C implementation of Amiga OFS/FFS for ADF/HDF and disk diagnostics, with metadata, bitmap and salvage utilities. README labels native-device handling and RDB writing experimental and warns that dircache writing has limited test coverage.

adflib-rust-vschwaberow-amiga-media.title: adflib (Rust)
adflib-rust-vschwaberow-amiga-media.display_title: adflib (Rust) — Amiga ADF, DMS and Hunk parsers
source_language: ADF/OFS/FFS, DMS and Amiga Hunk structures
adflib-rust-vschwaberow-amiga-media.notes: Separate pure Rust implementation inspired by Laurent Clévy's C ADFlib, according to README. Inspected src/disk.rs, dms.rs and hunk.rs contain disk, compressed-image and Hunk structures/parsing code. README describes incomplete support, specifically add/create plans; archived repository and build/runtime capabilities unverified.

aexp-amiga-mega65-core.title: AExp
aexp-amiga-mega65-core.display_title: AExp — Amiga 500 FPGA core for MEGA65

runtime_profiles.name: MEGA65 FPGA core
runtime_profiles.notes: Developer guide supports R3/R3A, R4, R5 and R6. Requires a legal 256 KiB Kickstart 1.3 ROM and FAT32 SD media. Guest Amiga memory sizes are not host hardware minima.

aexp-amiga-mega65-core.notes: Minimig-derived general Amiga 500 OCS/PAL FPGA implementation for MEGA65 with fx68k CPU, floppy images, display and input support. Source-build and installation paths are documented. The modeled 512 KiB Chip plus 512 KiB Slow RAM describe the guest, not a host RAM minimum; broad compatibility is an upstream claim.

after-shock-spectrum.title: After Shock
after-shock-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

aha-arm-thumb-superoptimiser-dpt.title: Aha!
aha-arm-thumb-superoptimiser-dpt.notes: Adaptation of Henry S. Warren's Aha! instruction superoptimiser. README identifies added ARM/Thumb-oriented BIC and RSB handling and preserves original source on the distrib branch; Makefile synthesizes short sequences from sample C fragments. Not an original Warren source claim or analysis of a particular RISC OS program.

ahx2play-native-replayer.title: ahx2play
ahx2play-native-replayer.notes: Direct C port of the AHX tracker's internal replay implementation, with Paula sound-chip modeling and SDL/WinMM output adapters. replayer.c explicitly preserves edge cases from the original 68020 version. CMake builds a native player; sound-chip modeling does not make this a guest-CPU wrapper. No independent compile/audio test.

air-sea-attack-cvbasic-port.title: Air/Sea Attack — CVBasic port
air-sea-attack-cvbasic-port.display_title: Air/Sea Attack — CVBasic reconstruction and port
air-sea-attack-cvbasic-port.status: Native CVBasic rewrite with source and three documented target-family builds.
air-sea-attack-cvbasic-port.notes: README states original CreatiVision 6502 binary was disassembled and rewritten in CVBasic. Substantial source implements semantic game states rather than a CPU interpreter. Build script invokes CVBasic/gasm80 for all three target families and supplies SG, COL and MSX ROM names. Source references an intermediate semantic C port but does not publish its provenance here. Original assets/design remain separately copyrighted. Build instructions and prebuilt release claims are upstream evidence only; no parity or hardware tests. README reports prebuilt ROMs and gameplay imagery; build recipe invokes CVBasic v0.9.2/gasm80 for each target. Positive fields are upstream port/release evidence only; no independent parity, compile or hardware verification. No independent compilation, execution, gameplay, hardware or byte-exact verification was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/siriokds/Air-Sea-Attack-CVBasic/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/siriokds/Air-Sea-Attack-CVBasic/blob/main/src/airsea.bas https://github.com/siriokds/Air-Sea-Attack-CVBasic/blob/main/src/build.sh https://github.com/siriokds/Air-Sea-Attack-CVBasic/commit/5f61956c538b66d47ac2ad5109218ee39b439db5

airwolf-monogame-alaiing.title: Airwolf2023
airwolf-monogame-alaiing.notes: Original C#/MonoGame re-creation of the CPC Airwolf gameplay with real level, enemy, helicopter, collision and UI code. Creator explicitly says it is not emulation, recreates only gameplay and may omit original features. This is a modern remake, not a native CPC port or a claimed disassembly. Source and .NET 6/MonoGame project inspected; build, runnable release and gameplay completion were not verified.

akalabeth-sg1000-sc3000-port.title: Akalabeth
akalabeth-sg1000-sc3000-port.status: Released native C port; v0.8.2 adds SC-3000 keyboard support.
akalabeth-sg1000-sc3000-port.notes: Repository description establishes SG-1000/SC-3000 target. Native C implements character creation, world generation, dungeons, monsters and gameplay. Included BASIC source credits nanochess's 2019 GW-BASIC adaptation, making that the directly evidenced source lineage. SDCC Makefile emits Akalabeth.sg. Release 0.8.2 supplies a 48 KiB ROM and SC-3000 keyboard fixes. No top-level README or independent build/playtest. Build needs SDCC, ihx2sms, folder2c and target libraries. Do not label a new Apple II disassembly; this is a native C adaptation with a GW-BASIC reference. Upstream v0.8.1 explicitly says compiled with SDCC 4.5; v0.8.2 ships 48 KiB Akalabeth.sg and fixes keyboard controls. These support upstream build/runtime/playability, not an independent build or exact match. No independent compilation, execution, gameplay, hardware or byte-exact verification was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/amoibos/Akalabeth/blob/main/Makefile https://github.com/amoibos/Akalabeth/blob/main/main.c https://github.com/amoibos/Akalabeth/blob/main/engine.c https://github.com/amoibos/Akalabeth/blob/main/misc/Akalabeth_orig.bas https://github.com/amoibos/Akalabeth/commit/efe1d7af0c2ee11d19c07a840d82704b98c61e48 https://github.com/amoibos/Akalabeth/releases/tag/0.8.2

akikowolf-cd32-native-port.title: Akiko Wolf
akikowolf-cd32-native-port.display_title: Akiko Wolf — native CD32 Wolfenstein 3D port

runtime_profiles.name: Stock CD32 shareware game
runtime_profiles.notes: Root README describes unmodified CD32 performance. Exact CPU/RAM minimum is not inferred solely from the platform; source compilation target is recorded separately.

akikowolf-cd32-native-port.notes: CD32-optimized shareware Wolfenstein 3D source port with controller mapping and rendering optimizations. Credits AWolf, the PSP port and id Software. Source includes SAS/C build instructions and 68020 assembly; root supplies a CD32 ISO. README notes graphical/gameplay glitches and planned sound/music rather than claiming a complete port. No local build/play test.

akira-famicom-g0me3.title: Akira
akira-famicom-g0me3.notes: The author's Back From Source repository reconstructs the Famicom Akira program in banked assembly and includes a DASM build script for an NES image. RetroRE labels this a partial reverse engineering effort. Reassembly exists as a documented script; successful execution and byte identity have not been verified.

akumajou-dracula-x68000-15khz.title: Akumajou Dracula — X68000 15 kHz display hack
akumajou-dracula-x68000-15khz.display_title: Akumajou Dracula — X68000 15 kHz display hack

runtime_profiles.name: 15 kHz X68000 build
runtime_profiles.notes: Requires the original game files; tested on a real Sharp X68000 Compact with 15 kHz output. No RAM minimum is stated.

akumajou-dracula-x68000-15khz.notes: Fan-made 15 kHz display conversion for the original X68000 Akumajou Dracula, generated from a source disassembly and built with the documented run68x assembler/linker flow. It requires user-supplied original game files and has been tested on real X68000 Compact hardware; it is not described as an original-source restoration.

aleste-msx2-vdp-archive.title: Aleste520EX
aleste-msx2-vdp-archive.display_title: Aleste 520EX — MSX2 game VDP patch analysis
source_language: MSX2 Vampire Killer game ROM and patch binaries
aleste-msx2-vdp-archive.notes: The Documentation/VDP Emulator directory supplies original/patched Vampire Killer Z80 listings and diffs explaining Aleste game BIOS/VDP adaptation; surrounding repository is a broader Aleste hardware/software archive. Build and current playability not established.

vs-sr-cd32-alfredchicken.title: Alfred Chicken — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-alfredchicken.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Alfred Chicken. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

ali-baba-apple2-xekri.title: Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves — Apple II reconstruction
ali-baba-apple2-xekri.upstream_name: Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves
ali-baba-apple2-xekri.display_title: Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves — Apple II reconstruction
subjects: Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves
ali-baba-apple2-xekri.notes: Literate reverse engineering of Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves for Apple II. The build tangles and assembles reconstructed sources and can rebuild/verify the full disk image byte-for-byte against the reference.

alice-personal-pascal-source-restoration.title: Alice Personal Pascal
alice-personal-pascal-source-restoration.display_title: Alice Personal Pascal — historical IDE source and portability work
alice-personal-pascal-source-restoration.notes: Preserves Alice's Atari ST source and the original DOS-derived Unix port as groundwork for portability. Alice is a syntax-directed Pascal editor/interpreter with debugging. The atari source includes GEM UI and native assembly; the Unix Makefile links ncurses. Haiku is an announced goal, not a verified working output. README says the Atari source needs cleanup before useful builds. CPU fields cover the inspected native ST assembly only; the DOS-derived C provenance does not establish an exact DOS CPU or modern host CPU.

alien-spectrum.title: Alien
alien-spectrum.notes: Fully annotated disassembly; rebuilt image is byte-identical to the tape and a dependency-free web port has a parity suite.

alien-c64-python-remake.title: Alien (1984) — Python remake and disassembly
alien-c64-python-remake.notes: Playable Python reimplementation of the 1984 C64 Alien built from a complete disassembly of the original disk. The repository also includes alientools for NIB/G64/D64 decoding, CBM-DOS reconstruction, program extraction and disassembly, plus annotated RE documentation and an ORIGINAL mode intended to reproduce observed disk behaviour. The maintained output is a portable Python 3.12+ program rather than a fixed native CPU target; the reviewed README gives no minimum CPU or RAM requirement.

alien8-tcdev-spectrum.title: Alien 8 — tcdev
alien8-tcdev-spectrum.notes: tcdev reverse-engineering project; repository marks Alien 8 as WIP and aims for reassemblable/relocatable source.

alien-breed-3d-source-derived-pc-port.title: Alien Breed 3D I
alien-breed-3d-source-derived-pc-port.display_title: Alien Breed 3D — Amiga source-derived C port
alien-breed-3d-source-derived-pc-port.notes: Native C reimplementation of the original Amiga game's gameplay and renderer, using the historical 68000 assembly source as reference and preserving Amiga data formats. SDL2 desktop and Emscripten builds are documented. This is source-derived porting, not a disassembly of an Amiga binary; no Amiga executable is run by the port.

alien-breed-amiga-hitchhikr.title: Alien Breed — Amiga disassembly
alien-breed-amiga-hitchhikr.notes: Complete Amiga Alien Breed disassembly from the Disk 2 executable. The build extracts the original binary, assembles reconstructed hunks, joins them into an executable and provides emulator-based original/generated testing; the project also removes self-modifying code and comments large portions of the program.

alien-soldier-mega-drive-source-reconstr.title: alien_soldier_src
alien-soldier-mega-drive-source-reconstr.display_title: Alien Soldier — byte-identical Mega Drive source reconstruction

runtime_profiles.name: Japanese ROM reconstruction
runtime_profiles.notes: Byte-identical Japanese cartridge includes reconstructed 68000 code and Z80 sound components and is validated through twelve emulator checkpoints; no minimum RAM is stated.

alien-soldier-mega-drive-source-reconstr.notes: Source Reconstruction 1.0 for the Japanese cartridge. The AS-based build reproduces the canonical 2 MB ROM byte for byte, validates symbols/layout/assets, replays twelve emulator checkpoints, traces CPU behavior and preserves confidence/provenance boundaries.

alis-silmarils-vm.title: ALIS — Silmarils virtual machine
alis-silmarils-vm.notes: Reimplements Silmarils ALIS VM using original game data. Primary compatibility matrix marks multiple ST and Amiga versions playable (including Mad Show, Targhan, Colorado), while Manhattan Dealers and Operation: Cleanstreets are broken; playability is per game/version, not universal.

alpha-waves-atari-original-source.title: Alpha Waves
alpha-waves-atari-original-source.display_title: Alpha Waves — original Atari ST source archive
alpha-waves-atari-original-source.notes: Preserves Christophe de Dinechin's Alpha Waves source archive, including the large Cube game implementation, ST polygon-fill routines and original assets. cube.s identifies the 1990 author/project and enables VERSION_ST. README links the original archive and community build work, but warns that the expanded Git source has damaged newline formatting and recommends using Alpha-Waves.zip. No reproducible clean build or current runtime is asserted. Conditional Amiga code does not establish a complete Amiga port in this archive.

alynxdj-atari-lynx-music-tracker.title: ALYNXDJ
alynxdj-atari-lynx-music-tracker.display_title: ALYNXDJ — original Atari Lynx music tracker

runtime_profiles.name: Atari Lynx ROM
runtime_profiles.notes: Primary design documentation states one 65C02, 64 KiB unified RAM and native Mikey/Suzy use; save persistence additionally requires a 2 KiB 93C86-compatible EEPROM.

alynxdj-atari-lynx-music-tracker.notes: Original Lynx homebrew music tracker, not reverse-engineered or RE-derived. Upstream documents a native 65C02 .lnx build, real-hardware validation, four-channel Mikey synthesis, streamed PCM kits, EEPROM persistence and ComLynx/MIDI bridging.

amaurote-128-spectrum-analyser.title: Amaurote 128
amaurote-128-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Amaurote128 directory contains an approximately 942 KiB Analysis.json annotation database; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

amber-remix-amiga-amberstar.title: Amber Remix — Amiga Amberstar data decoder
amber-remix-amiga-amberstar.upstream_name: Amber Remix — Amiga Amberstar data decoder
amber-remix-amiga-amberstar.display_title: Amber Remix — Amiga Amberstar data decoder
amber-remix-amiga-amberstar.notes: Rust decoder/playback for original Amiga Amberstar containers, text, graphics, maps and Hippel-CoSo music; scripts and items are only partially decoded. Credits Pyrdacor format documentation and related playback work; requires user-supplied data. The project consumes data containers rather than original executable code, so an original/source CPU does not apply.

amberstar-amber-framework.title: Amber — early Amberstar reimplementation and data framework
amberstar-amber-framework.display_title: Amber — early Amberstar reimplementation and data framework
amberstar-amber-framework.status: Early-development Amber framework and Amberstar prototype; no complete-game or playable claim.
amberstar-amber-framework.notes: One repository-root record covers the shared Amber libraries and in-progress Amberstar implementation. Original Atari ST, Amiga and DOS data loaders are named by the README. Amberstar.Game/Game.cs contains direct game state, screen/event/time/render logic; Amberstar.net.csproj targets .NET 9 with AOT publishing. Android is an intended framework platform and has configurations; functioning exports were not verified. This is distinct from the already catalogued Ambermoon.net and Ambermoon research repositories. Reviewed 2026-10-05. Build/run/play statements are upstream reports; no candidate code was compiled or executed in this review. Evidence: https://github.com/Pyrdacor/Amber/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/Pyrdacor/Amber/blob/main/Amberstar.Game/Game.cs https://github.com/Pyrdacor/Amber/blob/main/Amberstar.net/Amberstar.net.csproj

ambermoon.title: Ambermoon
ambermoon.notes: Binary and data-format research feeding the broader Ambermoon reconstruction ecosystem.

ambermoon-advanced.title: Ambermoon Advanced

runtime_profiles.name: Amiga build
runtime_profiles.notes: The source explicitly detects 68020+ processors while retaining a 68000 fallback; no minimum RAM or chipset was stated in the reviewed source.

ambermoon-advanced.notes: Unofficial Ambermoon extension. Track only changes that exercise or expose reverse-engineered knowledge of the original engine/formats. AM2_CPU.s explicitly distinguishes 68020+ execution from its 68000 fallback, establishing the native output floor without implying a RAM or chipset minimum.

ambermoon-re-tooling.title: Ambermoon reverse-engineering tooling
ambermoon-re-tooling.notes: Tools and documented methodology used to reverse engineer Ambermoon internals; feeds Ambermoon.net research.

ambermoon-net.title: Ambermoon.net
ambermoon-net.notes: Modern reimplementation substantially informed by reverse engineering of original Ambermoon behaviour and data. The publish profiles explicitly name win-x86, win-x64, linux-x64, linux-arm64, osx-x64 and osx-arm64 outputs; no minimum host CPU or RAM was found in the reviewed project files.

ambermoon-sourceror.title: AmbermoonSourceror
ambermoon-sourceror.notes: Work-in-progress CLI tool that converts Ghidra ASCII exports of Ambermoon AM2_CPU/AM2_BLIT into Amiga assembler. Its compile script explicitly invokes vasmm68k_mot with -m68000 and emits a HUNK executable; upstream documents no successful or byte-identical rebuild, and does not separately state the CPU of the analysed original input.

amberstar.title: Amberstar
amberstar.notes: Research and format decoding across the Amiga, Atari ST and DOS versions.

amberworld-research.title: Amberworld
amberworld-research.display_title: Amberworld — Amber trilogy format & code reverse engineering
amberworld-research.notes: Oliver Gantert's long-running Amberworld project. Its site documents extraction/conversion tools and source releases for Amberstar, Ambermoon and Albion, extensive reverse-engineered file formats, and a later return to disassembled game-code analysis. The homepage, both format pages and SourceForge file index do not identify the exact CPU architecture of that disassembled code.

amiberry-mcp-server.title: Amiberry MCP Server
amiberry-mcp-server.display_title: Amiberry MCP Server — emulator control and debugging
amiberry-mcp-server.notes: Python MCP integration for the Amiberry emulator, including machine control, live memory access, save states, ROM identification and screenshots. Runtime controls require Amiberry built with USE_IPC_SOCKET=ON; its README limits the server to macOS and Linux.

amibinkd-native-mailer.title: AmiBinkD — native AmigaOS binkd mailer
amibinkd-native-mailer.status: Maintainer-reported production inbound/outbound FTN mailer; current README recommends v10.35.
amibinkd-native-mailer.notes: Native binkd mailer port. Makefile targets m68k-amigaos-gcc with nix13 and -msoft-float; source uses bsdsocket.library directly and includes Amiga DOS/process glue. README reports inbound/outbound production use. Not ixemul-based and not CPU emulation. Runtime stability and production test claims were not independently repeated; older-version warnings and concurrency prose may differ from stale Makefile comments. No minimum 68k CPU asserted. README explicitly says it cross-compiles and links cleanly and documents successful production inbound/outbound sessions and soak tests. True flags reflect upstream reports, not local tests. No independent compilation, execution or benchmarking was performed during this catalogue review. Evidence: https://github.com/SpitfireTN/AmiBinkD/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/SpitfireTN/AmiBinkD/blob/main/Makefile https://github.com/SpitfireTN/AmiBinkD/blob/main/amiga_glue.c https://github.com/SpitfireTN/AmiBinkD/blob/main/branch.c https://github.com/SpitfireTN/AmiBinkD/commit/a015b071f88ea598f74aa9cd385cf82acbedee5e

amiblitz3-amiga-basic-compiler.title: AmiBlitz3
amiblitz3-amiga-basic-compiler.display_title: AmiBlitz3 — native Amiga BASIC compiler and IDE
types: native Amiga BASIC compiler and IDE
amiblitz3-amiga-basic-compiler.notes: Complete AmiBlitz3 distribution with compiler/IDE, libraries, includes and examples. README explicitly specifies a 68020 CPU, 8 MB RAM and Workbench 2.1 as IDE requirements, noting compiled output has different requirements. Period-platform development tooling, not a reconstructed game.

jotd-amidar-amiga.title: Amidar — Amiga arcade port

runtime_profiles.name: Amiga 500
runtime_profiles.notes: README requires 1 MB and states 50 fps even on a 68000 A500.
