jotd-amidar-amiga.notes: 1:1 Amiga 500 port in 68k assembly preserving original visuals, sounds, intro and 50 fps target.

amidisk-classic-amiga-preservation.title: AmiDisk — classic Amiga disk preservation
amidisk-classic-amiga-preservation.notes: Native AmigaOS 2.04+ disk imaging and copying project with trackdisk.device and ADF baseline. README distinguishes planned recovery, bootblock and filesystem features from current M0 baseline.

amiforensics-amiga-toolkit.title: AmiForensics — Amiga analysis toolkit
amiforensics-amiga-toolkit.notes: Fifteen native Amiga commands plus optional workstation workflows for HUNK, bootblock, resident, memory, disk and patch inspection. README documents a -m68000 AmigaOS 2.04+ intended baseline and `make check`; AROS/FS-UAE and host-side qualification are distinct from real Commodore AmigaOS qualification, which remains unclaimed.

amifuse-filesystem-emulation.title: AmiFUSE
amifuse-filesystem-emulation.notes: Mounts Amiga HDF/RDB and ADF images by executing native filesystem handler binaries through m68k emulation, including PFS3. ADF use requires an external driver. Documented as an alternative to reimplementing each filesystem format; not a reconstructed filesystem driver.

kickstart-11-a1000-disassembly.title: Amiga 1000 Kickstart 1.1 v31.34 disassembly
kickstart-11-a1000-disassembly.notes: PAL Amiga 1000 Kickstart 1.1 v31.34 disassembly used to reconstruct ROM relocation tables for a Seven Cities of Gold WHDLoad install.

amiga-asm-development-workflow-neildavis.title: Amiga ASM Development Workflow
amiga-asm-development-workflow-neildavis.display_title: Amiga ASM Workflow — reproducible assembly and asset pipeline
amiga-asm-development-workflow-neildavis.notes: Linux automation pipeline for Amiga assembly projects: GIMP/PNG/IFF conversion, ZX0 packing, copper palette/icon generation, assembly/linking and bootable ADF construction. Includes a credited demonstration derived from Bare-Metal Amiga Programming and Salvador decompression; catalogue scope is the integrated development tooling, not a new disassembly.

assembly-library-amiga-gfazioli.title: Amiga Assembly Library
assembly-library-amiga-gfazioli.display_title: Amiga Assembly Library — original source and C bindings

runtime_profiles.name: assembly.library
runtime_profiles.notes: Requirements are explicitly documented for the library, not evidence that the archived source rebuilds unaided.

assembly-library-amiga-gfazioli.notes: Preserves assembly.library source with dated 1990–1995 history, resident/function-table code, Exec/DOS/graphics/UI routines, C headers/bindings and examples. Modern Next.js documentation provides API explanations. The actual lib.asm version string is 41.22 while README badge says 41.21. Some private include dependencies are not established, so compilability is unknown. Claude Code guidance applies to the modern documentation, not historical source provenance.

amiga-basic-decompiler-djnice.title: Amiga BASIC Decompiler
amiga-basic-decompiler-djnice.notes: Standalone Python 3 decompiler for AmigaBASIC binary files. README documents extended token pairs, numeric constants, name-table resolution and Latin-2 text output; these breadth claims come from the project and are not independently validated. Distinct from seawolf’s earlier Go converter.

vscode-amiga-debug-bartmanabyss.title: Amiga C/C++ Compile, Debug & Profile
vscode-amiga-debug-bartmanabyss.display_title: VS Code Amiga C/C++ debugger & profiler
vscode-amiga-debug-bartmanabyss.notes: Self-contained VS Code Amiga C/C++/assembly toolchain with bundled cross-GCC/GDB and WinUAE/FS-UAE integration. Provides source/assembly debugging, memory/watchpoints, frame and DMA profiling, graphics/blitter/Copper inspection, executable-size profiling and source-correlated disassembly.

citadel-amiga-original-source.title: Amiga Citadel 1.0

runtime_profiles.name: Original Citadel runtime
runtime_profiles.notes: README requires at least 0.5MB Chip plus 0.5MB other memory (preferably Fast). CPU minimum is not explicitly given. Separate development-machine requirement is 1MB Chip plus 4MB Fast and is not a game runtime requirement.

citadel-amiga-original-source.notes: Original Virtual Design Citadel 1.0 source and data, plus its editor. The main game engine has documented AsmOne assembly/run instructions; some intro animations and ancillary data are absent. The Remonstered engine is explicitly not included. Minimum runtime memory is distinct from the larger development-machine requirement. Source comments date original development to 1994–1995; re_started remains null because this is original code.

amiga-devbench-mcp.title: Amiga DevBench
amiga-devbench-mcp.display_title: Amiga DevBench — serial debugger and MCP development environment
amiga-devbench-mcp.notes: Host/target bridge over serial to a real or FS-UAE Amiga, with memory/register inspection, breakpoints, remote execution, a web dashboard and MCP tools. The optional patched FS-UAE enables a separate emulator-level debugger; ordinary FS-UAE still supports the serial bridge. Docker is used for the 68k cross compiler.

amiga-file-forge-workbench.title: Amiga File Forge
amiga-file-forge-workbench.display_title: Amiga File Forge — disk, ROM and Hunk analysis workbench
amiga-file-forge-workbench.notes: Web and Linux workbench for Amiga floppy, hard-drive, archive and ROM images. Current release documents RDB partition work, Amiga filesystems, resident modules, Hunk analysis, annotated 68k disassembly and exact-hash guarded patches. It is host-side tooling, not software running on an Amiga; some historical-media and emulator-dependent tasks require user-supplied inputs.

amigaghidra-scripts-caddy666.title: Amiga Ghidra annotation scripts
amigaghidra-scripts-caddy666.notes: Collection of 15 Ghidra scripts for Amiga exception vectors, library calls, resident structures, compiler clues and OCS/ECS/AGA plus Akiko/Gayle register maps. README merely calls them experiments; no tested compatibility or installation procedure is asserted.

discovery-amiga-gngeo.title: Amiga GnGeo
discovery-amiga-gngeo.notes: Neo Geo emulator port for classic Amiga. Makefile targets m68030 and selects Generator68K/MAME Z80 cores; source includes debugger and disassembler components.

amiga-imploder-decompiled-lab313ru.title: Amiga Imploder — decompiled compressor
amiga-imploder-decompiled-lab313ru.notes: Dr. MefistO describes the Imploder compression algorithm as decompiled and fully restored; the repository contains portable C implode/explode routines and a Windows DLL/Lazarus GUI release. The exact CPU of the legacy implementation is not stated, and the host-side restoration does not constitute a native target-CPU port. Hitchhikr credits these routines as the basis for the separately tracked imploder packer.

amiga-lzx-rust.title: Amiga LZX — Rust reconstruction
amiga-lzx-rust.notes: Author describes LLM-assisted reconstruction: original compressor decompiled with Ghidra, a specification written, then Rust implementation built from the spec, with unlzx.c informing decompressor documentation. CLI/library create, list, extract and test Amiga LZX archives; runs on modern hosts.

amigapython-source-revival.title: Amiga Python — Python 2.0 preservation and revival
amigapython-source-revival.display_title: Amiga Python — Python 2.0 preservation and revival

runtime_profiles.name: Historical AmigaPython 2.0 distribution
runtime_profiles.notes: Historical release requires a 68030 and FPU, hard disk, and 4 MB (possibly more). Optional networking needs AmiTCP; user authorization needs usergroup.library. Does not describe the proposed Python 2.7.18 revival.

types: historical source preservation / native language port
amigapython-source-revival.status: Historical Python 2.0 sources and releases preserved; updating to Python 2.7.18 is a stated goal.
amigapython-source-revival.notes: Repository contains original Amiga Python sources, archives and an Amiga SMAKEFILE producing Python20. SCOPTIONS explicitly sets CPU=68030 and MATH=68881. README identifies Irmen de Jong's 1999-2000 port. Do not describe Python 2.7.18 as completed: it is the revival's goal. The observed build is the historical Python 2.0/68030+FPU configuration; no successful modern build was independently established. SMAKEFILE/SCOPTIONS preserve a Python20 build configuration, while README.AMIGA still describes Python16 and requires external distribution files. No successful present-tree rebuild or runnable 2.7.18 release established; flags remain unknown. No independent compilation, execution or benchmarking was performed during this catalogue review. Evidence: https://github.com/amigazen/AmigaPython/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/amigazen/AmigaPython/blob/main/Source/SMAKEFILE https://github.com/amigazen/AmigaPython/blob/main/Source/SCOPTIONS https://github.com/amigazen/AmigaPython/blob/main/Source/README.AMIGA https://github.com/amigazen/AmigaPython/commit/4eec5bc91db41e9a4dae3b1a2f37e341a945024d

amiga-sources-moon70.title: Amiga Sources
amiga-sources-moon70.display_title: Amiga Sources — Abyss demo source archive
amiga-sources-moon70.notes: Author-released ASM-One sources for multiple historical Abyss Amiga demos and music discs; some contributions are partial, so the collection is not represented as full source for every production.

amiga-re-rust-toolkit.title: amiga-re — Rust reversing toolkit
amiga-re-rust-toolkit.notes: Rust CLI and libraries for ADF file recovery, HUNK parsing, 68000 disassembly, bootcode tracing, IFF/ILBM/8SVX decoding and bounded emulated calls/frame capture. README advertises structured output for AI-assisted workflows; this alone does not establish that AI wrote or analysed the project.

va2000-amiga-picasso96-driver.title: amiga2000-gfxcard
va2000-amiga-picasso96-driver.notes: The hardware repository includes the reverse-engineered Picasso96 Amiga RTG driver under drivers/gfx. Its primary build script explicitly invokes m68k-amigaos-gcc with -m68020 and produces mntgfx.card; the README records Workbench running through the driver, but states no RAM floor.

amiga68ktools-jotd.title: amiga68ktools
amiga68ktools-jotd.notes: Host-side Python/Rust utilities for Amiga object analysis and WHDLoad patching. The primary readme documents IRA-assisted resourcing, relocation and patch-list analysis, memory-dump scanning and 68k CPU-dependent-code detection; the tools do not emit one fixed native target executable.

amiga-hunk-parser-rust-emoon.title: amiga_hunk_parser — Rust HUNK parser
amiga-hunk-parser-rust-emoon.notes: Separate Rust crate by the same author for parsing generic Amiga HUNK executables. Cargo.toml and source are present, but the short README asserts no completeness or fidelity result; a Rust toolchain was unavailable in this audit environment, so build success remains an explicit research gap.

amigaasm-ghidra-exporter.title: AmigaAsm
amigaasm-ghidra-exporter.notes: Amiga m68k assembly exporter for Ghidra; repository README is terse, so successful rebuilds and ROM fidelity are unverified.

amigabasic-binary-parser-seawolf.title: AmigaBASIC Binary-to-ASCII Converter
amigabasic-binary-parser-seawolf.notes: Go converter reads tokenized AmigaBASIC files, replaces known keyword codes, resolves names/labels from the file trailer and writes a text program. README and Go tests establish a working parser, without a claim of complete keyword or numeric coverage.

ida-amiga-debugger-lab313ru.title: amigadbg — IDA/Amitools Amiga debugger
ida-amiga-debugger-lab313ru.notes: Windows IDA Pro 6.8/6.95 debugger plugin for AmigaOS through Amitools. Primary source requires IDA's m68k processor module (`PLFM_68K` / `m68k`) and exposes 68k registers; the Visual Studio project defines 32- and 64-bit Windows plugin configurations. This is a distinct live-debugging integration, not the author's IDA or Ghidra Hunk loader.

amigadx-total-commander-disk-plugin.title: amigadx
amigadx-total-commander-disk-plugin.display_title: amigadx — Total Commander Amiga disk plugin
source_language: ADF, ADZ, DMS and HDF disk images
amigadx-total-commander-disk-plugin.notes: Total Commander plugin described as read/write for ADF and HDF and read-only for ADZ and DMS. The README names MinGW64 build and untested Premake Visual Studio generation; no independent compatibility verification or original filesystem authorship claim.

amigaffh-formats.title: AmigaFFH — Amiga file formats
amigaffh-formats.notes: R package for reading Amiga native formats, including IFF images and tokenized AmigaBASIC programs. Repository is a CRAN mirror of pepijn-devries/AmigaFFH; install snippet in README unexpectedly names ProTrackR, so package installation was not verified here.

amiga-hunk-parser-c-emoon.title: AmigaHunkParser — C HUNK parser
amiga-hunk-parser-c-emoon.notes: C library and command-line test program for generic Amiga HUNK executables. The supplied Makefile built cleanly with GCC during this audit and the resulting ahp program displayed its expected input-file usage; this establishes a host parser, not a CPU claim for every HUNK input or a fidelity comparison against historical tools.

php-amiga-iff-ilbm-converter.title: AmigaIFFConverter — ILBM writer
php-amiga-iff-ilbm-converter.notes: PHP JPEG/PNG to ILBM writer with HAM6 and ECS modes and optional ByteRun1 compression. README reports opening generated HAM6 output in DeluxePaint IV. Source-derived asset pipeline, not recovered historical code.

amigainfo-icon-tool.title: amigainfo
amigainfo-icon-tool.display_title: amigainfo — Amiga .info icon parser and converter
amigainfo-icon-tool.notes: Python library and CLI reads, modifies and writes classic, NewIcons, GlowIcons, ARGB and PowerIcons files; exposes tooltypes and icon metadata for preservation/inspection.

amigaos-kickstart-rcs-history-restoratio.title: AmigaOS Kickstart — RCS source-history restoration
amigaos-kickstart-rcs-history-restoratio.notes: Rebuilds a Git timeline from surviving original AmigaOS 3 RCS source revisions. Tags represent approximate inferred states from pre-1.0 through 3.1; early source trees are especially incomplete and ordering can be uncertain. This is archival source-history reconstruction, not source recovered from ROM binaries; no reproducible build is claimed.

amiga-quarterback-extractor.title: AmigaQB_extract
amiga-quarterback-extractor.notes: Recovers Central Coast Software Quarterback backups from ADF images, including damaged or catalogless sets. README documents v4.x through v6.x, compressed markers, catalog layout and format research checked against original GPL Quarterback source. Host-side recovery tool, not an Amiga executable.

amiga-rom-explorer-ginnov.title: AmigaROMExplorer
amiga-rom-explorer-ginnov.display_title: AmigaROMExplorer — Amiga ROM catalog and local scanner
source_language: Amiga Kickstart and firmware ROM files
amiga-rom-explorer-ginnov.notes: macOS ROM atlas with local ROM scanner, checksum index and manifest parser. The inspected OllamaClient.swift offers optional LLM-based ROM research; it does not replace the deterministic local matching path. Firmware-identification scope and actual accuracy need independent samples.

amigo-ios-amiga-emulator.title: Amigo
amigo-ios-amiga-emulator.display_title: Amigo — Amiga emulator for iPhone, iPad and Apple Silicon
amigo-ios-amiga-emulator.notes: Native Apple-platform WinUAE adaptation with SwiftUI interface, ROM/disk import and configurations spanning classic Amigas. README reports App Store release 0.7.7 and documents arm64 iOS cross-builds. CPU interpretation is a reusable whole-Amiga emulator, so it qualifies as generic tooling. No independent install/runtime test.

amimcp-amiga-automation.title: amimcp

runtime_profiles.name: Baseline agent
runtime_profiles.notes: README describes the baseline amiagent as approximately 85 KB and able to run on a bare 68000; that binary-size figure is not a RAM minimum.

evidence.excerpt: amiagent — a small C daemon on the Amiga. AmigaOS 2.04 and up, bare 68000, ~85 KB, needs nothing but bsdsocket.library.

runtime_profiles.name: 68020+ agent
runtime_profiles.notes: README documents a separately built 68020+ agent; no separate RAM minimum is stated.

evidence.excerpt: cd agent && make CPU=68020      # 68020+ build

runtime_profiles.name: Apollo 68080 agent
runtime_profiles.notes: Speed-optimized Apollo 68080 build; upstream notes that bebbo's amiga-gcc supports the required -m68080 option. No RAM minimum is stated.

evidence.excerpt: cd agent && make CPU=68080      # Apollo 68080, speed-optimised

amimcp-amiga-automation.notes: Original Python MCP server plus AmigaOS C agent for remote shell, files, screenshots, ARexx and GUI interaction. The agent has explicit 68000 baseline, 68020+ and Apollo 68080 builds; the baseline requires AmigaOS 2.04+ and bsdsocket.library. This is original development tooling, not a reconstruction of historical executable code.

amiport-native-porting-toolkit.title: amiport
amiport-native-porting-toolkit.display_title: amiport — AmigaOS native porting and test toolkit
amiport-native-porting-toolkit.notes: Coherent POSIX-to-AmigaOS porting project combining compatibility libraries, cross-compilers, package management and automated vamos/FS-UAE tests. README describes shipped native utility ports and an explicit Claude Code agent pipeline. Root retained rather than splitting the catalogue into dozens of tiny utilities; stated test counts are upstream claims.

amiquake-c2p-reconstruction.title: AmiQuake GCC Port
amiquake-c2p-reconstruction.display_title: AmiQuake — Quake port with recovered C2P routine

runtime_profiles.name: GCC port
runtime_profiles.notes: 68040 or 68060 with FPU; no minimum RAM established.

evidence.excerpt: Amiga with 68040/68060 CPU + FPU

amiquake-c2p-reconstruction.notes: GCC port of AmiQuake based on awinquake 0.9. An 842-byte NovaCoder chunky-to-planar routine was extracted from AmiQuake 1.36 and rewritten as readable 68k assembly; the author reports working console, palette and viewport tests. AI assistance is asserted without naming a model/tool.

amitcp-ng-roadshow-abi.title: AmiTCP_NG
amitcp-ng-roadshow-abi.notes: GPL AmiTCP/IP 3.0b2 fork with separately implemented Roadshow-compatible bsdsocket.library extensions based on the published SDK ABI. Explicitly does not contain or disassemble Roadshow code.

amitools-amiga-toolkit.title: amitools
amitools-amiga-toolkit.display_title: amitools — Amiga binary, ROM & filesystem toolkit
amitools-amiga-toolkit.notes: Host-side toolkit for classic 68k AmigaOS binaries and storage formats. Includes hunktool/Hunk libraries for inspecting and relocating Amiga binaries and object files, romtool for dissecting/building Kickstart ROMs, ADF/HDF/RDB/OFS/FFS tooling, and vamos, an API-level AmigaOS emulator with library-call, structure and memory tracing useful for analysing old executables and running historical development tools.

amostools-kyz.title: amostools
amostools-kyz.notes: Portable host tools for AMOS programs: dumpamos extracts source and memory banks, listamos renders source as text, and unlockamos unlocks procedures. The primary Makefile builds all three with GCC; the README documents command-line use and extension-token requirements, but no host CPU/RAM floor.

ample-mame-apple-frontend.title: Ample
ample-mame-apple-frontend.notes: MAME front end with a custom Apple II/Macintosh-focused MAME build and Uthernet II support; a system emulator rather than a disassembly.

cpc-basic-1-1.title: Amstrad CPC BASIC 1.1
cpc-basic-1-1.notes: Completed 'unassembly' into relocatable/modifiable source; generated ROM output is compared with the original and intended to be identical.

cpc464-rom-disassembly.title: Amstrad CPC464 Firmware ROM
cpc464-rom-disassembly.notes: Richard Lloyd's CPC464 operating-system ROM disassembly, generated with Disark then hand-finished and labelled for reassembly with MAXAM.

cpc6128-firmware-source.title: Amstrad CPC6128 Firmware
cpc6128-firmware-source.notes: Bread80's relocatable/modifiable firmware unassembly; assembled output is checked against and intended to exactly match the original ROM.

amstrad-diagnostics-llopis.title: Amstrad Diagnostics
amstrad-diagnostics-llopis.display_title: Amstrad Diagnostics — native CPC/Plus diagnostic suite
amstrad-diagnostics-llopis.notes: Author-maintained native diagnostic suite tests RAM, ROM, keyboard and CRTC behavior, with substantial hardware routines and distinct ROM, RAM, cartridge, disk and tape build variants. Companion ROM dump code supports retro system investigation. Source and multi-format packaging script inspected; no independent build or diagnostic execution performed.

zxmicrojack-amstrad-cpc-fpga.title: AmstradCPC6128 — ZX-Uno/ZX-Tres FPGA core
zxmicrojack-amstrad-cpc-fpga.notes: Whole-repository CPC6128 FPGA core derived from Miguel Angel Rodriguez Jodar's CPC464 core, extended by Microjack with 128 KB and SD-backed disk emulation. README records known-good ZX-Uno r4 and ZX-Tres r5, supports two drives and standard/extended CPC disk images with 512-byte-sector limitations, and lists compatibility failures. Build depends on ZXMicroJack/ctrl-module's amstradcpc branch; no independent nested project is split out.

amstrad-cpc-rom-hacks-tools.title: AmstradCPCRomHacks
amstrad-cpc-rom-hacks-tools.display_title: Amstrad CPC ROM Hacks — ROM analysis and patch scripts
source_language: CPC firmware and accessory ROM images
amstrad-cpc-rom-hacks-tools.notes: Python tools list visible/hidden ROM commands, dump strings with optional XOR decoding and patch Graduate CP/M accessory ROM personal data; analysis is tied to real CPC ROM structures.

amy-studio-colecovision-development-envi.title: Amy Studio
amy-studio-colecovision-development-envi.display_title: Amy Studio — browser-based ColecoVision development environment
amy-studio-colecovision-development-envi.notes: Runnable browser development environment with the Amy compiler/transpiler/optimizer, a gasm80-compatible Z80 assembler, compression codecs, examples and a self-hosted GearColeco debugger. Current commits add native Coleco ADAM EOS filesystem/project, serial-presence and debugger-keyboard support. It is substantial original development tooling, not a reverse-engineered subject.

ana-amiga-framework.title: ANA (ANA's Now on Amiga)
ana-amiga-framework.display_title: ANA — Amiga C game framework and development tools
ana-amiga-framework.notes: Original C framework for classic Amiga with fixed-step loop, planar image/font rendering, input, Paula SFX/MOD playback, sprite/BOB helpers, tilemap experiments, converted assets and example games. An accompanying VS Code extension checks toolchains, builds, launches emulators and creates SDK-backed projects. Stock A1200 is the documented practical showcase target; the final native fine-scroll backend is still planned.

ancient-legacy-decompressor.title: Ancient
ancient-legacy-decompressor.notes: Modern C++ decompressor/library for a broad collection of legacy compression formats used heavily on Amiga, Atari and other 1980s/1990s systems. It cleanly reimplements many historically awkward or undocumented algorithms, including PowerPacker, XPK backends, CrunchMania, StoneCracker, RNC, DMS, ByteKiller and numerous clones, and tests implementations against a large corpus of legacy files.

ancipital-c64.title: Ancipital
ancipital-c64.notes: Reverse-engineered commented source; README explicitly states the game compiles and plays.

anfs-zornslemma-418-disassembly.title: ANFS 4.18 bare disassembly
anfs-zornslemma-418-disassembly.notes: ZornsLemma ANFS 4.18 assembly listings and a compare-oriented build script; inspected listing is largely automatic labels and missing local ROM inputs prevent verification. Separate earlier effort on the same ROM later covered more comprehensively by acornaeology/acorn-nfs.

another-world-js-dos.title: Another World JS
source_language: Another World DOS demo/anniversary game data
another-world-js-dos.notes: Browser port interprets the game’s 26 bytecode opcodes and converts DOS demo/anniversary assets. Its Amiga palette option does not imply Amiga disk-data support. This is a distinct browser implementation alongside the tracked raw(gl) engine.

another-world-vm-tools.title: Another World VM Tools
another-world-vm-tools.notes: Pure-Rust Another World VM resource unpacker, bytecode disassembler and assembler across several releases including the Amiga, with OFS ADF extraction and byte-identical bytecode round-trip documented. Byte-identical VM bytecode round-trip does not imply an Amiga executable rebuild.

another-world-cross-port-archaeology.title: Another World — cross-port archaeology
source_language: original release executables and game data
another-world-cross-port-archaeology.notes: Active comparative archaeology of Another World releases, with checksum provenance, extractors and bytecode disassemblies. Includes the original Amiga lineage. Original game fixtures are expected from a separate sibling archive; do not infer that every release has been completely decoded. The CPU fields are intentionally not applicable: the cross-port comparison currently disassembles the game's virtual-machine bytecode and produces research artifacts, rather than reconstructing a native host instruction set.

another-world-cross-port-reconstruction.title: Another World — cross-port source reconstruction
another-world-cross-port-reconstruction.notes: Active work toward one conditional source tree for multiple release lineages, including Chahi's 1991 Amiga bytecode. README and PLAN document byte-identical round trips for 29 levels across five ports. Current outputs are Another World VM bytecode resources: engine binary reconstruction and whole-port packaging are explicitly outside the present scope, so native source and target CPUs are not applicable. Depends on sibling archaeology and external VMTools.

appengine-riscos-desktop-library-dpt.title: AppEngine
appengine-riscos-desktop-library-dpt.display_title: AppEngine — RISC OS desktop C library
source_language: RISC OS desktop and graphics APIs
appengine-riscos-desktop-library-dpt.notes: Reusable RISC OS desktop application C library under libs/appengine in the PrivateEye repository. README distinguishes AppEngine from the PrivateEye image viewer and TagCloud demo; source directories include Wimp, VDU, dialogues, gadgets, graphics, I/O and networking, with CMake build integration. The viewer is an application consumer, not a reconstructed target.

apple-ii-system-software-cmosher.title: Apple ][ System Software Source Code
apple-ii-system-software-cmosher.display_title: Apple II system software and DOS — reverse-engineered source
apple-ii-system-software-cmosher.notes: Christopher Mosher describes this package as reverse-engineered source code for Apple II series system ROMs and DOS. Exact build equivalence, supported ROM variants, and runnable hardware minimums still need review.

apple-ii-desktop-a2stuff.title: Apple II DeskTop
apple-ii-desktop-a2stuff.display_title: Apple II DeskTop — disassembly and enhanced ProDOS GUI

runtime_profiles.name: Apple II DeskTop on 8-bit Apples
runtime_profiles.notes: README lists 8-bit Apple II models and clones with 128 KiB; mouse is optional.

evidence.excerpt: 8-bit Apples and clones with 128k of memory

apple-ii-desktop-a2stuff.notes: The project disassembles and extends Mouse Desk / Apple II DeskTop, a ProDOS 8 GUI. Its README identifies 128 KiB 8-bit Apple systems and clones and links build/running instructions and disk images. No narrower CPU or chipset minimum is asserted.

apple2-plus-rom-james-davis.title: Apple II Plus ROM
apple2-plus-rom-james-davis.display_title: Apple II Plus ROM — full-system annotated disassembly
apple2-plus-rom-james-davis.notes: James P. Davis independently annotated the Apple II Plus emulator ROM image across $C000–$FFFF, identifying errors in the image and extensively editing/integrating earlier Apple, Sander-Cederlof, McFadden and other reference material. The listing explicitly credits those predecessors; it is not presented as original Apple source. SourceGen project file is linked from the ROM index.

apple-lisa-mister-fpga-core.title: Apple-Lisa_MiSTer

runtime_profiles.name: Lisa Office System on MiSTer
runtime_profiles.notes: Office System requires at least 1 MB of configured Lisa RAM; 512 KB is only useful for ROM diagnostics.

apple-lisa-mister-fpga-core.notes: Hardware-accurate Lisa 1/2/5 core ported from LisaFPGA to MiSTer. It models the 68000, 6504 and COP421 subsystems, boots Lisa Office System, and supports ProFile and writable Sony 400K images; blank-floppy initialization remains incomplete.

applem-apple-ii-emulator-debugger.title: ApplEm
applem-apple-ii-emulator-debugger.display_title: ApplEm — Apple II/IIgs emulator and debugger
applem-apple-ii-emulator-debugger.notes: Browser/desktop Apple II family emulator modelling II Plus, enhanced IIe, IIc and IIgs. Primary documentation describes a built-in CPU debugger, memory heat map, disk explorer with BASIC detokenizer/disassembler, a 65C816 checked against 5.1 million recorded real-silicon states, and programmatic MCP/AG-UI control. AI-agent integration is a feature, not evidence that project development used AI.

applevision-apple2-6502disassembly.title: AppleVision
applevision-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Disassembly of Bob Bishop's AppleVision demo, split into its Integer BASIC and embedded machine-language components, with commented listings and SourceGen project files/binaries.

apurify-amiga-memory-debugger.title: APurify — original Amiga memory-access instrumentation tool
apurify-amiga-memory-debugger.display_title: APurify — original Amiga memory-access instrumentation tool
apurify-amiga-memory-debugger.status: Original author source archive of a historical no-MMU memory debugger; fresh build/run unverified.
apurify-amiga-memory-debugger.notes: Original author's source for a historical memory debugger: assembly parsers, instrumentation runtime and front end, with compiler-specific makefiles. It can process compiler-generated or reverse-engineered assembly. Historical toolchain and source syntax; no modern build/run attempted. README repeats archive-era text saying source was not in the binary distribution, while this GitHub root demonstrably contains source. README preserves historical v1.5/v1.6 distribution/install instructions and June 1999 provenance; source and compiler-specific makefiles are present. Neither a successful current-tree rebuild nor a verified current runnable artifact is established, so all build/run/play flags remain unknown. The stale archive text saying source was absent does not negate the source now published at this root. Original author source archive; no known catalogue duplicate. No independent compilation, installation, execution, playtest or original-program binary comparison was performed in this catalogue review. Evidence: https://github.com/Samuel-DEVULDER/APurify/blob/master/README.md https://github.com/Samuel-DEVULDER/APurify/blob/master/mit-parser/main.c https://github.com/Samuel-DEVULDER/APurify/blob/master/Makefile.gcc https://github.com/Samuel-DEVULDER/APurify/commit/1aefc21e3c464e9d5add65cfe65a7cb4c8d677df

archie-face-c-framework.title: Archie-FACE — Archimedes C demo environment
archie-face-c-framework.notes: C Archimedes demo framework with SWI/video handling, bank swapping, input/debug helpers and fluid simulation modules inspected in main.c. Coherent reusable source and demo harness at repository root; no minimum supported machine independently exercised.

archie-verse-arm-framework.title: Archie-Verse — ARM demo framework
archie-verse-arm-framework.notes: ARM assembly Archimedes trackmo framework with configured demo parts, video/music, frame timing, debugging and script modules; README states ARM2/ARM250 targets. Independent reusable framework; do not split its demo parts into separate project records.

archieklang-archimedes-synth.title: ArchieKlang — Archimedes synth port
archieklang-archimedes-synth.notes: ARM assembly sound synthesizer port of AmigaKlang, with imported reference material, sample generation, QTM test harness and build scripts. Credits AmigaKlang as predecessor; this is an Archimedes music subsystem port, not an original Amiga source reconstruction.

archiludo-acorn-native.title: ArchiLudo — native Acorn Archimedes Ludo port
archiludo-acorn-native.display_title: ArchiLudo — native Acorn Archimedes Ludo port

runtime_profiles.name: Native 26-bit RISC OS game
runtime_profiles.notes: README explicitly requires ARM2 or ARM3 and RISC OS 3.10+. No RAM minimum is stated. The author’s ARM3/4 MB A305 is a test configuration, not a minimum. Upstream claim only; not run locally.

types: Native homebrew game port and rules reimplementation
archiludo-acorn-native.status: Native RISC OS Ludo port; upstream reports released gameplay on real ARM3 hardware and Arculator, with ARM2/RISC OS 3.10+ requirements.
archiludo-acorn-native.notes: Real C rules engine and RISC OS WIMP application implement Ludo moves, capture, finish order, variants and configurable opponents. Makefile integrates ArchieSDK/OSLib, host tests and RISC OS application packaging. README documents source lineage back to author's 1992 C128 game. The earlier xahmol/ludo family is separately recorded as ludo-xahmol-native-family. CREDITS is more specific than stale README artwork wording. Game-opponent AI is distinct from explicit Claude Code development evidence. Distinct same-author RISC OS implementation descended from xahmol/ludo, separately catalogued as the earlier native Ludo/GeoLudo family in this batch. README states GNU GPLv3. CREDITS preserves author/source/asset attribution; current board geometry directly reuses GeoLudo, while shipped pawn silhouettes are newly generated and dice use drawn pips. Rules/AI are reimplemented rather than literal source copies. Reviewed 2026-10-05 by primary documentation, source, build-file and tree inspection. All local build, test, emulation and runtime checks remain unperformed. Positive flags are evidence-scoped upstream reports only; byte_exact remains unknown. Last activity is the latest default-branch commit date, not repository creation or pushed_at. Evidence: https://github.com/xahmol/ArchiLudo/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/xahmol/ArchiLudo/blob/main/src/game_logic.c https://github.com/xahmol/ArchiLudo/blob/main/docs/GAME_LOGIC.md https://github.com/xahmol/ArchiLudo/blob/main/CREDITS.md https://github.com/xahmol/ArchiLudo/blob/main/Makefile https://github.com/xahmol/ArchiLudo/commit/488f24d243f4f448d2e04ebd0ce6bbe46935d9c0

follin-music-source-archive.title: ARCHIVE-FOLLIN
follin-music-source-archive.display_title: Follin music archive — recovered C64 and CPC/Spectrum source
subjects: Tim and Geoff Follin music and sound drivers
follin-music-source-archive.notes: Recovered Tim and Geoff Follin period music and driver source from Tatung Einstein floppies. Author reverse-engineered a 6502 detokenizer and began modern Z80 assembler builds for AY music examples; this is source recovery, not a game disassembly.

archon-c64-reconstruction.title: Archon — C64 source reconstruction
archon-c64-reconstruction.notes: Reverse-engineered reconstruction of the C64 Archon game logic as extensively commented, relocatable Kick Assembler source. Original addresses are retained as documentation while variables, constants and routines are renamed and reorganised for readability rather than binary identity.

arduino-z80-disassembler-bread80.title: Arduino-Hosted-Z80-Disassembler
arduino-z80-disassembler-bread80.notes: Arduino-ready Z80 single-instruction disassembler handles incomplete opcode streams; the README explicitly excludes a hardware connection, full-program control-flow analysis and label generation.

alternate-reality-dungeon-ardungeon.title: ardungeon
alternate-reality-dungeon-ardungeon.display_title: Alternate Reality: The Dungeon — Atari 8-bit byte-checked disassembly
alternate-reality-dungeon-ardungeon.notes: Atari 8-bit disassembly/reconstruction of Alternate Reality: The Dungeon. The Makefile assembles many sector fragments with ca65/ld65, recreates encrypted companions, concatenates five disk images, and checks individual binaries and final images against stored SHA-1 references.

arkanoid-msx-disassembly-mcolom.title: Arkanoid
arkanoid-msx-disassembly-mcolom.notes: Manually annotated disassembly of Taito's MSX Arkanoid. The source header documents its z80dasm origin, z80asm rebuild command and the SHA-1 expected from the rebuilt ROM.

arkos-player-bbc.title: Arkos Tracker players for BBC Micro
arkos-player-bbc.display_title: Arkos Tracker players for BBC Micro

runtime_profiles.name: Stock BBC Model B replay
runtime_profiles.notes: README says the replays run on a stock Model B with no second processor or sideways RAM; no RAM amount is stated.

arkos-player-bbc.notes: BBC Model B 6502 AKL, AKM and AKY tracker replay code plus AY-3-8912-to-SN76489 conversion and measured verification notes. README states the new AKM player fills a previous Z80-only gap. Credits original Arkos music format and source players. Author explicitly says Claude wrote new code under human direction and review; timing/build claims are upstream.

armalyte-c64-analyser.title: Armalyte
armalyte-c64-analyser.notes: Title-specific C64 binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Armalyte directory contains a large Analysis.json annotation database (~803 KB) plus saved analyser/emulator state and configuration. This is tracked as an analysis-state project, not as a reconstructed source tree.

ase-atari-system-emulator.title: ASE — Atari ST-family system emulator
ase-atari-system-emulator.status: Upstream provides releases and build instructions; Linux support is described as expected but untested.
ase-atari-system-emulator.notes: Primary README describes a C# Atari ST-family emulator using Moira, partly derived from the author's 1990s emulator and Hatari. Substantial machine implementation and .NET project are present. README supplies Moira wrapper build and dotnet publish commands. Generic system emulation, not a game-specific CPU wrapper. Linux support is described as expected but untested by the author; no local build or compatibility validation. README supplies Moira build and dotnet publish instructions, says ready-to-use releases exist, and reports Windows/macOS execution. True flags reflect upstream evidence, not an independent build. Linux remains untested upstream. No independent compilation, execution or benchmarking was performed during this catalogue review. Evidence: https://github.com/thebitculture/ase/blob/main/README.MD https://github.com/thebitculture/ase/blob/main/ASE/ASE.csproj https://github.com/thebitculture/ase/blob/main/ASE/CPU.cs https://github.com/thebitculture/ase/blob/main/ASE/Memory.cs https://github.com/thebitculture/ase/commit/4a60df85090ad3485c5bd6dec73b26ab8664d42a

asteroids-arcade-6502disassembly.title: Asteroids
asteroids-arcade-6502disassembly.notes: SourceGen reconstruction of Asteroids rev 4 based on earlier Computer Archeology/Nick Mikstas analysis, covering the 6502 program and vector-generator command ROM. The project adds a DVG disassembler, project files/binaries and binary-construction instructions.

atari-osb-ntsc-source-restoration.title: Atari 8-bit OS-B NTSC ROM
atari-osb-ntsc-source-restoration.display_title: Atari OS-B NTSC — paper-source restoration and verified ROM build
subjects: Atari 400/800 Operating System Revision B NTSC ROM

runtime_profiles.name: OS-B NTSC ROM
runtime_profiles.notes: The primary README identifies this 10 KiB OS-B NTSC ROM for Atari 400 and 800 machines; no RAM minimum is stated.

atari-osb-ntsc-source-restoration.notes: Restores Atari's published OS-B source listing by scanning, OCR and proofreading, then converts it to ca65 syntax. The Makefile compares the generated listing bytes with the paper-derived path and checks the result against the included 10 KiB ROM.

atari-file-forge-workbench.title: Atari File Forge
atari-file-forge-workbench.display_title: Atari File Forge — ST disk and ROM analysis workbench
source_language: ST floppy, hard-drive, ROM and 68000 binaries
atari-file-forge-workbench.notes: Web and Linux workbench for Atari ST through Falcon floppy, hard-drive, archive and ROM images. Current release documents GEMDOS editing, AHDI/ICD partitions, STX protection reports, flux containers and 68000 analysis. It is host-side tooling, not a native Atari ST application; the Amiga File Forge sibling handles a different platform and formats.

atari-st-rom-listings-sarnau.title: Atari ST BIOS ROM comparative listings
atari-st-rom-listings-sarnau.upstream_name: Atari ST BIOS ROM comparative listings
atari-st-rom-listings-sarnau.display_title: Atari ST BIOS ROM comparative listings
subjects: Atari ST BIOS ROM comparative listings
atari-st-rom-listings-sarnau.notes: Comparative annotated BIOS/XBIOS assembly for TOS 2.06, TOS 3.06 and STBook ROM variants. c64-typein-ocr-reconstruction.notes: Magazine MLX 2 and BASIC listings parsed from OCR and corrected with JS checksum routines; includes resulting source/PRG variants and VICE test notes. A collection of historically published programs, with reusable conversion tooling at root.

jeffsand-c64-ultimate-cli.title: c64 — C64 Ultimate command-line and disk tools
jeffsand-c64-ultimate-cli.display_title: c64 — C64 Ultimate command-line and disk tools
jeffsand-c64-ultimate-cli.notes: Repository-wide C64 Ultimate CLI supports mounting/running PRG/CRT/D64 media, keyboard control, directory inspection, upload, monitoring and D64 creation. src/d64.ts implements 35/40-track D64 parsing and notes it was ported from Ready app's D64Parser.swift. package.json defines the TypeScript build and Node >=20; README discloses help from Claude. AI-agent-ready output is a separate feature from that authorship disclosure.

chronocoders-c64-1541-emulator.title: C64 — cycle-accurate C64/1541 emulator and debugger
chronocoders-c64-1541-emulator.display_title: C64 — cycle-accurate C64/1541 emulator and debugger
chronocoders-c64-1541-emulator.notes: C11 emulator models C64 and 1541 CPU domains, IEC bus, GCR media and peripherals. README documents Make/SDL2 builds and running commercial software; docs/debugging.md describes headless scripted runs, state snapshots and optional bus/PC watchpoints, implemented in src/debug.c. Upstream claims no other emulator code was used and cites hardware documentation and test models. These are upstream accuracy/test claims, not independently reproduced tests.

calint-c64-native-game-experiments.title: c64 — native C64 scrolling game experiments
calint-c64-native-game-experiments.display_title: c64 — native C64 scrolling game experiments
calint-c64-native-game-experiments.notes: Whole-repository native C64 experiments culminating in a scrolling miniature game. Assembly implements VIC-II/CIA/processor-port control, with Python asset generators, Tiled maps and dated PRG snapshots. README states tagged versions have been played through to completion and explains a switch to an unrolled row-based tile renderer; run.sh builds with cl65 and launches VICE x64sc. These are original development experiments, not a binary-derived reconstruction.

c64-re-agent-marcellmajor.title: C64-RE Agent
c64-re-agent-marcellmajor.notes: LangGraph-based research workbench accepts a 64 KB C64 memory dump and question, combines static Capstone disassembly with optional VICE MCP introspection and maintains an evidence-backed knowledge base. Separate from the tracked C64RE/TRX64 projects.

c64-ruby-cross-development-tools.title: c64-ruby — C64 assets, code generation and build tools
c64-ruby-cross-development-tools.display_title: c64-ruby — C64 assets, code generation and build tools
source_language: C64 PRG and VICE snapshot formats
c64-ruby-cross-development-tools.notes: Lars Haugseth's repository combines palette/image processing and concrete build/deployment helpers. Codegen implements opcode bytes, addressing modes and cycle counts, including undocumented NMOS instructions; its simple assembler accepts numeric operands rather than resolving a full symbolic language. Rake orchestration depends on an external shared directory/linker files. Gem metadata requires Ruby >=2.0 and old chunky_png/rubygame versions; README still lists first gem release as TODO. Current installation/running was not verified.

c64gameframework-cadaver.title: c64gameframework
source_language: C64 hardware and game resource formats
c64gameframework-cadaver.notes: Reusable 50 Hz scrolling engine and developer tools, sprite cache/multiplexer, loaders and example disk/cartridge builds; not a reconstruction of Steel Ranger or MW ULTRA.

c64re-mcp-workbench.title: C64RE
c64re-mcp-workbench.display_title: C64RE — MCP-assisted C64 software analysis workbench

runtime_profiles.name: C64RE workbench
runtime_profiles.os: Node.js 22 or newer; TRX64 0.12.3; user-supplied Commodore ROMs
runtime_profiles.notes: No minimum host CPU or RAM is stated.

c64re-mcp-workbench.notes: C64 forensic and semantic-disassembly workbench. The Node.js 22+ application verifies reconstructed assembly with byte diffs and uses TRX64 0.12.3 with user-supplied ROMs. Current checks share private cartridge IDs 87–89 with related tools; C64RE itself is not an emulator.

c64wasm-rust-browser-emulator.title: c64wasm — Rust C64 and 1541 emulator

runtime_profiles.name: Browser WebAssembly emulator
runtime_profiles.notes: README documents the browser/WASM output and locally served ES-module frontend. Copyrighted BASIC, KERNAL, character and 1541 ROMs are required and not bundled; the app can accept user files or rebuild public listings. No browser-version, CPU or RAM minimum is stated.

c64wasm-rust-browser-emulator.status: Author-reported browser emulator; cycle accuracy, ROM reconstruction and compatibility tests not independently rerun.
c64wasm-rust-browser-emulator.notes: Rust C64/1541 emulator with JavaScript/WebAssembly browser frontend, machine/chip modules, ROM-listing rebuild helpers and test tooling. Generic machine emulation and ROM tooling. Compatibility fixtures or named games/demos remain test inputs, not separately reconstructed subjects. README links an author-published live browser demo and describes boot/disk operation, supporting runnable=true as an upstream claim. Cargo/wasm-bindgen commands and CI recipes were inspected, not executed, and no workflow pass was independently checked. Tests needing ROMs can skip when ROMs/listing sites are unavailable. Cycle-exactness and CRC-based ROM repairs are author claims, not this review’s verification; compilable and byte_exact remain null. Generic emulator only: named software used for compatibility does not become reconstructed-game evidence. Cycle-exactness and conformance claims are author-reported; no emulator/tests were run. Copyrighted ROMs are not bundled; source contains routines to rebuild/check public ROM listings, and some tests skip without ROMs. README offers MIT or Apache-2.0 for the emulator. Copyrighted Commodore ROMs are not included; reconstruction from public listings and local browser storage do not change the underlying ROM rights.  Author says Claude assisted code generation/refactoring, tests and VICE comparison; design decisions, reviews and real-software testing remain the author's. Reviewed on 2026-10-05; no independent build, execution or byte comparison was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/rvanee/c64wasm/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/rvanee/c64wasm/blob/main/crates/c64-core/src/c64/board.rs https://github.com/rvanee/c64wasm/blob/main/crates/c64-core/src/cpu/mos6502.rs https://github.com/rvanee/c64wasm/blob/main/Cargo.toml https://github.com/rvanee/c64wasm/blob/main/build_wasm.sh https://github.com/rvanee/c64wasm/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml Latest upstream commit: https://github.com/rvanee/c64wasm/commit/adeaa0986801bc4f747593fa72463ef3ac6b6d5e

discovery-cannonball-c.title: Cannonball-C for Amiga
discovery-cannonball-c.notes: Amiga 68k port of djcc ANSI C conversion of djyt Cannonball, based on September 2015 code. Distinct host/language adaptation of reverse-engineered OutRun engine; original Cannonball lineage credited.

castle-master-ii-spectrum-disassembly.title: Castle Master II Spectrum annotated disassembly
castle-master-ii-spectrum-disassembly.display_title: Castle Master II Spectrum annotated disassembly
subjects: Castle Master II Spectrum annotated disassembly
castle-master-ii-spectrum-disassembly.notes: Santiago Ontañón’s original and annotated game/loader listings for the Freescape title; includes author interpretation of rendering, clipping and math, with MDL-assisted loader pass. Do not transfer scope to CPC.

cat-mouse-zx-spectrum-next.title: Cat and Mouse
cat-mouse-zx-spectrum-next.display_title: Cat and Mouse — creator-remade ZX Spectrum Next maze game
source_language: Game Boy Advance assets and level data
cat-mouse-zx-spectrum-next.notes: Steve Monks remade his own earlier Spectrum/Amiga/GBA concept in native Z80/Next assembly. Zeus project includes real maze/AI/object logic and emits .snx; README identifies tested Zeus 3.98 and explains compile/run workflow. No independent build/play; snapshot format and old Zeus expectations must be kept as documented. Earlier versions are provenance, not separate projects. README explicitly names tested Zeus command-line version 3.98, generated .snx and emulator/hardware run instructions; distributed snapshot exists. No independent build/play test.

caverns-freitag-apple2-6502disassembly.title: Caverns of Freitag
caverns-freitag-apple2-6502disassembly.display_title: Caverns of Freitag — Apple II mixed-language disassembly
caverns-freitag-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Apple II Caverns of Freitag archaeology covering the Applesoft programs, machine-language graphics/ampersand routines, map and object data, with a SourceGen project set for the binaries.

cc65-lynx-game-template.title: CC65 Game template
cc65-lynx-game-template.display_title: CC65 Game template — Atari Lynx reproducible development environment
cc65-lynx-game-template.notes: Atari Lynx game starter with C/assembly runtime code, debug/release linker configurations, sprite-packing steps and cartridge images. Makefile targets Lynx with cc65/ca65/cl65; the devcontainer builds cc65 in Alpine. Catalogued as reusable development infrastructure rather than a standalone finished game.

cd32launch-jotd.title: CD32Launch
cd32launch-jotd.notes: Runs OS-compliant Amiga games with CD32 joypad remapping, memory/chipset downgrading, VBR patching and optional small patchlist slaves. Its readme contains copied CD32Load option text after the introductory launch-specific section; avoid treating those options as independently verified CD32Launch behavior.

cd32load-jotd.title: CD32Load
cd32load-jotd.notes: CD32/IDE loader for WHDLoad slaves. README reports selected A600 installs with 1 MB chip RAM and testing on real CD32 and A1200; this is game dependent, not a universal 1 MB minimum.

cdtv-ir-keyboard-protocol.title: CDTV IR keyboard — U75 ROM-derived transmitter
cdtv-ir-keyboard-protocol.display_title: CDTV IR keyboard — U75 ROM-derived transmitter
cdtv-ir-keyboard-protocol.notes: Documents 40-bit wireless keyboard framing, qualifiers and timings discovered in the CDTV U75 controller ROM, with a Pico SDK C transmitter demo currently pinned to the Pico 2 W board. The build does not pin Arm versus RISC-V output, so no target CPU is asserted. Link the already tracked U75 analysis as predecessor; no claim that Commodore shipped the keyboard.

cdtv-os-235-patch.title: CDTV OS 2.35 patch

runtime_profiles.name: CDTV/A570 patched ROM
runtime_profiles.notes: The FAQ says timing was checked for 68000, 68010 and 68020. It does not state a minimum RAM figure.

runtime_profiles.name: Tested 68030 accelerator configurations
runtime_profiles.notes: The FAQ reports TF536 and Viper 530 testing; 68040/68060 remain unknown, and one A570 setup needs its 2 MB expansion disabled.

cdtv-os-235-patch.notes: Public bsdiff patch transforms a user-supplied Commodore 2.30 Extended ROM into unofficial 2.35 images. Author says original modules were reconstructed as byte-matching assembly after Ghidra/vasm analysis; that source and complete ROM images are not published, so exactness is an upstream claim rather than independently verified here. The FAQ explicitly covers 68000/68010/68020 timing and tested 68030 accelerators; it leaves 68040/68060 compatibility unknown.

amiga-cdtv-u62-firmware.title: CDTV U62 — front-panel controller firmware analysis
amiga-cdtv-u62-firmware.upstream_name: CDTV U62 — front-panel controller firmware analysis
amiga-cdtv-u62-firmware.display_title: CDTV U62 — front-panel controller firmware analysis
amiga-cdtv-u62-firmware.notes: Annotated LC6554H U62 controller ROM listing with address/raw bytes and a Python disassembler. Covers CDTV front panel, remote-control link and CD-drive behavior. Listing is expressly for reading, not assembling; one BANK interpretation remains unproven.

cdtv-u75-rom-disassembly.title: CDTV U75 controller ROM disassembly
cdtv-u75-rom-disassembly.notes: 6500/1 U75 controller ROM disassembly documents IR remote, keyboard and CDTV front-panel protocols. Original pre-production ROM dump is credited to CDTV Land (2022); this repository analyzes that dump rather than claiming to have made it. The README explicitly credits Claude-assisted emulator-harness development and a final codebase review.

cdtvload-jotd.title: CDTVLoad
cdtvload-jotd.notes: Loader for non-DOS games from CD using WHDLoad slaves. Source contains an IRA-derived partial reversal of an earlier Psygore loader; no general build or runtime result established.

centipede-arcade-6502disassembly.title: Centipede
centipede-arcade-6502disassembly.notes: Centipede rev 4 arcade ROM disassembly with SourceGen project files/binaries, binary-construction instructions and substantial analysis of graphics, entity behavior, difficulty progression and cocktail-mode display handling.

championship-lode-runner-c64.title: Championship Lode Runner
championship-lode-runner-c64.notes: Commented reconstructed source including copy protection; repository description states the goal is a bit-for-bit identical recreation.

championship-manager-italia-st-decompila.title: Championship Manager Italia — ST reconstruction
championship-manager-italia-st-decompila.notes: Reconstructed the hard-drive install executable in assembly using Ghidra and Fred’s disassembler. Author documents a VASM build tested in Hatari, with code approximately 99% covered and an optional copy-protection bypass; rebuilt program is explicitly not 100% accurate to the original. The CMAN93 folder contains English 1993 game binaries, without a second published source reconstruction.

chaos-guesser-szeliga-spectrum.title: Chaos: The Battle of Wizards — Guesser/szeliga
chaos-guesser-szeliga-spectrum.display_title: Chaos: The Battle of Wizards — Guesser/szeliga
chaos-guesser-szeliga-spectrum.notes: Incomplete commented Chaos disassembly by Guesser and szeliga, preserved in Michael Cook's archive and rendered at zxnet.co.uk.

chaos-lewis-lane-spectrum.title: Chaos: The Battle of Wizards — Lewis Lane
chaos-lewis-lane-spectrum.display_title: Chaos: The Battle of Wizards — Lewis Lane
chaos-lewis-lane-spectrum.notes: Modern annotated Chaos disassembly with extensive engine/data documentation and explicit Claude Code assistance.

chase-hq-spectrum.title: Chase H.Q.
chase-hq-spectrum.notes: Function-by-function readable C reconstruction developed alongside the Spectrum disassembly. The SkoolKit path rebuilds a Z80 TAP for real Spectrum hardware; the portable SDL, WebAssembly and RISC OS host builds do not establish a single additional native CPU target or minimum host specification.

chase-hq-spectrum-analyser.title: Chase H.Q.
chase-hq-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Chase H.Q. — ZX Spectrum analyser project
chase-hq-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The ChaseHQ directory contains an approximately 1193 KiB Analysis.json annotation database plus a custom Lua viewer script. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

chiller-c64-unorig.title: Chiller
chiller-c64-unorig.notes: Reverse-engineered/decompiled C64 Chiller source. Current documentation says the project has moved to Regenerator 2000 for analysis and preserves/analyzes both known soundtrack variants.

chiller2-c64-homebrew.title: Chiller 2: The Return of the Jackal
chiller2-c64-homebrew.upstream_name: Chiller 2: The Return of the Jackal
subjects: Chiller 2: The Return of the Jackal
chiller2-c64-homebrew.notes: Andy Vaisey/Cosine's source-available 2020 C64 platform game with twelve levels, playable boy/girl characters and PAL/NTSC handling. readme.txt documents controls, gameplay and named playtesters. ACME assembly source specifies PRG output and exomizer packaging; D64/TAP releases are present.

chip-and-dale-2-nes-g0me3.title: Chip 'n Dale Rescue Rangers 2
chip-and-dale-2-nes-g0me3.display_title: Chip 'n Dale Rescue Rangers 2 (NES) — Back From Source
chip-and-dale-2-nes-g0me3.notes: Back From Source reconstruction with separate program banks, script/text material and DASM assembly scripts producing a NES image. RetroRE classifies the disassembly as partial; no byte-exact equivalence or minimum hardware profile is asserted.

chipschallenge-lynx-native-recomp.title: Chip's Challenge Lynx Recomp
chipschallenge-lynx-native-recomp.display_title: Chip's Challenge — Atari Lynx native-C static recompilation

execution_paths.name: Generated native-C host
execution_paths.notes: Title-screen/headless bounded execution is documented. Host input is fixed to zero; interactive frontend wiring is pending. The generic toolkit interpreter prepares the initial snapshot but is not linked as the game-host execution path.

chipschallenge-lynx-native-recomp.notes: Experimental native-C static recompilation of the Atari Lynx game using lynxrecomp. The game-specific host registers generated functions and calls the translated entry point; it does not execute guest instructions through a CPU interpreter. Upstream demonstrates title-screen rendering, while interactive live input remains future work. User-supplied cartridge/boot ROM and generated C are required. Only fixed-function Suzy/Mikey support hardware is modeled by the runtime.

chips-8bit-chip-system-emulators.title: chips — embeddable 8-bit chip and system emulators
chips-8bit-chip-system-emulators.display_title: chips — embeddable 8-bit chip and system emulators
chips-8bit-chip-system-emulators.notes: Dependency-free C headers implement pin-level chips and embeddable C64/CPC/ZX/VIC20 system emulators. Separate chips-test repository carries runnable examples and validation; this root is the core implementation.

chips-test-8bit-emulator-examples.title: chips-test — runnable 8-bit emulator samples
chips-test-8bit-emulator-examples.notes: Separate test and example repository for floooh/chips headers, with runnable CPC and other machine emulators and WebAssembly demo build. Track parent chip/system implementation separately; these are validation/examples, not a CPC reconstruction.

chipwits-c-classic-mac-port.title: ChipWits-C — unfinished Forth-to-C Macintosh port
chipwits-c-classic-mac-port.status: Unfinished Forth-to-C Macintosh conversion; upstream explicitly says it does not build or work yet.
chipwits-c-classic-mac-port.notes: Substantial modular C game/controller/robot/room/editor implementation accompanies preserved Forth reference code. Robot actions explicitly map Forth screens to C dispatch and stack operations. README identifies Think C 5+ and classic one-bit Macintosh targets. The official original-source archive is separately recorded as chipwits-forth-original-source. Pomme/modern-host support is an aspiration, not an implemented target. Preserved Forth is reference material; the produced language is C. Distinct unfinished C conversion based directly on the official chipwits/chipwits-forth source release, separately catalogued in this same batch. LICENSE credits the 2025 C code to 45RPM Software Ltd under CC BY-SA 4.0, retains other original holders’ resource/Forth copyrights, and identifies ChipWits-Forth as ChipWits, Inc. ©1984–2024 under CC BY-SA 4.0. ChipWits trademark rights are retained. Reviewed 2026-10-05 by primary documentation, source, build-file and tree inspection. All local build, test, emulation and runtime checks remain unperformed. Positive flags are evidence-scoped upstream reports only; byte_exact remains unknown. Last activity is the latest default-branch commit date, not repository creation or pushed_at. chipwits-forth-original-source.title: ChipWits-FORTH — original Macintosh and C64 source restoration
chipwits-forth-original-source.display_title: ChipWits-FORTH — original Macintosh and C64 source restoration
types: Official original-source preservation and build restoration
chipwits-forth-original-source.status: Official original-source restoration with separate upstream-documented C64 disk/Super Forth and Macintosh disk/MacForth build/run procedures.
chipwits-forth-original-source.notes: Official ChipWits organization preserves original author Doug Sharp's restored source disks and readable Forth listings. Inspected game screens contain original game loaders, robot variables, opcode dispatch and game definitions. C64 instructions reconstruct compiler/loading order and include Python-to-D64 Forth screen restoration; Mac instructions build from the preserved final-source disk inside MacForth. Apple II source has not been recovered; scans/emulation links do not establish an Apple II source reconstruction. The main-branch latest commit is 2025-03-26 despite repository pushed_at being 2026-10-05. Keep readable exports and buildable disk images distinct. Original source archive from the rights-holder organization, separate from PascalHarris's unfinished C translation. Keep Mac/C64 editions within one preservation root for this candidate. This release is distinct from PascalHarris’s derivative C conversion and from the current commercial reboot. Reviewed 2026-10-05 by primary documentation, source, build-file and tree inspection. choplifter-apple2-reconstruction.title: ChoplifterReverse
choplifter-apple2-reconstruction.display_title: Choplifter — Apple II clean-room source reconstruction
choplifter-apple2-reconstruction.notes: Full clean-room reverse engineering of the 1982 Apple II Choplifter from the disk binary alone. The reconstructed game code is documented and builds/runs; the game portion is described as binary-identical, while the original custom floppy loader was intentionally replaced with a new ProDOS loader, so the complete produced disk is not treated as byte-exact.

chroma-grid-atari-game.title: Chroma Grid — Atari STe puzzle-game revival
chroma-grid-atari-game.display_title: Chroma Grid — Atari STe puzzle-game revival
chroma-grid-atari-game.status: Author-reported Sommarhack 2024 game release, reviving an unfinished 1994 original.
chroma-grid-atari-game.notes: T.O.Y.S. game released at Sommarhack 2024, described by its author as bringing an unfinished 1994 game to life. C++ game/level/editor sources are present; native executable build includes sibling toybox makefiles, and main.cpp selects Atari machine variants. Requires toybox 1.1 in a sibling tree. The host build references blitter emulation, but the Atari target is native C++ rather than a game-specific CPU interpreter. Do not infer every ST/Falcon model is fully supported from detection code. README says the game was released at Sommarhack 2024, supporting author-reported runnable/playable output. Current source compilation remains unverified and depends on a sibling toybox tree. No independent compilation, execution or benchmarking was performed during this catalogue review. Evidence: https://github.com/PeyloW/ChromaGrid/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/PeyloW/ChromaGrid/blob/main/Makefile https://github.com/PeyloW/ChromaGrid/blob/main/src/main.cpp https://github.com/PeyloW/ChromaGrid/blob/main/src/game.cpp https://github.com/PeyloW/ChromaGrid/commit/d7df07009696e1dbad4624045c7fddcb48a2ab8d https://github.com/PeyloW/toybox/blob/main/common.mk The repository also provides an SDL2 host-development build path; no precise supported host-OS list was established.

chronos-beeper-spectrum-study.title: Chronos — Spectrum beeper engine disassembly
chronos-beeper-spectrum-study.notes: Work-in-progress extracted Tim Follin Chronos music engine with assembly, songs and Makefile, plus notes distinguishing polyphony, bass, melody and drums; a subsystem study, not a whole-game source.

chuchu-rocket-atari-st-reforged.title: Chu Chu Rocket
chuchu-rocket-atari-st-reforged.display_title: Chu Chu Rocket — Atari ST byte-matched disassembly
chuchu-rocket-atari-st-reforged.notes: Complete, named 68000 source for Reservoir Gods' Atari ST Chu Chu Rocket 1.18 LITE. Default build reproduces CHUCHU.TOS and CHUCHU.LNK byte-identically; optional Reforged optimizations and fixes deliberately differ. README reports tests in Hatari and on a real Mega STe and explicitly credits Claude assistance. This is distinct from the original game's development source.

chuckie-egg-spectrum-ritchie.title: Chuckie Egg Spectrum Ritchie disassembly
chuckie-egg-spectrum-ritchie.notes: Separate Chuckie Egg Spectrum disassembly with assembly and source; Michael Cook’s later independent SkoolKit project credits some of its audio comments. Keep research attribution distinct.

chuckie-egg-spectrum-mrcook.title: Chuckie Egg Spectrum SkoolKit disassembly
chuckie-egg-spectrum-mrcook.notes: WIP tape-derived SkoolKit listing and control files, loader and game analyses; README credits selected audio comments from Ritchie Swann’s separate disassembly.

chzpart-atari-disk.title: CHZ Atari Disk Partitioning Tool
chzpart-atari-disk.notes: Partitions Atari-compatible disks on hardware with XHDI or prepares disk-image files on other systems. Supports TOS-era layouts and FAT16 initialization; this is original modern tooling rather than a reverse-engineered historical utility.

cidos-c64-disk-commands.title: CIDOS — Commodore disk BASIC commands
cidos-c64-disk-commands.notes: John C. Dale's assembly extension adds BASIC disk operations on C64 with 1541 and SD2IEC; source has a main CIDOS.asm and command include modules. Separate implementation from the tutorial index; README examples are upstream documentation, not independent runtime tests.

citadel2-electron-port.title: citadel2
citadel2-electron-port.display_title: Citadel 2 — BBC Micro to Acorn Electron port
citadel2-electron-port.notes: 2026 Acorn Electron port of the BBC Micro game; distributed as playable UEF/SSD images requiring 48K. Repository does not publish port source.

cjs-elephant-antics-spectrum-petemoore.title: CJ’s Elephant Antics Spectrum analysis
cjs-elephant-antics-spectrum-petemoore.notes: Partial loader/code disassembly plus Go map extractor and reconstructed level maps from the Spectrum tape blocks; development state described explicitly in README.

classic-mac-rom-source-reconstruction.title: Classic Macintosh ROM source reconstruction
classic-mac-rom-source-reconstruction.notes: Fully commented buildable source tree for five classic Macintosh ROM variants (128K, 512K and three Plus ROMs). The build explicitly verifies all five outputs as bit-identical to their reference ROMs.

clib2-amiga-c-runtime.title: clib2
clib2-amiga-c-runtime.notes: Amiga-specific ISO C runtime and headers written from scratch to support GCC-based Amiga development. No claim that it was recovered from a binary.

climber-5-atari-2600.title: Climber 5

runtime_profiles.notes: Joystick game for Atari 2600; README also documents 7800 pause-button behavior and PAL50 hardware testing.

climber-5-atari-2600.notes: Dennis Debro's authored Atari 2600 adaptation of the 1987 Atari 8-bit Climber 5. The README distinguishes the faithful Original mode from new Normal and Advanced designs and explicitly discusses 6502/7 assembly optimization. This is original homebrew adaptation work, not a reverse-engineered source reconstruction.

discovery-clock-tower-vm.title: Clock Tower VM analysis
discovery-clock-tower-vm.notes: ADC object-file disassembler/decompiler with Ghidra and IDA processor/debugger components, parser and PC/PlayStation listings. This is bytecode analysis, not evidence of a playable game emulator.

cobra-spectrum-analyser.title: Cobra
cobra-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Cobra directory contains an approximately 2645 KiB Analysis.json annotation database plus project configuration and graphics metadata. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

commodore-btx-decoder-ii-firmware-recons.title: Commodore BTX Decoder II — 6801 and C64 firmware reconstruction

types: firmware reverse engineering / commented mixed-CPU disassembly
commodore-btx-decoder-ii-firmware-recons.status: Commented mixed-CPU firmware reconstruction; byte-identical reassembly is upstream-reported and not independently rerun.
commodore-btx-decoder-ii-firmware-recons.notes: Reconstructs the 32-KiB Commodore Bildschirmtext Decoder II ROM. Generated 6801 firmware and separate C64 6502 bootstrap/payload sources are driven by maintained Python tools and TOML analysis annotations. Firmware/terminal-software reconstruction, not a game. The project-specific disassembler and checker serve the named ROM; bundled reference material is not separately promoted. README explicitly reports tools/check_asl.sh passing with zero assembler errors/warnings and an identical ROM, supporting compilable=true solely as an upstream-reported result. Local assembly, tests and binary comparison were not run; byte_exact remains null. Exit 77 is a skipped independent check, not success. No firmware execution claim is adopted. Byte-identical reconstruction and an independent ASL cross-check are author-reported, not rerun here. Round-trip identity does not establish full semantic recovery: documentation discusses static trace gaps and computed jumps, while the later build code describes typed tables and soft vectors. This is firmware/terminal software, not a game. Both legacy ROM revisions are committed, along with third-party assembler/ROM/reference material. No top-level license file was found; bundled third-party material must retain its separate provenance and rights. Project moved from sarnau/C64-BTX-Module. prior-analysis/README.md identifies the earlier repository and historical extraction. Both roots are absent from catalogue data. Recent commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5. The evidence is an explicit commit credit; it does not quantify AI contribution across the project. Reviewed on 2026-10-05; no independent build, execution or byte comparison was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/sarnau/btx-re/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/sarnau/btx-re/blob/main/out/btx_decoder_ii.asm https://github.com/sarnau/btx-re/blob/main/out/c64_payload.asm https://github.com/sarnau/btx-re/blob/main/prior-analysis/README.md https://github.com/sarnau/btx-re/blob/main/build.py https://github.com/sarnau/btx-re/blob/main/tools/check_asl.sh Latest upstream commit: https://github.com/sarnau/btx-re/commit/8c22d67ee17753020c1e3576ba0bb0523e9eab98

defender-c64-cartridge-disassembly.title: Defender — C64 cartridge disassembly
defender-c64-cartridge-disassembly.status: Substantial cartridge disassembly with reassembly tasks; build and gameplay unverified.
defender-c64-cartridge-disassembly.notes: Defender C64 cartridge disassembly, including game code, character set and sprites. README describes a CRT build with minimal commentary; the native source begins at $8000 with a CBM80 cartridge header. This is the batch’s game-disassembly record. It represents the C64 Defender binary, not the original arcade version or a new homebrew game. README says Ready To Use in VS Code, and tasks invoke KickAssembler, fc /b against _original_defender.bin and VICE cartconv. Author-specific Windows paths require adaptation. The presence of original/rebuilt BIN and CRT files and a comparison task is not a verified comparison result; all build flags remain unknown. The README describes a minimally commented CRT disassembly. An 8,673-line assembly file, character/sprite sources, original BIN, rebuilt BIN/CRT and a compare task are present. Windows VS Code tasks have author-specific paths. No assembly, binary comparison or gameplay was performed in this review. No root license file was present in the reviewed tree. Original cartridge data and graphics remain legacy assets; source availability is not a grant of redistribution rights. GitHub root is canonical DEFENDER-c64; one historical merge message names mikroman/DEFENDER. No Defender project or either supplied canonical root was present in the catalogue.  Reviewed on 2026-10-05; no independent build, execution or byte comparison was performed. ghidra-retro-machines.title: ghidra-retro-machines
ghidra-retro-machines.display_title: Ghidra Retro Machines — bank-aware loaders and retro CPU languages
ghidra-retro-machines.notes: Ghidra extension configures banked memory maps, ROMs, hardware registers and symbols for C64/C128/PET PRG and NES iNES analysis, and bundles explicit SPC700 and 65C816 language variants for SNES code. The SPC700 language is decode-capable with p-code still under rewrite; the 65C816 language is disassembly-oriented while its p-code is verified against exhaustive vectors. Current NES work resolves proven constant-pointer indirect jumps and bounds table-after-code jump tables by their switch window; Mega Man and Life Force rows were re-blessed, while Contra, Final Fantasy and TMNT changes remain held for owner review. Its exhaustive 65C816 vector baseline now reports 500 PASS, 8 N/A and 4 FAIL rows after isolating one named SBC (dp,X) test-vector oracle defect. The exception is guarded by tripwires that fail if the case starts passing or disappears, so it cannot mask wider regressions. Build and real-ROM gates therefore demonstrate bounded progress rather than universal correctness claims.
