The primary page distributes CPR, DSK and CDT images and explicitly states that no generative AI was used; it does not name the rebuilt program's CPU or a RAM minimum.

has-high-amiga-assembler.title: HAS (High Assembler)
has-high-amiga-assembler.notes: Python compiler for an assembly-first high-level language with typed control flow, inline assembly, macros, register control and Amiga libraries. hasc contains parser, AST, validators, code generator and optimizer; asset tools and examples remain part of this coherent compiler project. The compiler emits assembly and requires separately installed vasm/vlink for executables.

hatari-atari-emulator-debugger.title: Hatari
source_language: Atari hardware and TOS software behavior
hatari-atari-emulator-debugger.notes: Core Atari ST/STE/TT/Falcon emulator with a built-in debugger, conditional breakpoints, disassembly, symbol support, CPU/DSP profiling and remote-control facilities. Tracked as foundational software-archaeology and reproducible Atari development infrastructure.

sarnau-hatari-68k-disassembler.title: Hatari 68k disassembler component
sarnau-hatari-68k-disassembler.notes: Original author’s C 68k disassembler for Hatari covers 68k variants and FPU/PMMU. README says it requires the Hatari source to compile and is not a standalone runnable tool.

hatari-libretro-atari-core.title: Hatari libretro core
hatari-libretro-atari-core.display_title: Hatari — libretro Atari ST core adaptation
source_language: Atari hardware and m68k system behavior
hatari-libretro-atari-core.notes: Libretro-maintained rebasing of upstream Hatari 2.6.1. Root README retains Hatari documentation, but inspected src/retro contains libretro-specific main, disk control, VFS, screen, timing, audio and input integration. Core-specific integration is the recorded divergence; no separate original Atari binary analysis claimed.

haunted-house-atari2600-disassembly.title: Haunted House
haunted-house-atari2600-disassembly.notes: Work-in-progress reverse engineering and commented disassembly of Atari 2600 Haunted House. The README documents a DASM make/build path that produces haunted.bin for execution in Stella and includes decoded sprite/font observations.

head-over-heels-cpc.title: Head Over Heels
head-over-heels-cpc.notes: CPC reverse engineering includes code, room data and sound/music work; closely related Spectrum analysis is a useful cross-reference.

head-over-heels-spectrum.title: Head Over Heels
head-over-heels-spectrum.notes: Disassembly is repeatedly checked by recompiling back to the original Spectrum memory image.

head-over-heels-spectrum-analyser.title: Head Over Heels
head-over-heels-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Head Over Heels — ZX Spectrum analyser project
head-over-heels-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The HeadOverHeels directory contains an approximately 1008 KiB Analysis.json annotation database, plus custom overlay/viewer scripts; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

head-over-heels-spectrum-mkrivos.title: Head Over Heels Spectrum annotated reconstruction
head-over-heels-spectrum-mkrivos.display_title: Head Over Heels Spectrum annotated reconstruction
subjects: Head Over Heels Spectrum annotated reconstruction
head-over-heels-spectrum-mkrivos.notes: AI-assisted labelled Z80 listing for 48K/128K Head Over Heels, code-walk, game data and room render studies. README claims 100% line annotation and byte-exact output; these claims were not rerun.

hellgate-vic20.title: Hellgate
hellgate-vic20.notes: Disassembled and commented source for Jeff Minter's 1984 VIC-20 game Hellgate, with a reproducible 64tass build and runnable/browser version.

helloami-amiga-boot-workbench.title: HelloAmi
helloami-amiga-boot-workbench.display_title: HelloAmi — Amiga bootblocks and Workbench library reimplementation

runtime_profiles.name: ROM Workbench bootstrap
runtime_profiles.notes: README supplies per-ROM compatibility, including 1.0–3.1 and AROS. icon.library replacement targets V1.x; later ROMs already include it. LoadWB requires a ROM containing Workbench, with stated exceptions. No minimum CPU/RAM inferred.

helloami-amiga-boot-workbench.notes: Implements a small icon.library replacement so Workbench in V1.x ROMs can start without original Workbench disk files, a dynamic version.library, minimal OFS disk images and bootblocks including beta-Kickstart handling. Upstream reports broad ROM tests and documents unsupported LoadWB combinations. Not merely a Hello World tutorial; no CPU emulation core is involved.

vs-sr-cd32-heroquest2.title: HeroQuest II: Legacy of Sorasil — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-heroquest2.display_title: HeroQuest II: Legacy of Sorasil — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-heroquest2.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of HeroQuest II: Legacy of Sorasil. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

hex-survivors-bbc-mode7.title: HEX survivors
hex-survivors-bbc-mode7.display_title: HEX survivors — BBC Micro Mode 7 arena-survival game

runtime_profiles.name: BBC Micro Model B game
runtime_profiles.notes: README explicitly specifies BBC Micro Model B with 32 KB; source targets Mode 7 and guards below display memory.

hex-survivors-bbc-mode7.notes: Native 6502 source implements Mode 7 initialization, player/enemy state and auto-firing arena-survival gameplay; BeebAsm PowerShell build creates SSD. Creator explicitly credits Codex and Copilot and identifies Model B/32KB target. No independent build/play; script hardcodes Windows assembler/emulator paths and validates both even for build. Modern homebrew inspired by Vampire Survivors, not reconstruction of a legacy original. Creator supplies SSD, gameplay instructions and BeebAsm build path. These establish upstream build/play evidence only; paths are hardcoded and were not reproduced here.

highway-encounter-spectrum.title: Highway Encounter
highway-encounter-spectrum.notes: nzeemin SkoolKit reverse-engineering project. README status: Not finished.

hissoft-devpac-cpc.title: HiSoft DEVPAC (GENA/MONA)
hissoft-devpac-cpc.notes: Reverse engineering of the CPC DEVPAC assembler/editor and disassembler/debugger; both reconstructed listings reproduce their binaries byte-for-byte.

hlipa-amiga-ataribaby42.title: Hlípa — Atari ST to Amiga reconstruction/port
hlipa-amiga-ataribaby42.display_title: Hlípa — Atari ST to Amiga reconstruction/port

runtime_profiles.name: Low-resolution colour build
runtime_profiles.notes: The README requires at least 1 MB total RAM, including 512 KB Chip RAM. Workbench launch can require more free memory than booting from ADF.

evidence.excerpt: MC68000 or newer, OCS or newer, Kickstart 1.3 or newer, and at least 1 MB RAM with 512 KB Chip RAM.

runtime_profiles.name: Monochrome HIRES LACE build
runtime_profiles.notes: Also requires a display device supporting Amiga HIRES LACE: PAL 640x512 or NTSC 640x400. ECS and AGA are explicitly unnecessary.

evidence.excerpt: The HI version uses the same 68000/OCS/1 MB baseline and requires an Amiga HIRES LACE PAL 640x512 or NTSC 640x400 display.

hlipa-amiga-ataribaby42.notes: Native Amiga conversion of Hlípa built from reconstruction of the original Atari ST program. Both low-resolution and monochrome HIRES LACE variants use one -m68000 code base and require OCS+, Kickstart 1.3+, 1 MB total RAM and 512 KB Chip RAM; the HI variant also needs a suitable interlaced display mode. WinUAE coverage spans 68000, 68020 and 68060 configurations, while physical hardware remains untested.

hlipa-zx-ataribaby42.title: Hlípa — PMD 85 to ZX Spectrum reconstruction/port
hlipa-zx-ataribaby42.display_title: Hlípa — PMD 85 to ZX Spectrum reconstruction/port

runtime_profiles.name: Czech and English builds
runtime_profiles.notes: Runs at the normal model speed and needs neither extra memory nor AY sound. Upstream has simulator coverage for 48K and the original 128K ROM, but no physical-hardware test yet.

evidence.excerpt: Native Z80 code for ZX Spectrum 48K using the standard ROM; only 48K memory is used and neither extra memory nor AY is required.

hlipa-zx-ataribaby42.notes: Reconstructs and relocates the PMD 85 game logic as native Z80 code for ZX Spectrum 48K. Version 1.3 builds Czech and English TAP/SNA variants; the English variant translates menus, instructions, statistics and ending screens while sharing game logic and data. Extensive simulator regressions cover loading and gameplay through victory, but physical hardware remains untested.

hode-heart-of-darkness.title: hode
hode-heart-of-darkness.display_title: Heart of Darkness — reimplemented Windows engine
source_language: Heart of Darkness Windows demo/CD data
hode-heart-of-darkness.notes: Source reimplementation of the Heart of Darkness engine for original Windows demo/CD data. Documentation lists concrete resource files and tested releases; no original Amiga or Atari ST edition is asserted.

hollywood-poker-spectrum.title: Hollywood Poker
hollywood-poker-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

hopper-atari-tos-falcon-disassembler.title: hopper — Atari TOS and Falcon DSP disassembler
hopper-atari-tos-falcon-disassembler.upstream_name: hopper — Atari TOS and Falcon DSP disassembler
hopper-atari-tos-falcon-disassembler.display_title: hopper — Atari TOS and Falcon DSP disassembler
subjects: Atari TOS executables and Falcon DSP programs
tags: Atari TOS executables and Falcon DSP programs
hopper-atari-tos-falcon-disassembler.notes: Separate hopper68 and hopper56 command-line disassemblers decode Atari TOS 68000 executables and Falcon DSP program files. Instruction decoding lives in reusable libraries; shell build scripts and a Visual Studio project are present. No game-specific runtime or execution layer.

hover-bovver-c64.title: Hover Bovver
hover-bovver-c64.notes: Reverse-engineered and commented-source project for Jeff Minter's C64 Hover Bovver. The repository states that the game compiles and plays, while further cleanup and labelling remain.

huc6280disasm-andlabs.title: huc6280disasm
huc6280disasm-andlabs.notes: Go HuC6280 disassembler for flat boot ROMs and TurboGrafx-16-compatible ROM behavior. It follows code flow and attempts to track the stack and accumulator rather than performing only a linear sweep.

hugo-delire-hugo-js-cyxx.title: hugo.js
hugo-delire-hugo-js-cyxx.notes: Small HTML5 player for the Hugo Délire train mini-game, plus C resource-directory, animation unpack and BMP conversion tools. README documents the playable Web train sequence and root Makefile builds extract_dir and convert_ani. Scope is one mini-game and resource pipeline, not a complete Hugo Délire reimplementation; original executable architecture and resource edition are not established.

hulabee-sauce-vm-cyxx.title: Hulabee Sauce VM
hulabee-sauce-vm-cyxx.display_title: Hulabee Sauce — VM and asset tools
hulabee-sauce-vm-cyxx.notes: SDL2 rewrite of the proprietary Hulabee Sauce VM with .pan/.gg asset decoders and whisk.dll opcode tracing. vm/README.md names Moop and Dreadly and Ollo as supported games, requires original .pan files, and lists missing captions and VM garbage collection. The inspected tree establishes architecture-neutral Sauce bytecode but does not state the architecture of the original Windows tracing DLL or executable.

hunchback-c64-mark.title: Hunchback
hunchback-c64-mark.display_title: Hunchback — C64 byte-exact reverse engineering & restructure
hunchback-c64-mark.notes: C64 Hunchback reverse engineering with two lines of work: an explicitly byte-exact labelled reconstruction of the original game and a restructured variant with code tweaks, routine merging and data reorganisation.

hunchback-spectrum-ritchie.title: Hunchback Spectrum disassembly
hunchback-spectrum-ritchie.notes: Work-in-progress Spectrum Hunchback assembly source and build script with linked published analysis; unrelated to the separately tracked C64 Hunchback study.

hydrofool-spectrum.title: Hydrofool
hydrofool-spectrum.notes: nzeemin SkoolKit reverse-engineering project. README status: Good progress.

hyp2gdos-source-reconstruction.title: Hyp2GDOS — Atari ST source reconstruction
hyp2gdos-source-reconstruction.notes: Author readme.txt describes reconstructed sources for the 1997 Hyp2GDOS 1.1 binary that compile to an almost identical result. Disassembly listings and C source included; register allocation differs in places, so byte identity is not claimed.

hyper-sports-spectrum-analyser.title: Hyper Sports
hyper-sports-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Hyper Sports — ZX Spectrum analyser project
hyper-sports-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Hyper Sports directory contains an approximately 807 KiB Analysis.json annotation database; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

jotd-hyper-sports-amiga.title: Hyper Sports — Amiga arcade transcode

runtime_profiles.name: ECS version
runtime_profiles.notes: README requires 1 MB Chip RAM and some additional Fast RAM, but does not quantify the Fast-RAM amount.

evidence.quote: ECS version needs whdload, 1MB chip and some fast

runtime_profiles.name: AGA version
runtime_profiles.notes: README documents bootable-floppy and WHDLoad AGA variants without a CPU/RAM minimum.

evidence.quote: AGA comes in bootable floppy or whdload

jotd-hyper-sports-amiga.notes: Hyper Sports / Hyper Olympic '84 remake for AGA/ECS Amiga; README credits transcode, Amiga port, graphics and sound conversion.

hyperloader-cpc-llopis.title: HyperLoader
hyperloader-cpc-llopis.display_title: HyperLoader — CPC fast tape loader and CDT generator
hyperloader-cpc-llopis.notes: Concrete fast CPC tape loader with adaptive pulse measurement, synchronization and native loading code, paired with a Python CDT generator. Source credits Mert Boru's TurboLoader as the basis; this repository adds an implemented paired workflow rather than a passive binary mirror. Loader and generator inspected; generator uses Python 2 syntax. No build/run verification performed.

hagar-the-horrible-c64-source-preservati.title: Hägar the Horrible — C64 original-source preservation
hagar-the-horrible-c64-source-preservati.display_title: Hägar the Horrible — C64 original-source preservation
hagar-the-horrible-c64-source-preservati.notes: Preserves original programmer-supplied Hägar the Horrible source disks, extracted tokenized files and readable assembly. README documents VICE c1541/TMPview/petcat extraction; it does not demonstrate rebuilding the game or byte equality. released_files/HAGAR.TXT credits programmer Rasmus Wernersson and Gamebase64, identifies German release/unpublished English version, and is dated 23 June 2001. This conflicts with the README's stated 2021 release, so no source-release or reconstruction start date is asserted. Whole repository is one preservation project.

ida-amiga-hunk-loader-lab313ru.title: IDA Amiga Hunk loader
ida-amiga-hunk-loader-lab313ru.notes: Python IDA Pro loader for Amiga Hunk executables. Its primary loader source returns and selects IDA processor `68040` for imported inputs and implements Hunk parsing/relocation; this is loader-selected analysis architecture, not a claim that the generic Hunk container encodes a CPU. Distinct from the same author's separately tracked Ghidra loader.

ida-atari-st-gemdos-loader.title: IDA Atari ST GEMDOS loader
ida-atari-st-gemdos-loader.notes: IDA loader for Atari ST GEMDOS executables: maps TEXT/DATA/BSS, relocates data and imports global DRI/GST symbols, including extended names. README reports testing with IDA Pro 7.2 on macOS; other hosts are an upstream expectation rather than verified here.

discovery-inesldr.title: IDA iNES loader
discovery-inesldr.notes: iNES ROM loader credited to CaH4e3, updated to IDA 7 by Dr. MefistO. README describes mapper/bank limitations and reference relocation; no universal mapper support claim.

discovery-ida-refs-overrider.title: IDA references overrider
discovery-ida-refs-overrider.notes: IDA plug-in for overriding analysis references, with C++ plug-in and OverridesWindow source. Architecture-neutral analysis aid; no legacy CPU inferred from host language.

ida-stuff-retro-loaders-g0me3.title: ida_stuff
ida-stuff-retro-loaders-g0me3.display_title: ida_stuff — retro-console IDA loaders and analysis scripts
ida-stuff-retro-loaders-g0me3.notes: Multi-console IDA toolkit containing C++ loaders for iNES/FDS, Game Boy and Master System images, source and prebuilt loader binaries, CDL import/autorun scripts for NES, Game Boy, SNES and Genesis, and numerous title-specific analysis scripts. The source also includes 65816, m68000 and SH-4-oriented helpers. Visual Studio project files establish a source build path, but supported IDA/Windows versions were not documented.

idris-atari-st-reconstruction.title: Idris OS — partial Atari ST reconstruction
idris-atari-st-reconstruction.upstream_name: Idris OS — partial Atari ST reconstruction
idris-atari-st-reconstruction.display_title: Idris OS — partial Atari ST reconstruction
idris-atari-st-reconstruction.notes: Partial reconstructed Idris OS source tree: kernel holds original xidris/idrisk1a binaries and large .orig.s listings, plus C and assembly modules and a cross-toolchain GNUmakefile. Build and fidelity unverified.

idsk-cpc-disk-image-tool.title: iDSK
idsk-cpc-disk-image-tool.notes: CPCSDK command-line tool for adding, removing and listing files in Amstrad CPC DSK images. It manages AMSDOS headers and can render tokenized BASIC and DAMS source, making it directly useful for preservation and software archaeology.

iff2bpl-amiga-bitplane-converter.title: iff2bpl — Amiga bitplane converter
iff2bpl-amiga-bitplane-converter.notes: Two C command-line tools convert ILBM to interleaved/non-interleaved Amiga bitplanes or chunky data and raw bitplanes back to ILBM. README notes reverse direction currently uses a largely fixed palette.

iffshow-amiga-image-inspector.title: IFFshow — Amiga ILBM inspector
iffshow-amiga-image-inspector.notes: Python/PyGame viewer decodes Amiga ILBM including EHB, HAM6/8 and deep-color modes; also writes 24-bit and HAM IFF from modern images. Author notes PyGame can load IFF directly but this code implements decoding.

iffviewer-amiga-quicklook-ginnov.title: IFFViewer
iffviewer-amiga-quicklook-ginnov.display_title: IFFViewer — Amiga IFF Finder Quick Look extensions
iffviewer-amiga-quicklook-ginnov.notes: macOS Quick Look project containing separate IFFPreviewExtension parser and IFFThumbnailExtension C decoder. GINNOV Tools index identifies Finder previews. Its preview/thumbnail integration differs from the PixDeluxe image manager; exact IFF subformats and build requirements need review.

igor-objetivo-uikokahonia-interpreter-cy.title: Igor interpreter
source_language: Spanish CD release IGOR.EXE and IGOR.DAT
igor-objetivo-uikokahonia-interpreter-cy.notes: Proof-of-concept interpreter for Igor's Spanish CD release: README requires IGOR.DAT and IGOR.EXE, explains that hardcoded logic and assets reside in the original executable, and describes an x86 decoder/interpreter with rewritten palette, display and input traps. Missing original save/load screen is explicitly listed. Android and SDL front ends are present; no full-playability or binary-equality claim.

ik-plus-atari-st-reforged.title: IK+ Reforged
ik-plus-atari-st-reforged.display_title: IK+ — Atari ST compatibility and three-player patches

runtime_profiles.name: IK3J_PAR
runtime_profiles.notes: README documents STF, STE and Mega STE operation at 8 and 16 MHz and a parallel-port joystick adapter for player 3; STE and Mega STE were tested on real hardware.

runtime_profiles.name: IK3J_STE
runtime_profiles.notes: STE-only build with 1 MB or more, enhanced joystick port, DMA sound and blitter; README says it was tested on a real STE.

ik-plus-atari-st-reforged.notes: Builds a new loader, version-guarded patches, simultaneous third-player modes and JOYTEST around a user-supplied fixed IK+.PRG image. Version 7 extracts and patches that single-file program, skips its residual floppy check, produces checksum-verified PAR and STE folders, and was tested on real STE and Mega STE hardware. The repository does not distribute the game.

image-rider-stx.title: image-rider
image-rider-stx.display_title: image-rider — exploratory Atari ST STX parser
image-rider-stx.notes: Rust parser detects STX and its example can output track/sector image data. README explicitly says no listed image format is fully parsed and unknown input may fail; record limited to implemented exploratory extraction rather than complete STX decoding.

image2mode1-bbc-converter.title: image2mode1 — BBC raster palette converter
image2mode1-bbc-converter.notes: Python image optimization and conversion to MODE 1 binary plus BBC Master 6502 display engine with per-scanline palette swaps, Gradio preview and SSD export. The integrated raster-fx.asm serves this image conversion work; the author's separate raster-fx repository is a more general framework.

image2mode7-teletext-converter.title: image2mode7 — BBC Teletext image converter
image2mode7-teletext-converter.notes: Python optimization converts arbitrary images to 1000-byte BBC MODE 7 Teletext pages, with preview and DFS SSD export; older C++ binary also present. README credits Julian Brown's algorithm and explicitly says Claude co-wrote this implementation; do not attribute algorithm invention to this repository.

img2ans-cga-converter.title: img2ans — CGA ANSI art converter
img2ans-cga-converter.notes: Python image-to-ANSI converter using CP437 half-block characters and a 16-colour CGA palette for .ans art output. Development/asset tool for period PC text graphics, not a recovered game asset.

imogen-bbc-zornslemma.title: Imogen
imogen-bbc-zornslemma.notes: Large BBC Micro reconstruction using py8dis plus BeebAsm/ACME. The build script regenerates source for the loader, main game, auxiliary code and level/data components, reassembles them and compares reconstructed components against the original binaries.

imploder-hitchhikr.title: Imploder
imploder-hitchhikr.notes: Packs Amiga and X68000 executables or raw data using an implementation based on lab313ru reversed implode/explode routines; the 68000 decruncher was adapted from a Team17 game. Windows and Amiga executables are provided.

indy3-st-copy-protection.title: Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade ST protection
indy3-st-copy-protection.upstream_name: Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade ST protection
indy3-st-copy-protection.display_title: Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade ST protection
subjects: Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade
indy3-st-copy-protection.notes: Analyzes the Atari ST Kixx release SCUMM room-92 printed Translation Table check from three floppy dumps, reconstructing its coordinate-to-symbol computation and supplying annotated disassembly, card generator and optional patcher. No game reconstruction is claimed.

indy-heat-amiga-horace.title: Indy Heat — Amiga reverse engineering and track editor
indy-heat-amiga-horace.display_title: Indy Heat — Amiga reverse engineering and track editor
indy-heat-amiga-horace.notes: Active reverse engineering of Indy Heat's Amiga track/race structures and runtime behaviour, with browser-based editing/visualisation tooling and WHDLoad integration. Current work covers track resources, waypoints/AI, race presentation, graphics and custom-track workflows.

infernal-runner-cpc-js.title: infernal_js
infernal-runner-cpc-js.display_title: Infernal Runner — CPC binary/bytecode study and JS port
source_language: CPC disk image and Z80 machine code
infernal-runner-cpc-js.notes: JavaScript reimplementation derived from CPC DSK and Z80 analysis; documents the original cooperative bytecode VM and includes disasm.c, bytecode listings and assembly. Do not infer byte-exact source.

infiltrator-conversion-tools.title: Infiltrator conversion utilities
infiltrator-conversion-tools.display_title: Infiltrator conversion tools — C64 disassembly/asset export
infiltrator-conversion-tools.notes: Python tools convert Infiltrator’s disassembly text, sprites and character-set binaries into KickAssembler and CBM PRG Studio source, with labelled example output. This is an export bridge for C64 binary analysis, not a stand-alone Infiltrator game reconstruction.

infinite-dreams-amiga-disassembly.title: Infinite Dreams — Lunatics UK Amiga demo
infinite-dreams-amiga-disassembly.upstream_name: Infinite Dreams — Lunatics UK Amiga demo
infinite-dreams-amiga-disassembly.display_title: Infinite Dreams — Lunatics UK Amiga demo
subjects: Infinite Dreams — Lunatics UK Amiga demo
infinite-dreams-amiga-disassembly.notes: The original author recovered his lost 1992 demo source by disassembling the disks. Primary README documents a reassembled runnable original version plus a later single-disk adaptation with a new loader and compression; original recovered source and modified edition are distinct.

inspeccytor-spectrum-disassembler.title: inSpeccytor — Spectrum memory disassembly tool
inspeccytor-spectrum-disassembler.notes: macOS Swift/Xcode memory dump disassembler with Z80 decoder, CPU model, formats and UI code; sparse README, implementation verified by source inventory rather than inferred from project name alone.

integer-basic-apple2-santa-maria.title: Integer BASIC
integer-basic-apple2-santa-maria.display_title: Integer BASIC — Apple II ROM disassembly
integer-basic-apple2-santa-maria.notes: Paul R. Santa-Maria’s independently authored Integer BASIC disassembly, ported by Andy McFadden into a SourceGen project with a few further labels. The binary comes from the DOS 3.3 system master; the project page distinguishes this earlier disassembly from Wozniak’s handwritten original source and notes additional red-book-based documentation by Sean Gugler. This record represents the underlying disassembly, not a second independent SourceGen reconstruction.

into-the-eagles-nest.title: Into the Eagle's Nest
into-the-eagles-nest.notes: Complete Amiga disassembly, debugged and reassemblable to a working game according to the upstream README and source. A prior duplicate catalogue entry incorrectly attributed an Atari ST reconstruction to this Amiga-only repository; its README, assembly header and tree document only Amiga work.

into-eagles-nest-cpc.title: Into the Eagle's Nest — CPC analysis
into-eagles-nest-cpc.display_title: Into the Eagle's Nest — CPC analysis
into-eagles-nest-cpc.notes: Amstrad CPC disassembly/analysis project investigating game logic such as enemy respawn and comparing CPC map structures with the Amiga version.

ipf-flux-native-decoder.title: ipf-flux
ipf-flux-native-decoder.display_title: IPF flux — native Amiga/Atari preservation decoder
ipf-flux-native-decoder.notes: Pure Rust CAPS/IPF track decoder, independently compared with libcapsimage across a stated 5,569-image corpus. Decodes magnetic cells, timing, write splice and weak spans; no KryoFlux stream or multi-revolution support. IPF encompasses Amiga and Atari ST, but the README does not claim native ST filesystem decoding.

ira-amiga-reassembler.title: IRA — Amiga 68k reassembler
ira-amiga-reassembler.notes: Portable Amiga Hunk and raw 68k disassembler/reassembler by Tim Ruehsen, Christian Wasner, Ilkka Lehtoranta and Frank Wille. Aminet lists version 2.11 dated February 2025. Maintainer documentation provides GNU, Windows, macOS, AmigaOS and MorphOS builds and an AmigaBASIC workflow that diff-verifies regenerated assembly. The CPU choices describe decoded code, not a machine minimum or native output architecture.

iridis-alpha-c64.title: Iridis Alpha
iridis-alpha-c64.notes: Reverse-engineered and commented source; builds to a C64 PRG and has playable Windows/web variants.

jack-nipper-ii-spectrum-analyser.title: Jack the Nipper II
jack-nipper-ii-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Jack the Nipper II — ZX Spectrum analyser project
jack-nipper-ii-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Jack the Nipper II directory contains a 2498 KiB Analysis.json annotation database and exported Z80 assembly, map/viewer scripts and decoded graphics/map assets. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

jackal-nes-rayofjay.title: Jackal
jackal-nes-rayofjay.notes: Full commented NES Jackal disassembly. The README states all code is completely disassembled and that ASM6n builds the source to the original Jackal ROM when the original graphical data is supplied.

jagfx-atari-jaguar-graphics-tool.title: jagfx
jagfx-atari-jaguar-graphics-tool.display_title: jagfx — Atari Jaguar graphics extractor and ROM searcher
source_language: Atari Jaguar ROM graphics and compressed data
jagfx-atari-jaguar-graphics-tool.notes: General Atari Jaguar ROM graphics workbench. It decodes Jaguar pixel formats, searches headerless ROM regions for image stride patterns, locates palettes, identifies parameterized compression codecs, sweeps packed streams and exports assets without hard-coding a game.

cubanismo-jaguar-sdk.title: jaguar-sdk
cubanismo-jaguar-sdk.display_title: Jaguar SDK — restored Atari development toolchain
source_language: historical Atari Jaguar SDK sources and binary tools
cubanismo-jaguar-sdk.notes: Modernized, buildable restoration of the released Atari Jaguar development tools. jetpac-vic20-phillipeaton.title: JETPAC — VIC-20 annotated disassembly
types: Annotated game disassembly and reassembly project
jetpac-vic20-phillipeaton.status: Annotated VIC-20 disassembly with a documented Windows reassembly pipeline; output is raw binary, not a directly loadable PRG.
jetpac-vic20-phillipeaton.notes: Annotated 6502 listing includes native VIC/VIA setup, mapped variables and game routines. Hand-authored dasmfw info files drive code/data separation; the Makefile sequences dasmfw, sed and as65, then emits both MD5 sums. Author describes roughly 18 months of analysis and completion of labels, variables and code comments. JETPAC requires an 8 KiB memory expansion. That expansion is not recorded as total RAM. The underlying Spectrum heritage does not make this a Spectrum-output reconstruction. Independent VIC-20 analysis by Phillip Eaton; not a fork or duplicate of existing Spectrum/Electron entries. No repository-wide license or original-game redistribution permission was established in this review. Reviewed 2026-10-05 by primary documentation, source, build-file and tree inspection. All local build, test, emulation and runtime checks remain unperformed. Positive flags are evidence-scoped upstream reports only; byte_exact remains unknown. Last activity is the latest default-branch commit date, not repository creation or pushed_at. Evidence: https://github.com/phillipeaton/JETPAC_VIC-20_disassembly/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/phillipeaton/JETPAC_VIC-20_disassembly/blob/main/dasmfw/jetpac.asm https://github.com/phillipeaton/JETPAC_VIC-20_disassembly/blob/main/dasmfw/README.md https://github.com/phillipeaton/JETPAC_VIC-20_disassembly/blob/main/makefile https://github.com/phillipeaton/JETPAC_VIC-20_disassembly/blob/main/bin/README.md https://github.com/phillipeaton/JETPAC_VIC-20_disassembly/commit/84a3af415778f76f23610afd815f8f2d148b3d38

types: native platform port of reverse-engineered speech software
megasam-mega65-speech-port.status: Author-reported interactive MEGA65 speech port; local assembly and hardware/audio behavior unverified.
megasam-mega65-speech-port.notes: Native MEGA65 port of Mark Barton’s SAM/RECITER, based on DLehenbauer’s documented C64 disassembly. Relocates the synthesis/reciter code and replaces SID-volume output with streamed audio DMA. An RE-derived application/system-software port. It is neither a game nor a generic C64 emulator, and the related s-macke/SAM desktop C port is a separate implementation/target. README explicitly describes the working SAY> prompt, speech and BYE loop and supplies MEGA65 LOAD/RUN and banked BASIC-driver instructions; runnable=true is limited to that author-reported functionality. build.bat invokes bundled 64tass/c1541 and creates sam.d81; run.bat hard-codes a local Xemu path. Compilation and audio were not tested here. Relocation and output changes mean this is not an original C64 byte-identity exercise; byte_exact remains null. This is a native MEGA65 port of SAM, not a game or byte-identical C64 reconstruction. It retains the synthesis algorithm while relocating code and replacing SID output with audio DMA. Build uses Windows tools included in the repository; run.bat assumes a local Xemu path. Hardware/audio behavior was not tested. Credits identify SAM, DLehenbauer’s disassembly and the C reference authors. No root license file was found in this port; included original-derived code and bundled build executables should not be treated as newly licensed wholesale. README cites Commodore64128/c64-sam, whose GitHub metadata identifies fork parent DLehenbauer/c64-sam. Existing s-macke/SAM is a different C desktop port; megasam adds an independent MEGA65-native implementation/target and is not an unchanged mirror. BASIC-source/build update explicitly credits Claude Opus 5 (1M context). The evidence is an explicit commit credit; it does not quantify AI contribution across the project. Reviewed on 2026-10-05; no independent build, execution or byte comparison was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/xlar54/megasam/blob/master/README.md https://github.com/xlar54/megasam/blob/master/src/sam%20reciter.asm https://github.com/xlar54/megasam/blob/master/src/stream.inc https://github.com/xlar54/megasam/blob/master/src/sam_core.inc https://github.com/xlar54/megasam/blob/master/src/reciter_core.inc https://github.com/xlar54/megasam/blob/master/build.bat Latest upstream commit: https://github.com/xlar54/megasam/commit/8d0f45dc8be7f36682c8877a7ad15df5981477b9

Original utility-ROM integration incorporating ported and disassembly-derived loaders. The RE-derived-port classification is limited to those loader components, including documented JiffyDOS 1541 disassembly, rather than claiming Parobek itself reconstructs a historical ROM. C64 in source_platforms denotes loader lineage only. README documents ROM startup, directory-browser operation and a load-performance matrix; runnable=true is limited to author-reported utility operation, not every hardware mode. src/Makefile builds VIA/CPLD variants with ACME; source disables CIA BurstCart/CIA parallel support despite broader historical README descriptions. The db12b.prg directory browser is embedded. No compilation, emulator matrix or hardware test was performed here; byte_exact stays null. Hardware-dependent fastload modes require the appropriate drives, adapters and ROMs. Source explicitly disables CIA BurstCart/CIA parallel support even though README contains broader historical descriptions. An embedded directory browser is supplied as db12b.prg. No build, emulator matrix or hardware verification was run. No root license file was found. Source credits SJL264, SpeedDOS, HypaLoad, Pasi Ojala and JiffyDOS analysis; an embedded directory-browser binary and reference disassemblies retain separate provenance. Own utility integration, not an unchanged copy of those reference loaders; relation to The Servant is a name pun according to README. No root/subject match in current catalogue. Directory-browser integration commit explicitly credits Cursor. The evidence is an explicit commit credit; it does not quantify AI contribution across the project. Reviewed on 2026-10-05; no independent build, execution or byte comparison was performed. runtime_profiles.notes: README requires Python 3.5+, PyQt5 and Qt.py; no minimum CPU or RAM is stated.

peasauce-disassembler-rmtew.notes: Interactive Python/Qt disassembler for Amiga, Atari ST and X68000 68k executables. It exports assembler source but no fixed-CPU executable, so target CPU is not applicable.

jotd-pengo-amiga.title: Pengo — Amiga arcade transcode
jotd-pengo-amiga.notes: Original Pengo Z80 arcade game transcoded to 68k assembly. Primary documentation records fully playable Amiga output and tested/playable MVS and Neo Geo CDZ output in MAME; both checked-in build routes explicitly target m68000. No minimum hardware requirement is stated.

penny-arcade-apple2-6502disassembly.title: Penny Arcade
penny-arcade-apple2-6502disassembly.display_title: Penny Arcade — Apple II mixed BASIC/assembly disassembly
penny-arcade-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Disassembly of Bill Budge's 1979 Apple II Penny Arcade, whose Applesoft BASIC and assembly routines were embedded in a single cassette program. The project publishes listings for both portions, SourceGen files/binaries and analysis of the title animation, collision handling and BASIC/code embedding.

pentagram-tcdev-spectrum.title: Pentagram — tcdev
pentagram-tcdev-spectrum.notes: Adjacent tcdev discovery: Pentagram reverse engineering, explicitly marked WIP.

percy-potty-pigeon-spectrum.title: Percy the Potty Pigeon
percy-potty-pigeon-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

pet-frogger-original-source.title: PET Frogger — recovered original source
pet-frogger-original-source.notes: John C. Dale's 6502 Frogger game source from his school days, presented with Frogger.asm, project file and built PRG; README attributes the original game to 1983. Period original source rediscovered by its author; no claim of reverse-engineered or byte-matched source.

pfx-unpacker-atari-st.title: PFX Unpacker — Atari ST executables
pfx-unpacker-atari-st.notes: Python CLI/optional GUI extracts standard runnable TOS executables from PFX 1.13P and 2.1P packed files, translating XPFX.S decompression logic. It explicitly does not support ICE, Synergy, UPX or generic LHA archives.

phantom-fighter-original-source-recreati.title: Phantom Fighter
phantom-fighter-original-source-recreati.display_title: Phantom Fighter — Amiga source archive and modern recreation
phantom-fighter-original-source-recreati.notes: Billy Newport's own recovered 1988 Amiga source and assets, PAL/NTSC variants, plus Python/Pygame and browser recreations. Original Lattice C/assembly uses KOS boot/disk support. README explicitly attributes the Python version to Claude; current JavaScript also has a Claude co-author commit. Modern paths directly implement entities, collision, scrolling and rendering, with no guest-CPU execution found. The modern DESIGN.md claims 68010 tuning, conflicting with the author's README account of 68000 development and 68010 incompatibility; no runtime minimum is asserted. Source/archive build reproducibility and modern playability are not locally verified.

phantomas20-cpc.title: Phantomas 2.0 CPC

runtime_profiles.name: Creator-documented CPC release
runtime_profiles.notes: README explicitly requires at least 64 KB; no CPU minimum inferred.

phantomas20-cpc.notes: Author-published 2018 CPC remake of the Dinamic game, with substantial native assembly, room data, audio and public English/Spanish CDT plus DSK releases. No binary-derived reconstruction or byte-equivalence claim is made. Creator README documents gameplay, compatible emulators and real CPC loading; release 1.0.0 publishes two CDT images and a DSK. Source not independently assembled.

phantoms-five-apple2-6502disassembly.title: Phantoms Five
phantoms-five-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Apple II Phantoms Five disassembly covering the game and title sequence. The project provides SourceGen files/binaries and documents reconstruction of a suitable analysis binary from the cracked disk's custom loader layout.

pharaohs-curse-atari8-sarnau.title: Pharaoh's Curse
pharaohs-curse-atari8-sarnau.display_title: Pharaoh's Curse — Atari 8-bit disassembly & protection analysis
pharaohs-curse-atari8-sarnau.notes: Documented Atari 400/800 source reconstruction from protected ATX media. The project reverse engineers duplicate-sector/timing and CRC-error protection, extracts the loaded program and rebuilds it with ca65; the README states the generated object.prg should be binary identical to the extracted program.

phc25-sanyo-emulator-hitchhikr.title: PHC-25
phc25-sanyo-emulator-hitchhikr.notes: Windows PHC-25 emulator with source and a Windows executable. README credits Keiichi Tago's original emulator and calls this an improved, translated version; record the derivative software separately, without claiming original PHC firmware analysis or independent emulation tests.

pheenix-spectrum.title: Pheenix
pheenix-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

miami-chase-trainer-reconstruction.title: Phil Douglas Miami Chase trainer
miami-chase-trainer-reconstruction.display_title: Miami Chase — Amiga trainer menu reconstruction
subjects: Phil Douglas Miami Chase trainer menu
miami-chase-trainer-reconstruction.notes: Reconstructed source for Phil Douglas's Miami Chase trainer menu with a vasm build command and annotated resident code. The archive provides no specific original-binary comparison or runtime test for this file.

jotd-phoenix-amiga.title: Phoenix — Amiga arcade transcode

runtime_profiles.name: OCS/ECS build
runtime_profiles.notes: The non-AGA executable is assembled with -m68000; the project README identifies the non-AGA family as ECS without a numeric RAM floor.

runtime_profiles.name: AGA build
runtime_profiles.notes: The AGA executable is assembled with -m68020 and its WHDLoad slave explicitly requests both 68020 and AGA.

jotd-phoenix-amiga.notes: ECS/AGA Phoenix remake using reverse engineering and transcode work; README notes that the original code was transcoded while documenting a remaining behavioural discrepancy. Checked-in builds distinguish an m68000 non-AGA executable and an m68020/AGA executable.

phoenixbasic-gfa-basic-atari-st.title: PhoenixBasic — GFA BASIC 3.5 compatible interpreter
phoenixbasic-gfa-basic-atari-st.status: Partial TOS/AES coverage documented; Atari ST and host builds described.
phoenixbasic-gfa-basic-atari-st.notes: C89 compatibility interpreter for GFA BASIC 3.5 programs, with lexer/bytecode VM, selected GEMDOS/BIOS/XBIOS calls and console framebuffer. Repository documents a host build plus m68k Atari ST PRG build and test scripts. This is a modern language reimplementation, not execution of an original GFA BASIC binary.

phr-crew-sin-intro-amiga.title: PHR-Crew The Sin Intro
phr-crew-sin-intro-amiga.notes: ReSource disassembly and modernization of PHR-Crew The Sin Intro with extracted assets and 68000 assembly. No explicit build verification or binary identity claim.

pist-atari-st-ide.title: PiST
pist-atari-st-ide.display_title: PiST — Atari ST assembly IDE & debugger
pist-atari-st-ide.notes: Cross-platform Atari ST/STE 68000 assembly IDE integrating vasm/vlink with Hatari. Provides source-to-PC line mapping, breakpoints/stepping, registers, memory and labelled disassembly, hardware-register inspection, profiling, disk-image handling, sprite/bitplane tooling and an MCP/remote-control surface. Tracked as adjacent software-archaeology and reproducible retro-development infrastructure.

pitfall-ii-c64.title: Pitfall II
pitfall-ii-c64.notes: Historical reverse-engineering write-up covering sprites, memory layout, maps, interrupts and engine structures.

albank1-pitfall-c64-disassembly.title: Pitfall!
albank1-pitfall-c64-disassembly.display_title: Pitfall! — C64 cartridge disassembly case study
albank1-pitfall-c64-disassembly.notes: C64 Pitfall! cartridge listing with a worked JC64dis-to-DASM-to-cartconv process and byte-difference checks for fixing size/alignment. Contains an infinite-lives variant; independent from the existing Pitfall II record. Author used ChatGPT for learning, but says it was insufficient for the disassembly itself.

pixdeluxe-amiga-iff-manager-ginnov.title: PixDeluxe
pixdeluxe-amiga-iff-manager-ginnov.notes: macOS IFF viewer, image manager and PNG converter. Its own README credits svanderburg/libiff; inspected source contains IFFParser.swift and a bundled libilbm/miniiff bridge. Standalone management/conversion is separate from sibling IFFViewer's Finder Quick Look extensions.

plan-b-bbc-tobylobster.title: Plan B BBC disassembly
plan-b-bbc-tobylobster.notes: BBC Plan B 6502 disassembly. go_acme generates source with py8dis, assembles with ACME, compares it byte-for-byte with the original and builds a runnable SSD.

planetoid-bbc-mikroman.title: Planetoid
planetoid-bbc-mikroman.display_title: Planetoid — BBC Micro partial reverse engineering
planetoid-bbc-mikroman.notes: Partial BBC Micro Planetoid reverse-engineering/reconstruction project used to study the machine. The README identifies Planet2.asm as the main file, documents BeebAsm/Kick Assembler builds, notes corrections to an earlier reverse engineer's labels/constants and links the related r41n60w planetoid-disasm work.

planetoid-bbc-r41n60w.title: Planetoid BBC disassembly
planetoid-bbc-r41n60w.notes: Annotated Planetoid 6502 listing. No README, assembler pipeline or runnable binary is present, so target CPU and runtime are not applicable to this analysis-only repository.

platoon-native-swift-macos.title: Platoon for macOS
platoon-native-swift-macos.display_title: Platoon — native Swift reconstruction for macOS

runtime_profiles.name: Universal macOS app
runtime_profiles.notes: Apple Silicon and Intel builds; no minimum RAM specified. Xcode 16 is a build-time requirement.

execution_paths.name: Native Swift macOS application
execution_paths.notes: Swift package links PlatoonCore into native app; original routines translated to Swift, reference emulator stays under tools.

platoon-native-swift-macos.notes: Original Amiga 68000 routines translated to native Swift, retaining data layout and custom-chip behavior through reconstructed blitter/copper/Paula support. Reference Musashi/vAmiga executables are validation tools, not the app's game-CPU path. README reports full-section deterministic playthrough/regression comparisons; these are not original-platform binary matching. User supplies disk data. No local build/play test.

png2amiga-multiplatform-asset-converter.title: png2amiga

runtime_profiles.name: Standard x86-64 release build
runtime_profiles.notes: The README explicitly requires AVX2 for the standard x86-64 binaries and gives Intel Haswell (2013+) / AMD Zen (2017+) as examples. A compatibility build is available for older x86-64 CPUs, but no more specific lower CPU floor is asserted.

evidence.excerpt: The x86-64 binaries need AVX2 (Intel Haswell 2013+, AMD Zen 2017+). On an older CPU, use png2amiga-windows-x86_64-compat.exe from the same release.

png2amiga-multiplatform-asset-converter.notes: Cross-platform image/asset converter for Amiga, Atari ST/STE, IBM PC, C64, Genesis, SNES Mode 7, Game Boy Advance, Sega Master System/Game Gear, Amstrad CPC/CPC Plus, Thomson and Commodore TED targets. v1.109.0 (25 September 2026) added SMS/GG and CPC/CPC Plus output modes with packed-output round-trip tests. The README documents native CMake builds, a WebAssembly web app and pre-built desktop releases; standard x86-64 binaries require AVX2, while a compatibility build is provided for older x86-64 CPUs.

jotd-pooyan-amiga.title: Pooyan — Amiga arcade transcode

runtime_profiles.name: OCS/ECS/AGA PAL build
runtime_profiles.notes: The README explicitly documents a 60 Hz / 50 fps PAL build for OCS, ECS and AGA Amigas; the primary game objects are assembled for m68000. No RAM floor is stated.

jotd-pooyan-amiga.notes: Pooyan arcade port for Amiga; README credits reverse engineering, 68000 transcode and graphics/sound conversion and documents OCS/ECS/AGA PAL support. The primary game output is m68000.

populous-beginning-resource-editor.title: PopResourceEditor — Populous: The Beginning asset editor
populous-beginning-resource-editor.display_title: PopResourceEditor — Populous: The Beginning asset editor
populous-beginning-resource-editor.status: Upstream documents Windows asset-editor functionality and Visual Studio build requirements.
populous-beginning-resource-editor.notes: Game-specific asset manager/editor for palettes, indexed sprites, landscape textures, skies and v2 map previews. Alpha.cpp and other modules process asset data directly. It is supporting tooling, not a playable engine or historical development-tool reconstruction. VS2022/v143, C++20 and Windows SDK are required; bundled precompiled dependencies may need replacement for custom builds. Reviewed 2026-10-05. Build/run/play statements are upstream reports; no candidate code was compiled or executed in this review. Evidence: https://github.com/Toksisitee/PopResourceEditor/blob/master/README.md https://github.com/Toksisitee/PopResourceEditor/blob/master/Alpha.cpp https://github.com/Toksisitee/PopResourceEditor/blob/master/PopResourceEditor.vcxproj

vs-sr-cd32-powerdrive.title: Power Drive — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-powerdrive.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Power Drive. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

powerpacker-decompiled-lab313ru.title: PowerPacker 36.10 — decompiled compressor
powerpacker-decompiled-lab313ru.notes: Dr. MefistO states that the original PowerPacker library and compression algorithm, including password/encryption handling, were decompiled into a usable compressor/decompressor. The repository includes a Visual Studio project and test script; no Amiga-native rebuilt binary or byte-identity proof is established.

prehistorik-amiga-demo-browser-rewrite.title: Prehistorik Amiga demo — browser rewrite
prehistorik-amiga-demo-browser-rewrite.notes: Rewrites only the first-level playable Amiga Prehistorik demo from its ADF; the author README links a browser version. The reviewed README and complete source/tool tree do not identify the original executable CPU, so none is inferred from the Amiga/ADF label. This is not a full-game reconstruction or a DOS data port.

vs-sr-cd32-prey.title: Prey: An Alien Encounter — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-prey.display_title: Prey: An Alien Encounter — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-prey.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Prey: An Alien Encounter. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

prince-dastan-sokoban-within-amstrad-cpc.title: Prince Dastan: Sokoban Within — 64 KB Amstrad CPC puzzle game
prince-dastan-sokoban-within-amstrad-cpc.display_title: Prince Dastan: Sokoban Within — 64 KB Amstrad CPC puzzle game

runtime_profiles.name: Prince Dastan 64 KB CPC output
runtime_profiles.notes: README explicitly says the game uses 64 KB and runs on all Amstrad CPC computers. No further CPU revision, RAM expansion or chipset requirement is stated.

prince-dastan-sokoban-within-amstrad-cpc.status: Author-reported runnable on 64 KB Amstrad CPC; source build and complete playability unverified.
prince-dastan-sokoban-within-amstrad-cpc.notes: Euphoria Design’s original CPC RetroDev 2020 puzzle game credits Romain Giot, Gilles Rimauro and Dimitris Fragkos, with levels by Aymeric du Peloux and Hirohiko Nakamiya. Z80 model/controller/view source and RASM asset/build rules generate native disk, tape and snapshot variants. README says it uses 64 KB and runs on all Amstrad CPC computers. Original Sokoban-style puzzle title with a Prince Dastan theme. It is not source recovery of Prince of Persia; named level designers and borrowed tooling retain their separate credit. README explicitly states CPC operation using 64 KB, supporting author-reported runnable=true. The RASM pipeline uses bundled/older tools and Wine for an asset utility; no clean compilation or play-through was performed. Reviewed on 2026-10-05; no independent build or execution was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/rgiot/prince_dastan_sokoban_within/blob/main/README.txt https://github.com/rgiot/prince_dastan_sokoban_within/blob/main/sources/Makefile https://github.com/rgiot/prince_dastan_sokoban_within/blob/main/sources/src/sokoban.asm https://github.com/rgiot/prince_dastan_sokoban_within/blob/main/sources/src/controler.asm. Latest upstream commit: https://github.com/rgiot/prince_dastan_sokoban_within/commit/eed70bf813717fc24687204294e61fadba732fec

probos2000-c64-spectrum-port.title: probos2000
probos2000-c64-spectrum-port.display_title: PROBOS 2000 — C64 binary analysis to Spectrum 48K
subjects: 1991, USSR: Deep Space Probe Control Centre Janitor
source_language: 2020 C64 PROBOS PRG and extracted machine code
probos2000-c64-spectrum-port.notes: Original PRG self-extractor executed with Py65; recovered C64 code, graphics and timing informed a native Z80 Spectrum 48K TAP. RE notes explicitly reject cycle-perfect equality and document changed display and controls.

probos2000-spectrum-web-port.title: probos2000
probos2000-spectrum-web-port.display_title: PROBOS 2000 — native Web continuation of Spectrum port
subjects: 1991, USSR: Deep Space Probe Control Centre Janitor
source_language: Spectrum PROBOS 2000 port source and extracted artwork
probos2000-spectrum-web-port.notes: Separate JavaScript/canvas reimplementation of this repository’s native Spectrum port. README explicitly says there is no Z80 emulator or embedded binary and explains timing differences; do not equate it with a C64 direct port.

prog8-retro-compiler.title: prog8
prog8-retro-compiler.notes: Structured low-level language/compiler for 6502-family computers and 68000, with experimental Amiga 500/1200 targets; README says the m68k targets are not yet production-ready.

programmers-aid-apple2-james-davis.title: Programmer's Aid #1
programmers-aid-apple2-james-davis.display_title: Programmer's Aid #1 — Apple II ROM disassembly
programmers-aid-apple2-james-davis.notes: James P. Davis annotated the Programmer’s Aid #1 ROM as separate listings covering high-resolution graphics, program renumbering and append, relocation, tape verification, RAM test and music. The pages identify Davis’s SourceGen analysis and link the original Apple manual as background. SourceGen project file and binaries are linked from the ROM index.

project-eon-yeager.title: Project Eon
project-eon-yeager.notes: Cross-platform reimplementation with separate Original and opt-in Modern modes. Verified release packaging covers Linux/Windows x86-64 plus macOS and iPadOS arm64. Millennium DOS remains bounded to recovered driver transactions rather than gameplay. Deuteros' recovered Amiga path now supplies title and bootstrap surfaces to the Modern renderer, and the typed $217e4 CIA observation plus $217f2/$21926 return continuation are implemented; capture parity, complete opening flow and gameplay remain unverified.

propulse-amiga-protracker-module-editor.title: Propulse Tracker
propulse-amiga-protracker-module-editor.display_title: Propulse — Amiga MOD editor and playback engine
source_language: Amiga ProTracker MOD and related modules
propulse-amiga-protracker-module-editor.notes: Cross-platform MOD-compatible tracker with editor, sample tools, WAV export and imports for P61A, IT and S3M. README credits 8bitbubsy's playback engine as a predecessor based on a disassembly of Amiga ProTracker. It is a different editor and format tool, not the original ProTracker source.

proto-arc-archimedes-prototypes.title: proto-arc — Archimedes prototype framework
proto-arc-archimedes-prototypes.notes: ARM prototype harness with triple-buffer mode setup, QTM music, frame synchronization and debugger switches inspected in proto-arc.asm. Source describes this as stripped back from the author's stniccc-archie framework; no separate application claimed.

psgplay-atari-st-sndh-tools.title: psgplay
psgplay-atari-st-sndh-tools.display_title: PSG play — Atari ST SNDH player and reassembler
source_language: SNDH music binaries and YM2149/68000 behavior
psgplay-atari-st-sndh-tools.notes: SNDH/PSG player with 68000 emulation, tracing and reachability-guided SNDH disassembly; output can be edited and reassembled to alter metadata or code.

pssst-spectrum.title: Pssst
pssst-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

discovery-psx-loader.title: PSX loader for IDA
discovery-psx-loader.notes: Python PSX executable loader for IDA plus PsyQ data and signature applier. Separate analyzer integration from Ghidra loader.

psychedelia-colourspace-reconstruction.title: Psychedelia / Colourspace
psychedelia-colourspace-reconstruction.notes: Reverse-engineered and commented source collection for Jeff Minter's early light synthesizers: Psychedelia on C64/VIC-20/C16 and Colourspace on Atari 8-bit, with buildable versions for the documented platforms.

protracker-23f-amiga-reconstruction.title: pt23f
protracker-23f-amiga-reconstruction.notes: Amiga ProTracker 2 continuation based on re-sourcing/disassembly of ProTracker 2.3D; source modifies playback and sample handling, with downloadable executable and bootable ADF.

ptvpack-hitchhikr.title: PtvPack

runtime_profiles.name: Apollo Vampire replay
runtime_profiles.notes: README targets Apollo Vampire and makefile.am compiles for m68020. Source enables Vampire extensions; no generic CPU/RAM floor is claimed.

ptvpack-hitchhikr.notes: MOD packer and replay routine for Apollo Vampire. The Amiga build explicitly selects m68020 while replay source enables Vampire extensions; this is not a compatibility claim for every 68020 Amiga.

puae-libretro-amiga-core.title: PUAE
puae-libretro-amiga-core.notes: README identifies WinUAE 5.3.1 commit 51b7be3 as base. Inspected libretro/ contains dedicated core, disk-control and input implementations, virtual keyboard and model presets; distinct libretro integration, with upstream WinUAE credited.

puae-debugger-vscode.title: PUAE Debugger
puae-debugger-vscode.display_title: PUAE Debugger — Amiga source debugger & profiler
puae-debugger-vscode.notes: Amiga debugger/profiler built around the WinUAE-derived PUAE core. Supports Hunk/ELF debug information, source and instruction breakpoints, data watchpoints, reverse execution, CPU/DMA profiling, Copper/blitter inspection, memory reconstruction, standalone DAP use and headless MCP-driven emulator inspection.

pure-c-help-atari-st-source-reconstructi.title: Pure C/Pascal help tools — Atari ST reconstruction
pure-c-help-atari-st-source-reconstructi.upstream_name: Pure C/Pascal help tools — Atari ST reconstruction
pure-c-help-atari-st-source-reconstructi.display_title: Pure C/Pascal help tools — Atari ST reconstruction
source_language: Pure C/Pascal help compiler and viewer executables
pure-c-help-atari-st-source-reconstructi.notes: Compiler and viewer sources reconstructed from Pure C and Pure Pascal executables. An orig branch can compile to almost identical originals; master improves functionality. The decompiler is mostly based on a contemporary published article and should not be presented as binary-derived.

pushover-dos-browser.title: Pushover
source_language: Pushover DOS executable and game data
pushover-dos-browser.notes: Playable browser reimplementation based on the DOS executable and user-provided DOS assets, using static and live DOSBox tracing. Historical Amiga/ST releases are mentioned but their media are not analyzed or accepted; original data omission is normal bring-your-own-data design.

py8dis-zornslemma.title: py8dis
py8dis-zornslemma.notes: Programmable Python static-tracing disassembler supporting 6502, 65C02 and 8080 binaries. It handles runtime relocation, user-defined labels/data structures and optional input MD5 verification, and emits source for assemblers including beebasm, ACME, xa and z88dk-z80asm. It underpins several BBC Micro reconstruction projects discovered in the same graph.

c64-esshahn-pydisass6502.title: pyDisass6502
c64-esshahn-pydisass6502.notes: Python 6502/C64 PRG disassembler with opcode tables, optional user-specified code/data entry points and C64 hardware-map comments. README says early but functional, and documents command-line input/output and Fairlight example.

pygenerate-bbc-disk-reassembly.title: pygenerate BBC disk disassembly scaffold
pygenerate-bbc-disk-reassembly.notes: Python generator makes a rebuildable BBC SSD project with control scripts, original files, assembly and build harness; uses py8dis with BeebAsm or ACME.

pyjamarama-electron-port.title: pyjamarama
pyjamarama-electron-port.display_title: Pyjamarama — ZX Spectrum to Acorn Electron port
pyjamarama-electron-port.notes: 2026 Acorn Electron 48K fan conversion of the ZX Spectrum game, distributed as playable UEF/SSD images; no port source is published here.

pyramid-warp-msx-enhanced-disassembly.title: Pyramid Warp
pyramid-warp-msx-enhanced-disassembly.display_title: Pyramid Warp — MSX disassembly and enhanced ROMs

runtime_profiles.name: Enhanced ROM
runtime_profiles.notes: The README states the enhanced variant moves RAM start to $E000 and requires 8 KB; this is not a requirement for the original ROM.

evidence.excerpt: Moved RAM start from $C000 to $E000 (RAM requirement is now 8KB)

pyramid-warp-msx-enhanced-disassembly.notes: Annotated 1983 T&E SOFT ROM assembles to the original verbatim. Enhanced and Enhanced+ variants change graphics, sound, rooms and difficulty; their outputs should not be described as byte-identical to the original. README states the enhanced RAM start is $E000 and its RAM requirement is 8 KB, but does not establish the original ROM's minimum.

pad-amiga-disassembler.title: Pyrdacor Amiga Disassembler (pad)
pad-amiga-disassembler.notes: Early-stage tool intended to translate compiled Amiga executables back into recompilable 68k assembly. README explicitly describes the desired output as a goal, not an achieved byte-identical reconstruction.

quake-ii-q2tools-220.title: q2tools-220 — Quake II Valve-220 map compiler tools
quake-ii-q2tools-220.display_title: q2tools-220 — Quake II Valve-220 map compiler tools
quake-ii-q2tools-220.status: Documented BSP/VIS/RAD and asset-compilation tooling with development builds.
quake-ii-q2tools-220.notes: Modern Quake II level compiler descended from XaeroX/DarkEssence Valve-220 tools distributed with J.A.C.K. Combines BSP, VIS and RAD passes and format/lighting enhancements. Some extended limits and features require a compatible engine; it is not a game reimplementation. README links Linux/Windows/macOS development builds and gives CMake instructions. Reviewed 2026-10-05. Build/run/play statements are upstream reports; no candidate code was compiled or executed in this review. Evidence: https://github.com/qbism/q2tools-220/blob/master/README.md https://github.com/qbism/q2tools-220/blob/master/src/bsp.c https://github.com/qbism/q2tools-220/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt

albank1-qbasic-editor-interpreter-python.title: QBasic editor and interpreter — Python experiment
albank1-qbasic-editor-interpreter-python.upstream_name: QBasic editor and interpreter — Python experiment
albank1-qbasic-editor-interpreter-python.display_title: QBasic editor and interpreter — Python experiment
albank1-qbasic-editor-interpreter-python.notes: Substantive single-file Tkinter QBasic-style editor/interpreter with a framebuffer and BasicInterpreter implementation. README explicitly warns it is not fully working; no original binary-derived reconstruction or language conformance is claimed.

qr128-commodore-qr-generator.title: qr128 — Commodore QR-code routines
qr128-commodore-qr-generator.notes: BASIC and assembly QR generator with reusable 6502 routines and disk images for C128, C64 and VIC-20. MEGA65 and X16 support is explicitly unfinished.

qtm-vasm-archimedes-byte-identical.title: QTM v1.49b — byte-identical vasm port

runtime_profiles.name: QTM v1.49b reconstructed builds
runtime_profiles.notes: README reports four byte-identical variants, Arculator playback and timing measurements on an 8 MHz ARM2. This is a test context, not a universal RAM minimum.

qtm-vasm-archimedes-byte-identical.notes: Steve Harrison's tokenized BBC BASIC V ARM source transformed into editable vasm syntax. build.py checks four variants byte-for-byte; README reports Arculator playback and 8 MHz ARM2 measurements.

discovery-quackshot-asm.title: QuackShot assembly reconstruction
discovery-quackshot-asm.notes: Compilable AS assembly game source with data unpacking scripts and assembly batch. README explicitly records changed animation pointers, removed unused code and mirroring; do not label byte-exact.

quadromania-sdl-game.title: Quadromania — SDL tile puzzle with Atari MiNT port
quadromania-sdl-game.display_title: Quadromania — SDL tile puzzle with Atari MiNT port
quadromania-sdl-game.status: Upstream reports multiple running targets; Atari MiNT compiles and runs but is too slow to be playable.
quadromania-sdl-game.notes: Original tile-board game with complete C sources and Make/CMake build paths using SDL, SDL_image and SDL_mixer. Primary README explicitly lists Atari MiNT as a compiled and running target. Upstream explicitly says the Atari MiNT version is too slow to be playable. Target is MiNT with SDL, not an unqualified plain TOS/ST release. Atari build requires Makefile/toolchain adjustment. README explicitly calls Atari MiNT compilable and running but too slow to be playable. Other platforms are reported running. Global playable is left unknown because a single boolean cannot faithfully represent the MiNT exception; notes preserve it. No independent compilation, execution or benchmarking was performed during this catalogue review. Evidence: https://github.com/simonsunnyboy/quadromania/blob/master/README https://github.com/simonsunnyboy/quadromania/blob/master/Makefile https://github.com/simonsunnyboy/quadromania/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt https://github.com/simonsunnyboy/quadromania/blob/master/INSTALL https://github.com/simonsunnyboy/quadromania/commit/f08dcc61537d68f93e813170fd8ea1cf4cce4f87 https://github.com/simonsunnyboy/quadromania/blob/master/Makefile.wiz https://github.com/simonsunnyboy/quadromania/blob/master/Makefile.dingux

quazatron-spectrum-analyser.title: Quazatron
quazatron-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The directory contains a ~1.11 MB Analysis.json database, a ~353 KB exported Quazatron.asm listing, configuration/graphics metadata and custom Lua analysis/viewer scripts; tracked as binary-analysis/assembler-export work rather than claiming a byte-exact source reconstruction.

quiche-z80-pascal-compiler.title: Quiche
quiche-z80-pascal-compiler.display_title: Quiche — experimental Pascal-like Z80 cross compiler
quiche-z80-pascal-compiler.notes: Early work-in-progress Pascal-like cross compiler targeting Z80, with compiler, emulator and IDE source; README does not establish production use.

r68k-68000-core-tools.title: r68k
r68k-68000-core-tools.notes: Reusable Rust 68000 CPU core with tested instruction disassembly and assembly; not a complete Amiga or Atari ST emulator.

jotd-rally-x-amiga.title: Rally-X — Amiga arcade transcode

runtime_profiles.name: AGA build
runtime_profiles.notes: The checked-in AGA executable is assembled with -m68020. No RAM minimum is stated.

jotd-rally-x-amiga.notes: Namco Rally-X Amiga port with explicit Z80 reverse engineering, 68000 transcode and graphics/sound conversion. The repository builds distinct m68000 ECS and m68020 AGA outputs.

rambo-nes-g0me3.title: Rambo
rambo-nes-g0me3.notes: The repository describes itself as Rambo (NES) Back From Source and contains reconstructed bank assembly, game data, levels, scripts, music/player material and build scripts. A NES image build path is present; runtime and byte identity remain unverified.

rambo-c64-ricardoquesada.title: Rambo: First Blood Part II
rambo-c64-ricardoquesada.display_title: Rambo: First Blood Part II — C64 disassembly & patchable reconstruction
rambo-c64-ricardoquesada.notes: Commented C64 Rambo disassembly with a build-and-run workflow and optional gameplay/hardware patches, including copy-protection removal, single-load conversion, gamepad weapon switching and rumble support. The README supplies a current disk binary and gameplay instructions.

rampage-spectrum.title: Rampage
rampage-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

ranarama-spectrum-analyser.title: Ranarama
ranarama-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Ranarama directory contains a 1361 KiB Analysis.json annotation database and exported Z80 assembly and several buffer/screen analysis scripts. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

raptor-amiga-port-raybeez.title: Raptor Amiga Port
raptor-amiga-port-raybeez.display_title: Raptor: Call of the Shadows — native Amiga port
