runtime_profiles.notes: No FPU required; soft-float. README specifies 4 MiB Fast RAM minimum plus 2 MiB Chip RAM, with RTG or AGA display. Tested OS versions listed include 3.1.4, 3.2 variants and 3.9; no universal OS version floor inferred.

runtime_profiles.name: raptor_030_fpu
runtime_profiles.notes: Requires external 68881/68882 FPU. README specifies 4 MiB Fast RAM minimum plus 2 MiB Chip RAM, with RTG or AGA display. Tested OS versions listed include 3.1.4, 3.2 variants and 3.9; no universal OS version floor inferred.

runtime_profiles.name: raptor_nofpu
runtime_profiles.notes: Supports 68EC060/68LC060 without an FPU. README specifies 4 MiB Fast RAM minimum plus 2 MiB Chip RAM, with RTG or AGA display. Tested OS versions listed include 3.1.4, 3.2 variants and 3.9; no universal OS version floor inferred.

runtime_profiles.name: raptor
runtime_profiles.notes: Requires FPU. README specifies 4 MiB Fast RAM minimum plus 2 MiB Chip RAM, with RTG or AGA display. Tested OS versions listed include 3.1.4, 3.2 variants and 3.9; no universal OS version floor inferred.

execution_paths.name: Native m68k Amiga binaries
execution_paths.notes: C/C++ game implementation compiled by m68k-amigaos GCC; author-reported full gameplay, no local test.

raptor-amiga-port-raybeez.notes: AmigaOS port of skynettx/raptor's reverse-engineered C/C++ engine. Four CPU/FPU variants use native Amiga video, input and audio APIs. Requires separately supplied full PC/DOS v1.2 data. Upstream reports full gameplay on real hardware and WinUAE; not independently built or played. OPL music synthesis is a sound component, not guest game-CPU execution.

rasm-z80-assembler.title: RASM
rasm-z80-assembler.display_title: RASM — Z80 assembler and CPC media tooling
rasm-z80-assembler.notes: Author-maintained C Z80 cross-assembler includes CPC cartridge/snapshot/disk/tape generation, integrated compression, patching support and debug symbols. Inspected actual assembler source, integrated API example and build files. Z80 is the output instruction set, not a claim that the host executable runs on Z80. Build scripts and implementation inspected; README reports release tests, but this pass did not independently build/run them.

rastan-spectrum-analyser.title: Rastan
rastan-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Rastan directory contains an approximately 466 KiB Analysis.json annotation database; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

raster-fx-bbc-framework.title: Raster FX — BBC palette timing framework
raster-fx-bbc-framework.display_title: Raster FX — BBC palette timing framework
raster-fx-bbc-framework.notes: BBC Micro BeebAsm raster-effects framework with cycle-based interrupt timing, scanline palette changes, assembly source and disk output. Separate reusable timing framework; related image2mode1 repository includes its own integrated display engine.

rawgl-another-world-engine.title: raw(gl) — Another World engine reimplementation
rawgl-another-world-engine.notes: Reimplements the Another World virtual-machine/game engine. Primary README explicitly accepts original Amiga Bank*, Atari Bank* and Atari AW.TOS demo data, alongside DOS, 3DO and other editions; users supply data. Platform-specific exact behavioral parity is not asserted.

raw2iff-amiga-st-hitchhikr.title: raw2iff — Amiga/ST graphics converter
raw2iff-amiga-st-hitchhikr.notes: Plugin-based raw graphics-to-IFF ILBM converter with explicit Atari ST interleaved input and Amiga planar/bitplane options. Upstream provides Windows and Amiga executables and documents palette, offset and stride controls; the raw picture inputs carry no CPU, while the exact CPUs and minimum requirements of the supplied executables are not stated.

dos-rayman-disasm.title: rayman_disasm
dos-rayman-disasm.notes: README documents stripping a 16-bit DOS extender around a 32-bit game and the gog/ tree contains a large rayman_disasm.S listing. Research output is an analysis/disassembly, not a working port.

rc2014-512k-norflash-writer-bread80.title: RC2014 512K ROM writer
rc2014-512k-norflash-writer-bread80.display_title: RC2014 512K ROM/RAM board — Z80 flash writer

runtime_profiles.notes: Official 512K ROM/512K RAM module with SST39SF040 NOR flash; other modules are untested.

rc2014-512k-norflash-writer-bread80.notes: Z80 assembly utility for erasing and writing SST39SF040 NOR flash on the RC2014 official 512K ROM/512K RAM module. Provides byte, sector and bank routines plus manual sample calls; bundled raw binary/Intel HEX outputs. README reports RASM assembly and tests on this board only; no claim for other modules or independently verified hardware behavior.

rdos-apple2-6502disassembly.title: RDOS
rdos-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Disassembly of SSI's compact RDOS 3.3 disk operating system, with SourceGen project files/binaries and documentation of its filesystem and Applesoft ampersand-command interface. The author notes an earlier full RDOS 2.1 disassembly was used to develop ProDOS RDOS.

rebelstar-raiders-basic-source.title: Rebelstar Raiders
rebelstar-raiders-basic-source.display_title: Rebelstar Raiders — recovered Spectrum BASIC/Z80 source
rebelstar-raiders-basic-source.notes: Source and data for the 1984 game extracted from original TZX tapes with tzxcat plus a custom Go formatter, with comments added by the project author. The source includes Sinclair BASIC and small Z80 graphics/sound routines; no rebuilt tape or runnable-output claim is documented.

rec98-touhou-pc98.title: ReC98
rec98-touhou-pc98.display_title: ReC98 — bit-perfect Touhou PC-98 source reconstruction
rec98-touhou-pc98.notes: Reconstructs the first five Touhou games for NEC PC-9801 from their binaries. Upstream states that every commit builds executables indistinguishable from the originals; TH01 is complete while the remaining games continue to be reverse engineered and finalized.

dos-clyde-re.title: reclyde
dos-clyde-re.display_title: Clyde's Adventure — DOS executable and asset analysis
dos-clyde-re.notes: Partial executable disassembly and tools for RLE, EGA images and castle layouts; extractors recover some volumes and first six castles. Runnable refers to the analysis extractors, not a playable game reconstruction.

regenerator2000-commodore-disassembler.title: Regenerator 2000
regenerator2000-commodore-disassembler.display_title: Regenerator 2000 — Commodore 6502 disassembler, debugger & MCP RE workbench
regenerator2000-commodore-disassembler.notes: Modern interactive 6502 disassembler for Commodore 8-bit systems. It combines manual code/data/graphics analysis, VICE debugging, automatic packed-program emulation/unpacking, assembly/HTML export, headless round-trip assemble/diff verification and an MCP server with analysis skills for automated reverse engineering.

reject-st-demo-reconstruction.title: Reject demo — reconstructed Atari ST source
reject-st-demo-reconstruction.upstream_name: Reject demo — reconstructed Atari ST source
reject-st-demo-reconstruction.display_title: Reject demo — reconstructed Atari ST source

runtime_profiles.name: Patched Reject demo
runtime_profiles.notes: README also requires hard drive and colour display; emulator configuration can match the machine.

evidence.excerpt: An Atari ST or later with at least 1 megabytes of memory, TOS 1.04 minimum, a hard drive, and a colour display.

reject-st-demo-reconstruction.notes: Senior Dads recreated the lost source and original media from the Reject demo binary, then added music and graphics-mode support. README provides Devpac 3 or vasm/vlink build steps and a patched running version.

reminiscence-flashback-engine.title: REminiscence — Flashback engine reimplementation
reminiscence-flashback-engine.notes: Reimplements the Flashback engine and consumes original DOS, Amiga, Macintosh or PC-98 data files. The reviewed tree contains format/resource decoders rather than a native-instruction translator or executable loader, so a single source CPU is not applicable. Primary README is for release 0.5.6.

electron-repton2-expansion-snuggsy.title: Repton 2 Expansion — Acorn Electron
electron-repton2-expansion-snuggsy.notes: Binary-only Electron Repton 2 expansion adding play area, per-screen counters, map and rewind-to-home-screen behavior. README says v0.9 only tested on Elkulator 1. Credit original Repton 2 and distinguish documented modification from source reconstruction.

repton-2-gfoot-bbc.title: Repton 2 — BBC Micro disassembly
repton-2-gfoot-bbc.notes: A py8dis script annotates Repton 2's main executable and a Makefile drives disassembly/reassembly. The source includes an appended loader that reproduces selected initialization steps; no full disk or byte-exact claim is made here.

repton2-bbc-tobylobster.title: repton2disassembly
repton2-bbc-tobylobster.notes: Disassembly and reassembly of Repton 2's main BBC Micro executable. py8dis scripts generate annotated assembly, a fix-up pass targets xa, and the bundled binary folds initialization behaviour from the original D.REPA loader into a directly launchable form; because that output is intentionally transformed, the tracker does not mark it byte-exact.

dos-shortline-resl.title: reSL
dos-shortline-resl.notes: The original branch preserves per-function offsets into the v1.1 DOS binary; main is a playable SDL2 C/C++ port rather than a byte-exact DOS reassembly. Primary build instructions explicitly use Visual Studio's x64 tools and Emscripten/WebAssembly; other portable hosts are not assigned CPUs without output-specific evidence.

resource-amiga-reassembler.title: ReSource
resource-amiga-reassembler.notes: Amiga ReSource reassembler/disassembler maintained from a resourced reconstruction of ReSource itself. Development notes describe regenerating assembly from ReSource project data and comparing rebuilt executables; documented assembler differences mean the rebuilt binary is not byte-identical.

resource-dasm-classic-mac-toolkit.title: resource_dasm
resource-dasm-classic-mac-toolkit.display_title: resource_dasm — classic Mac resource and machine-code archaeology suite
resource-dasm-classic-mac-toolkit.notes: Cohesive reverse-engineering suite centered on classic Mac OS resources, executable code and game data. It includes resource conversion, 68K/PowerPC/x86/SH-4 disassembly, a corresponding emulator/debugger, reverse-engineered resource decompression, archive/asset tools, and selected GameCube format utilities.

resrc4-portable-amiga-hunk-disassembler.title: ReSrc4 — portable Amiga Hunk disassembler
resrc4-portable-amiga-hunk-disassembler.notes: Portable Amiga Hunk disassembler recognizing library calls and some jump tables, with 680x0 and FPU decoding. README reports testing against Civilization ECS, LightWave and an 020-era lha.exe, and documents partial Hunk coverage; the similarly named ReSource project is a separate record.

restunts2-stunts-reconstruction.title: restunts2
restunts2-stunts-reconstruction.notes: Archived successor to the original restunts project. It recreates a working, debuggable 16-bit DOS Stunts 1.1 executable with Open Watcom, exports assembler from collaborative Ghidra analysis and verifies ported C against original code; DOS32 and Linux x86-64 targets are test-only, not playable games.

retaliate64-community-edition.title: Retaliate for the Commodore 64 (Community Edition)
retaliate64-community-edition.display_title: Retaliate CE — Commodore 64 native space-shooter remake

runtime_profiles.name: Community Edition
runtime_profiles.notes: README explicitly describes playing on a real C64 or C128; no exact minimum CPU model or RAM is stated.

runtime_profiles.name: Community Edition in C64 mode
runtime_profiles.notes: README explicitly lists C128 among real-hardware play options; no numeric minimum is inferred.

retaliate64-community-edition.notes: Native 6502 assembly remake of Romans I XVI Gaming's Roku/Android Retaliate. Repository publishes the Community Edition and distinguishes its limits from commercial DX. README supplies real C64/C128 and VICE play instructions, CBM .prg Studio build steps and D64 packaging instructions.

retro-io-amiga-atari-extractor.title: retro-io
retro-io-amiga-atari-extractor.display_title: retro-io — Amiga ADF and Atari ST/MSA extractor
retro-io-amiga-atari-extractor.notes: Java library and GUI with implemented ADF, ST and MSA extraction, common virtual disk API and ZIP export. README explicitly warns that format support may not be complete; image writing and web interface are planned, not implemented.

retrodebugger-c64-atari800-nes.title: RetroDebugger — C64, Atari 8-bit and NES
retrodebugger-c64-atari800-nes.notes: Real-time code and memory debugger embedding VICE, Atari800 and NestopiaUE cores with platform frontends and tests. README calls this a beta and requires users' own ROMs. Credit the three emulator engines; the debugger frontend is the repository's work.

retrodev-cpc-asset-raster-ide.title: Retrodev
retrodev-cpc-asset-raster-ide.display_title: Retrodev — CPC asset, raster and assembly IDE
retrodev-cpc-asset-raster-ide.notes: Integrated CPC development environment with bitmap/tile/sprite/map conversion, palette solving, RASM builds, scriptable exports and timing-validated Z80 raster-handler generation. README marks CPC/CPC+ supported while Spectrum, C64 and MSX are only prepared for; do not advertise those planned targets as implemented.

retroghidra-atari-st-loader.title: RetroGhidra — Atari ST executable loader
retroghidra-atari-st-loader.notes: Ghidra extension lists its Atari ST executable loader as done. Its Commodore Amiga Hunk loader only identifies files and does not load them yet; no Amiga analysis support is claimed.

retroio-multiplatform-media-tool.title: RetroIO
retroio-multiplatform-media-tool.display_title: RetroIO — 8-bit disk and tape image inspector
source_language: DSK, CDT, D64, D71, D81, T64, TAP, TZX and TRD media images
retroio-multiplatform-media-tool.notes: Go command-line utility for inspecting emulator disk/tape images: Amstrad and C64 directory listings, multi-platform geometry/metadata and experimental ZX Spectrum BASIC extraction. It operates on media formats, so no original or output CPU is assigned.

return-home-amstrad-cpc.title: Return Home — Amstrad CPC Z80 space shooter
return-home-amstrad-cpc.display_title: Return Home — Amstrad CPC Z80 space shooter
return-home-amstrad-cpc.notes: Original native CPC shooter with substantial Z80 source and a distributed DSK. README documents RASM/Python assembly, play controls and emulator testing, explicitly discloses Claude Code assistance, and says original hardware has not been verified. src/return_home.asm clarifies firmware calls are used during boot before direct hardware control. The included Z80 test emulator and profiler support development; they are not the primary game output.

return-mutant-camels-c64.title: Return of the Mutant Camels
return-mutant-camels-c64.notes: Llamasoft Source Project disassembly of Return of the Mutant Camels; the collection describes this as a first-pass reconstruction separating game code from data and providing a runnable build.

neuromancer-dos-reuromancer.title: Reuromancer
neuromancer-dos-reuromancer.notes: 64-bit Windows port of the 1988 DOS Neuromancer game. LibNeuroRoutines contains reverse-engineered general-purpose game algorithms and still includes chunks of original disassembled code adapted to x64 MASM, with a stated plan to replace them incrementally with equivalent C. A companion ResourceBrowser inspects and exports assets from the original DAT files.

revenge-mutant-camels-c64.title: Revenge of the Mutant Camels
revenge-mutant-camels-c64.notes: Disassembled and commented source for Jeff Minter's 1984 C64 game Revenge of the Mutant Camels, with a reproducible 64tass build and playable browser version.

reverse-engineer-azel-panzer-dragoon-sag.title: Reverse-Engineering Azel RPG
reverse-engineer-azel-panzer-dragoon-sag.display_title: Panzer Dragoon Saga — SH-2 reverse-engineering corpus
reverse-engineer-azel-panzer-dragoon-sag.notes: Research corpus for Panzer Dragoon Saga/Azel with SH-2 assembly, C decompilation, disc/file analysis and hardware documentation. The README reports bounded per-PRG decompilation percentages rather than a complete or runnable reconstruction.

revs-bbc-micro-moxon.title: Revs — BBC Micro reconstruction
revs-bbc-micro-moxon.notes: Geoff Crammond's Revs reconstructed by hand from the BBC Micro binaries with multiple supported variants; the reference build is checksum-verified against the original.

flashback-rextract-amiga-to-st.title: RExtract — Flashback Amiga disk extractor
flashback-rextract-amiga-to-st.notes: Browser-side extraction of Flashback Amiga install disks into the DATA layout of the author’s Atari ST REminiscence port. Decodes IPF/ADF/ADZ and OFS/FFS; converts 21 MOD tracks to YM register streams. Requires user-supplied disks.

rg-rampage-c64-jason-kelk.title: RG Rampage — Commodore 64 native game source
rg-rampage-c64-jason-kelk.display_title: RG Rampage — Commodore 64 native game source
rg-rampage-c64-jason-kelk.status: Original native source release; no independent compilation or execution in this review.
rg-rampage-c64-jason-kelk.notes: Jason Kelk’s original source credits him for code, graphics and sound effects. The ACME assembly contains native C64 memory layout, seven level indices, sprite construction and character display code; a PRG is also committed. Creator-owned game root with graphics and sound includes; no explicit root license was found. Preserve source-available wording rather than asserting an open-source license. build.bat invokes ACME and rg_rampage.prg is present, but no README, successful-build report or gameplay instructions establish the present source’s build/play behavior. Do not turn a build script or binary filename into a positive test result; all flags remain null. Reviewed on 2026-10-05; no independent build or execution was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/JasonKelk/RG-Rampage-C64/blob/master/rg_rampage.asm https://github.com/JasonKelk/RG-Rampage-C64/blob/master/build.bat. Latest upstream commit: https://github.com/JasonKelk/RG-Rampage-C64/commit/d58da68f62383ff0a1bb9f433a5d3d413c26216a

rick-dangerous-oracle-trainer.title: Rick Dangerous — Oracle trainer menu reconstruction
rick-dangerous-oracle-trainer.display_title: Rick Dangerous — Oracle trainer menu reconstruction
rick-dangerous-oracle-trainer.notes: Weetibix / Oracle is credited for the historical Oracle Rick Dangerous trainer menu. Volker Schwaberow's collection presents reconstructed assembly; File header names Weetibix/Oracle and the reconstruction; labelled game patch addresses and Amiga OS/hardware calls are present. No original-binary comparison, successful build or runtime test is established for this component.

dos-rigelengine.title: RigelEngine
dos-rigelengine.display_title: Duke Nukem II — modern reverse-engineered engine

runtime_profiles.name: Low-end Linux SBC
runtime_profiles.notes: The README says the engine needs less than 64 MB RAM, which is a usage bound rather than an exact minimum and is therefore not stored as min_ram_kib. OpenGL 3.0 or OpenGL ES 2.0 is required.

evidence.excerpt: Runs on a single-core ARMv6 CPU at 700 MHz, needs less than 64 MB RAM, and requires OpenGL 3.0 or OpenGL ES 2.0.

dos-rigelengine.notes: Separate from Duke2Reconstructed: modern C++ engine informed by original DOS disassembly, reading original game data and supporting all four episodes. Primary build files produce x86-64 and WebAssembly outputs, while the README documents operation on a 700 MHz ARMv6 Raspberry Pi 1. The advertised web build is currently unavailable.

rip-and-tear-c64-demo-analysis.title: rip-and-tear
rip-and-tear-c64-demo-analysis.display_title: Rip and Tear — C64 demo effects analysis notes
rip-and-tear-c64-demo-analysis.notes: VICE save states and research notes documenting experimental reverse engineering of C64 demo effects; the README explicitly says the work is still limited in scope.

river-raid-spectrum.title: River Raid
river-raid-spectrum.notes: Annotated disassembly built from the original tape image; build process checks generated output against the game image and can apply fixes.

rnc-propack-decompiled-lab313ru.title: RNC ProPack — decompiled compressor
rnc-propack-decompiled-lab313ru.notes: Decompiled RNC ProPack compression tool with pack/unpack, search and extraction modes and a Makefile plus Visual Studio project. Its README notes original-game-specific packing parameters for Earthworm Jim and Aladdin; original tool CPU/platform is not specified there.

roadster-amiga-network-commodity.title: Roadster
roadster-amiga-network-commodity.display_title: Roadster — native Amiga Roadshow network controller

runtime_profiles.name: Native Amiga commodity
runtime_profiles.notes: Requires Roadshow. No minimum RAM specified.

roadster-amiga-network-commodity.notes: New C/GadTools Amiga commodity inspired by Roadie, controlling Roadshow interfaces with status, Ping/TraceRoute and ARexx integration. README says written from scratch and shows operation on the author's A500. Included source/build script and documented release packaging support a native homebrew record. No local test.

robin-of-the-wood-spectrum.title: Robin of the Wood
robin-of-the-wood-spectrum.notes: nzeemin SkoolKit reverse-engineering project. README status: Good progress.

robocod-trsi-trainer.title: Robocod — TRSI trainer menu reconstruction
robocod-trsi-trainer.notes: TRSI is credited for the historical TRSI Robocod trainer menu. Volker Schwaberow's collection presents reconstructed assembly; File header identifies the reconstructed Robocod trainer; assembly plus a separate music binary and assets are present. No original-binary comparison, successful build or runtime test is established for this component.

robocop-spectrum-analyser.title: Robocop
robocop-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Robocop directory contains an approximately 518 KiB Analysis.json annotation database; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

robocop-3-nes-g0me3.title: RoboCop 3
robocop-3-nes-g0me3.notes: The repository identifies itself as a RoboCop 3 NES Back From Source project and contains large annotated bank files, RAM/sound/sprite definitions, research notes and DASM build scripts. Reassembly is documented, but successful execution, playability and byte identity were not independently verified.

robot-jet-action-c64-source.title: Robot Jet Action — original C64 game source
robot-jet-action-c64-source.display_title: Robot Jet Action — original C64 game source
robot-jet-action-c64-source.notes: Original game code/graphics by Tomasz 'Carrion' Mielnik and music/SFX by Kamil 'Jammer' Wolnikowski, published for educational use under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. main.c explicitly requires KickC 0.82 and warns later versions do not compile; make.sh generates data before the main build. robotron-2084-apple2-fschuhi.title: Robotron 2084 — Apple II reverse engineering
robotron-2084-apple2-fschuhi.notes: Apple II Robotron 2084 reverse-engineering workbench and disassembly. The project evolved from a Python emulator/debugger with tracing and memory/call-tree tools to C#/Virtu and SourceGen-assisted analysis; its current disassembly is retained in the repository.

jotd-rocn-rope-amiga.title: Roc'n Rope — Amiga arcade transcode

runtime_profiles.notes: README reports 50 fps on an unexpanded A1200; the checked-in AGA executable is assembled with -m68020. No numeric RAM minimum is inferred from the machine model.

jotd-rocn-rope-amiga.notes: Roc'n Rope Amiga port; README credits reverse engineering, 68000 transcode and graphics/sound conversion.

rocket-podule-arculator.title: Rocket Podule — Arculator sync interface
rocket-podule-arculator.notes: C podule DLL for the Arculator emulator to expose Rocket Sync Tracker timeline/track operations; author commits add key callbacks and remove a redundant build dependency. Uses Rocket Sync protocol/code; the Arculator integration is the reviewed addition.

rockford-hidden-level-patcher.title: Rockford Patcher
rockford-hidden-level-patcher.display_title: Rockford — DOS hidden-level recovery and patcher

README describes the running attract sequence, controls and implemented player/enemy systems, supporting upstream-reported runnable/playable output. st-remote-debugger-blagay.upstream_name: ST Remote Debugger — Visual C++ host
st-remote-debugger-blagay.display_title: ST Remote Debugger — Visual C++ host
st-remote-debugger-blagay.notes: Host-side Visual C++ debugger source includes a 68k disassembler, memory/register requests and step/run/upload command protocol. Repository has no README or clear target-side source and references a relative external minIni path; build and working target connection remain unverified.

sopwith-atari-st-neilrackett.title: ST Sopwith
sopwith-atari-st-neilrackett.display_title: ST Sopwith — native Atari ST port

runtime_profiles.name: Native Atari backend release
runtime_profiles.notes: Release explicitly requires 512KB RAM. Makefile targets 68000, but this profile does not independently infer a CPU minimum. Latest commit says STDL backend needs more than 512KB, so the memory claim applies to the native backend only.

sopwith-atari-st-neilrackett.notes: Brings released Sopwith source to Atari ST with native C/68k code, custom levels, sound, palettes and medals. Native Atari backend and optional STDL-based backend are interchangeable. The release needs 512KB; STDL needs more. Latest commit reports rendered-frame equivalence and timing improvements, which are not byte-exact binary evidence. No reverse-engineering-derived-port tag is applied because original source is used.

vt100-cartridge.title: ST VT100 Terminal Emulator cartridge
vt100-cartridge.display_title: ST VT100 — Atari ST terminal-emulator source reconstruction
vt100-cartridge.notes: All functions reconstructed into period-style C/assembly and checked against the original disassembly.

st1-zx1-streaming-decompressor.title: ST1 — streaming ZX1 decompression for 68000
st1-zx1-streaming-decompressor.status: Upstream-tested streaming decompressor, packers and YX6 music-player output; not independently built or benchmarked.
st1-zx1-streaming-decompressor.notes: README and native 68000 assembly verify resumable ZX1 decompression, including fixed-memory ring streaming. Java/C# packers and Atari-oriented tests accompany the 68k code. Upstream explicitly credits Claude Code for decoder/optimization work and Codex for the C# implementation. Input is trusted-only and unchecked; performance/test assertions remain upstream claims. README describes runnable PRG generation and Atari/Hatari tests; latest commit reports a passing emulation suite and matching register checksum. Byte-for-byte compressed data compatibility is not evidence of an original executable match. No independent compilation, execution or benchmarking was performed during this catalogue review. Evidence: https://github.com/odipar/ST1/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/odipar/ST1/blob/main/68k/ST1.S https://github.com/odipar/ST1/blob/main/68k/ST1_ring.S https://github.com/odipar/ST1/blob/main/pom.xml https://github.com/odipar/ST1/commit/96cddfa9f3f3139b612f3ecc26522b64b0034b3e The Java and C# host packers are portable components; this review did not establish a precise supported host-OS list.

stage-swaptro-amiga-disassembly.title: Stage-Swaptro
stage-swaptro-amiga-disassembly.display_title: Stage-Swaptro — Amiga demo disassembly and variants
stage-swaptro-amiga-disassembly.notes: Reverse engineers the packed Stage swaptro extracted from Sanity's Velveteen 18 disk, documents its load address and memory map, and provides buildable 68000 source plus several patch-based visual/music variants. README includes a Makefile workflow for applying patches, assembling and making a floppy; game playability is not applicable to a demo.

star-raiders-atari8-sidney-cadot.title: Star Raiders Atari 8-bit source analysis
star-raiders-atari8-sidney-cadot.notes: Atari 400/800 Star Raiders 6502 reconstruction. The ca65/ld65 Makefile builds an 8 KiB cartridge and verifies it against the supplied MD5 checksum.

star-wars-arcade-audio-firmware.title: star-wars-arcade-audio
star-wars-arcade-audio-firmware.display_title: Star Wars arcade — audio firmware disassembly
star-wars-arcade-audio-firmware.notes: Commented disassembly of Atari's 1983 Star Wars sound ROM pair 136021.107/136021.208. The source identifies F9DASM as the disassembler and A09 as the assembler and documents RIOT/POKEY-style sound-board registers; no byte-identity claim is made.

amisc-amiga.title: StarCraft — AmiSC 68K

runtime_profiles.name: Native AmigaOS build
runtime_profiles.notes: README states 68020 minimum with no FPU, AGA or RTG graphics, and enough memory for about 20 MB of sprite graphics plus sound samples. That working-set description is not treated as an exact total-RAM minimum; 68060 is recommended for AGA and a fast 68040 for RTG.

evidence.excerpt: AmigaOS 3.0 or later; 68020 minimum, no FPU required; AGA chipset, or a graphics card (RTG / Picasso96).

amisc-amiga.notes: Native Amiga 68k StarCraft port that reads the user's original MPQ-derived game data and supports playable skirmishes. The repository currently publishes binaries/documentation but not the port source, so implementation provenance cannot be audited from source.

stardust-msx-reassembly-antxiko.title: Stardust MSX annotated tape reconstruction
stardust-msx-reassembly-antxiko.notes: Finished, commented seven-block MSX cassette reconstruction of Topo Soft Stardust. The primary README and Makefile state that five Z80 listings rebuild all 93,861 tape bytes byte for byte, gated by a supplied TSX hash, Pasmo, z80dasm and Python 3; this audit did not rerun the build.

stardust-spectrum-partial-reconstruction.title: stardust-48k
stardust-spectrum-partial-reconstruction.display_title: Stardust — partial ZX Spectrum source recovery
stardust-spectrum-partial-reconstruction.notes: Original developers captured a Spectrum snapshot, profiled executed regions and produced editable Z80 assembly; README says intro and second stage are absent and source is not yet ready for complete reassembly. CPC release is historical context only.

starflight-st-asset-analysis.title: Starflight
starflight-st-asset-analysis.display_title: Starflight — Atari ST binary and asset analysis
starflight-st-asset-analysis.notes: Indexed as an Atari ST Starflight research repository with a Ghidra project and Python BTX, AGO and OMEGA font/tile readers. The canonical GitHub URL returned 404 on 2026-10-01, so prior descriptive metadata is retained pending relocation but the formerly asserted m68000 source CPU has been removed rather than inferred from Atari ST.

starflight-reverse.title: Starflight Reverse
starflight-reverse.notes: Reverse engineering of the 1986 DOS game Starflight. The project exploits retained/encrypted Forth word names and the game's indirect-threaded representation to recover thousands of words, decode overlays and emit C representations of the recovered routines. A separate remastered successor, canadacow/starflight-reverse, builds on this recovered codebase with full Forth/assembly emulation and a new Vulkan presentation layer; it is tracked independently.

starflight-reverse-remastered.title: Starflight Reverse — Remastered
starflight-reverse-remastered.display_title: Starflight — Vulkan remaster from recovered Forth/x86 runtime

runtime_profiles.name: Windows x64 build
runtime_profiles.notes: Upstream says Windows x64 with Visual Studio 2022 Community Edition is the most likely build path, while warning that the checked-in build may currently be broken.

runtime_profiles.name: Linux x64 build
runtime_profiles.notes: Upstream names Linux x64 via CMake/Vcpkg but warns that the checked-in build may currently be broken. No RAM or OS-version minimum is stated.

starflight-reverse-remastered.notes: Independent remastered successor to the s-macke Starflight reverse-engineering line. It retains/emulates the recovered Forth and assembly execution so the whole game is playable, while adding a new real-time Vulkan/rotoscoped presentation layer with switchable classic EGA/CGA output. Tracked separately from s-macke/starflight-reverse because this project is an RE-derived playable reimplementation/remaster rather than only the underlying disassembly/recovery work.

starquake-spectrum.title: Starquake
starquake-spectrum.notes: Ritchie Swann disassembly; README explicitly describes it as work in progress with routines/data still undocumented.

starquake-spectrum-analyser.title: Starquake
starquake-spectrum-analyser.notes: Substantial title-specific ZX Spectrum analysis project. The Starquake directory contains a 3281 KiB Analysis.json annotation database and large annotation database plus decoded player/effect graphics. Tracked as binary-analysis/analysis-state work; no byte-exact reconstruction claim is inferred.

star-raiders-atari8-lwiest.title: StarRaiders
star-raiders-atari8-lwiest.display_title: Star Raiders — Atari 8-bit fully documented source reconstruction
star-raiders-atari8-lwiest.notes: Complete, extensively documented assembly-language reconstruction made directly from the 8 KB Star Raiders cartridge ROM and finished in September 2015. When scans of Atari's original source later resurfaced, the author compared them with the reconstruction and reports only a few trivial corrections, while retaining substantially richer explanatory documentation.

starship-commander-apple2-6502disassembl.title: Starship Commander
starship-commander-apple2-6502disassembl.display_title: Starship Commander — Apple II mixed-language disassembly
starship-commander-apple2-6502disassembl.notes: Apple II Starship Commander analysis spanning roughly two dozen Applesoft programs plus machine-language sound, graphics and font routines. The project provides commented BASIC listings, SourceGen projects for binaries and a cross-program variable map.

state-of-the-art-amiga-sota.title: State of the Art — C demo reimplementation
state-of-the-art-amiga-sota.upstream_name: State of the Art — C demo reimplementation
state-of-the-art-amiga-sota.display_title: State of the Art — C demo reimplementation
subjects: State of the Art — C demo reimplementation
state-of-the-art-amiga-sota.notes: Reimplements the Spaceballs Amiga demo in C using its original graphics, animation and audio. README says the demo is complete but some timing is off; SDL2, mikmod and Python 3 are needed for the documented native build. No claim of original-source recovery or byte-identical output.

c64-mist64-static6502.title: static6502
c64-mist64-static6502.notes: Old static 6502-assembly-to-C translator used to generate the cbmbasic core. Repository explicitly says it should not be used for current work and points to libcpu as its successor; catalogued as historical tooling with that limitation.

stdl-atari-st-porting-library.title: STDL — Atari ST DirectMedia Layer
stdl-atari-st-porting-library.notes: Planar-native compatibility layer and converter for porting SDL 1.2 games to ST/STE, used by several ports. The README documents cross-compilation with m68k-atari-mint-gcc, runnable TOS examples under Hatari, byte-identical BLiTTER/CPU checks on target, and measured stock-ST/Mega-STE behavior. The 26 September update adds per-step YM tone/noise effects and preserves their millisecond timing at both 50 and 60 Hz. SDL source/assets are inputs to the porting library, so source CPU is not applicable.

stellar-7-apple2-6502disassembly.title: Stellar 7
stellar-7-apple2-6502disassembly.display_title: Stellar 7 — Apple II disassembly & engine analysis
stellar-7-apple2-6502disassembly.notes: Detailed Apple II Stellar 7 disassembly covering the loader, title code, both game-engine portions, briefing/gameplay overlays and level/object data. The project publishes SourceGen files/binaries plus extensive analysis of 3D objects, mechanics and data structures.

albank1-stellar-dodger-c64-disassembly.title: Stellar Dodger
albank1-stellar-dodger-c64-disassembly.notes: PRG listing includes BASIC SYS loader and code/data annotation. Single-file JC64dis/DASM-based listing; source header has assembly instructions, but original matching and a working build were not independently checked.

stepping-back-atari-demo.title: Stepping Back — MegaBuSTers Atari ST demo
stepping-back-atari-demo.display_title: Stepping Back — MegaBuSTers Atari ST demo
stepping-back-atari-demo.status: 2024 demo release; author tested with Hatari 2.5.0 and EmuTOS 1.3.
stepping-back-atari-demo.notes: 2024 MegaBuSTers demo. Main assembly and build script are present; script assembles STEPBACK.PRG with rmac and packages disk/source archives. README reports development using rmac 2.2.25 and Hatari 2.5.0 with EmuTOS 1.3. Plain-ST baseline. Wider TT/Falcon compatibility is only believed, not guaranteed; README warns about unsupported startup resolutions. Licensing has additional terms, so do not simplify to unqualified stock AGPL. README reports the assembler/test environment and shipped PRG/floppy/source forms; build.sh corroborates the process. Upstream build/run evidence only. No independent compilation, execution or benchmarking was performed during this catalogue review. Evidence: https://github.com/jbqueru/stepback/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/jbqueru/stepback/blob/main/stepback.s https://github.com/jbqueru/stepback/blob/main/build.sh https://github.com/jbqueru/stepback/commit/48fb7b35f838cd2fbf014021b395d41a964f5017

stm32-usbfloppytracer-amiga-st.title: STM32 USB Floppy Tracer
stm32-usbfloppytracer-amiga-st.display_title: STM32 USB Floppy Tracer — Amiga/Atari physical disk imaging
stm32-usbfloppytracer-amiga-st.notes: STM32F407 firmware plus Rust host CLI/GUI reads ADF and ST and writes ADF, IPF, ST and experimental patched STX. The firmware configuration explicitly selects Rust's thumbv7em-none-eabihf target for Cortex-M4F/M7F; the documented working board is STM32F407, so ARM is recorded as an output CPU without assigning CPUs to the disk-image inputs. Written tracks are verified; weak-bit and some STX protections remain experimental.

storm-coming-up-amiga.title: Storm Coming Up intro
storm-coming-up-amiga.notes: ReSource-based disassembly and documented modernization of Storm Coming Up, including Copper/Blitter checkerboard analysis. Author states the supplied source assembles and runs.

stormbringer-spectrum.title: Stormbringer
stormbringer-spectrum.notes: Complete 48K RAM disassembly by Philip M. Anderson; source preserved in Michael Cook's archive.

stos-atari-basic-source.title: STOS BASIC
stos-atari-basic-source.display_title: STOS BASIC — Atari ST compiler and interpreter source
stos-atari-basic-source.notes: Mixed archive of historical STOS BASIC interpreter/compiler, extension and project assembly sources, including an orig tree and adapted src/compiler trees. Core STOS and compiler sources are explicitly 68000-oriented and emit/run native Atari ST code. Specialized Falcon and later-CPU extensions remain component-specific and do not change the core 68000 classification. The repository does not yet establish a verified end-to-end modern build or a single minimum runtime profile.

street-rod-kylofon-sdl3.title: Street Rod — native VGA SDL3 reconstruction
street-rod-kylofon-sdl3.display_title: Street Rod — native VGA SDL3 reconstruction

execution_paths.name: Native reconstructed output

street-rod-kylofon-sdl3.status: Author-reported playable port; catalogue review did not build or run it.
street-rod-kylofon-sdl3.notes: Native C reconstruction of the full VGA game with optional Street Rod SE car data. Maintains original data/memory structure, adds a launcher, and requires original assets; alternate graphics adapters remain unported. Reviewed on 2026-10-05; build/playability claims are upstream reports, not independent execution. stspeech-atari-st-c-port.title: stspeech
stspeech-atari-st-c-port.display_title: ST Speech — Atari ST synthesizer reconstruction in C
source_language: 1986 Atari ST speech binary and disassemblies
stspeech-atari-st-c-port.notes: Portable C recreation of the 1986 ST text-to-speech synthesizer, with original binary disassemblies and documented code-lineage comparison; claims sample-for-sample output, not original source or binary equality.

sttrans-stbook-analysis.title: STTRANS
sttrans-stbook-analysis.display_title: STTRANS — Atari STBook transfer protocol research
sttrans-stbook-analysis.notes: Research repository containing the original STTRANS.PRG, its Ghidra project and an 8.9 KB Python serial companion implementing command, path, block and checksum handling. The checked-in primary binary identifies as an Atari ST M68K contiguous executable; the Python companion is host-side protocol tooling and emits no translated native target. No reconstructed STTRANS executable or hardware minimum is claimed.

stunt-car-racer-bbc-kieranhj.title: Stunt Car Racer
stunt-car-racer-bbc-kieranhj.display_title: Stunt Car Racer — C64-to-BBC Master reverse-engineered port
stunt-car-racer-bbc-kieranhj.notes: BBC Master 128 port derived from a raw C64 6502 disassembly. The team reverse engineered game functionality and data structures, rearranged them for the BBC memory map, and replaced or augmented graphics, sound and I/O for BBC hardware.

stunt-car-racer-ste-patches.title: Stunt Car Racer STE
stunt-car-racer-ste-patches.notes: Experimental blitter replacements for selected ST rendering routines. Make produces overlay binaries; run the unmodified game under Hatari and load patches into memory using the debugger. No standalone runnable disk image and no demonstrated performance improvement. STE with at least 1 MiB specified.

sturmbios-cpm68k-amiga.title: SturmBIOS
sturmbios-cpm68k-amiga.display_title: SturmBIOS — CP/M-68K BIOS and boot system for Amiga

runtime_profiles.name: PAL Amiga CP/M-68K
runtime_profiles.notes: README states PAL only, one or two floppy drives, no hard-disk support and use of the first 512 KiB of RAM. No exact total-RAM minimum is inferred from that memory map. Higher 68020/030/040 support remains experimental.

sturmbios-cpm68k-amiga.notes: New native Amiga BIOS/boot and disk-image integration for CP/M-68K, retaining original CP/M CCP/BDOS and supplying Amiga hardware support. Includes documented bootable ADF creation with vasm/cpmtools and terminal/serial/disk interfaces. 68020/030/040 support is explicitly experimental; no independent boot test.

sugarboxv2-cpc-emulator-debugger.title: SugarboxV2
sugarboxv2-cpc-emulator-debugger.display_title: SugarboxV2 — CPC emulator and source debugger
sugarboxv2-cpc-emulator-debugger.notes: Cross-platform CPC 464/664/6128/CPC+ emulator with an integrated debugger and headless mode. Its JSON-over-TCP server supports register/memory access, stepping, breakpoints, labels, media control and CRTC/ASIC/Gate Array/PSG/PPI/FDC/tape state; a linked VS Code extension adds source-level DAP debugging.

sundog-st-psystem.title: SunDog: Frozen Legacy
sundog-st-psystem.display_title: SunDog — Atari ST p-system runtime reconstruction

runtime_profiles.name: Linux build
runtime_profiles.notes: Requires SDL2 development files, Meson and Ninja; GNU readline is needed only for the debugger. Running the game requires a user-supplied original 360K ST disk image. The renderer requires OpenGL ES 2+; no CPU or RAM minimum is stated.

runtime_profiles.name: macOS build
runtime_profiles.notes: Upstream documents Mesa, Meson, Ninja, SDL2 and Chromium setup plus a user-supplied original disk image. It does not state a CPU, RAM or macOS-version minimum.

sundog-st-psystem.notes: Runs original Atari ST SunDog p-code and data from a user-supplied 360K ST disk image via a C p-system IV interpreter; recreates the few ST graphics assembly routines. The game code and assets are not distributed. Upstream documents Linux/macOS build paths.

dos-supaplex-binary-patches.title: Supaplex
dos-supaplex-binary-patches.notes: Assembly files patch portions of the original DOS executable via incbin; fixes include smooth scrolling, copy-protection bypass, input and sound changes. This is not a full game disassembly or reconstructed source tree.

jotd-super-bagman-amiga.title: Super Bagman — Amiga arcade transcode

runtime_profiles.name: 68000 Amiga build
runtime_profiles.notes: The main executable and game objects are assembled with -m68000. The README says it should run on an A500, but does not give a verified general RAM floor.

jotd-super-bagman-amiga.notes: Amiga version uses approximately 99% transcoded original code; README credits Z80 reverse engineering and Z80→68k transcode.

super-c-nes-vermiceli.title: Super C
super-c-nes-vermiceli.display_title: Super C — NES byte-exact annotated disassembly
super-c-nes-vermiceli.notes: Annotated NES Super C disassembly discovered through the Contra project's sibling link. Its README explicitly states that the build scripts reassemble the US ROM to a byte-for-byte match and can also build PAL Probotector II, with supporting bank/graphics/sound/debugging documentation.

super-foul-egg-ios-ant512.title: Super Foul Egg — iOS remake-lineage port

smb3-nes-captainsouthbird.title: Super Mario Bros. 3
smb3-nes-captainsouthbird.display_title: Super Mario Bros. 3 — NES byte-exact disassembly
smb3-nes-captainsouthbird.notes: NESASM-based disassembly of Super Mario Bros. 3 US PRG1. The README explicitly states that it reassembles into a byte-for-byte perfect clone and is intended for internal research and technical ROM hacking; support files for NoDice/MusConv are included.

super-pacman-arcade-disassembly.title: Super Pac-Man
super-pacman-arcade-disassembly.notes: Project-specific Super Pac-Man 6809 listing, ROM-byte extraction and in-progress Amiga translation. The makefile explicitly emits m68000 OCS/ECS objects and m68020 AGA objects, but README and loader names still describe Mappy and required generated inputs are not all present; no successful build, playable output or minimum hardware profile is inferred. The latest reverse-engineering fixes explicitly credit Claude.

supercars3-amiga-remake-jotd.title: Supercars 3 — Super Cars I/II remake
supercars3-amiga-remake-jotd.notes: Java remake preserving the original Super Cars and Super Cars II circuits, using enhanced or extracted graphics/music while adding new cars, weapons, a circuit editor and levels. Primary readme lists 31 original circuits, host compatibility and known AI/physics differences; exact original media variants and degree of behavioral parity remain unverified.

superdiskindex-flux.title: SuperDiskIndex
superdiskindex-flux.notes: Experimental command-line tool analyzes SCP flux images from Greaseweazle, reports disk state and exports Amiga ADF/Atari images with file listings and block maps. README states Linux only and explicitly lists many known bugs.

superfrog-floppy-analysis-yanekk.title: Superfrog floppy format and level-analysis tools

vs-sr-cd32-superfrog.title: Superfrog — CD32 reverse-engineering documentation
vs-sr-cd32-superfrog.notes: Measurement-first reverse-engineering documentation of the Amiga CD32 release of Superfrog. The repository redistributes no game assets; reproducible tools derive structural, executable, compression, graphics/audio and archaeological findings from user-supplied media.

super-mario-bros-nes-mstan-recomp.title: SuperMarioBrosRecomp
super-mario-bros-nes-mstan-recomp.display_title: Super Mario Bros. — NES-to-PC static recompilation

execution_paths.name: native PC build

super-mario-bros-nes-mstan-recomp.notes: Independent game project built on NESRecomp. The primary README states that original 6502 ROM machine code is translated to C and compiled to native x64. swift64-macos-c64-emulator.title: Swift64 — native macOS C64 emulator

runtime_profiles.name: Swift64 macOS application
runtime_profiles.notes: README and Package.swift explicitly require macOS 14+. User-supplied BASIC, KERNAL and character ROMs are needed; 1541 ROM is optional for fast-load but required for true-drive mode. No host ISA/RAM minimum or broad game compatibility is established.

swift64-macos-c64-emulator.status: Packaged macOS emulator with upstream-reported BASIC boot; many games/demos and true-drive cases remain incomplete.
swift64-macos-c64-emulator.notes: Swift macOS C64 emulator with shared Emu6502 core, C64 chip/1541 models, debugger and Metal/AVFoundation application. The same root also contains a secondary, earlier-stage NES emulator. Generic machine emulator/debugger tooling. vamiganet-browser-amiga-emulator.title: vAmiga.net
vamiganet-browser-amiga-emulator.notes: Browser adaptation of vAmiga with a C++ emulation core, Emscripten build and Svelte/TypeScript interface. README links a running deployment and gives local build/run commands. CMake's 512 MB WebAssembly allocation is not treated as a minimum browser/system RAM requirement. No local execution test.

vamigados-browser-filesystem.title: vAmigaDOS — browser image explorer
vamigados-browser-filesystem.notes: Browser shell for inspecting and editing Amiga ADF/HDF disk images, powered by the vAmiga emulator compiled to WebAssembly. Offers directory navigation, file operations and filesystem diagnostics; indexes a useful archival tool rather than independent OS reconstruction.

vampire-killer-msx2-0xe1f.title: Vampire Killer
vampire-killer-msx2-0xe1f.notes: WIP fully labeled-source disassembly of Konami's 128 KiB MSX2 MegaROM. All banks assemble without leftover binary inclusions and make verify SHA-1-checks the generated ROM; upstream explicitly describes a human-guided, largely AI-executed workflow without naming the AI tool.

vasm-m68k-mot-vscode-amiga.title: vasm m68k MOT — Amiga debugging variant
vasm-m68k-mot-vscode-amiga.display_title: vasm m68k MOT — Amiga debugging variant
vasm-m68k-mot-vscode-amiga.notes: Unofficial vasm mirror adapted for vscode-amiga-debug, with GCC-compatible section names and memory-type section suffix support visible in author commits. Credit vasm upstream; tracked fork changes, not authorship of the assembler.

vchar64-commodore-asset-editor.title: VChar64
vchar64-commodore-asset-editor.display_title: VChar64 — Commodore 64/128 character, tile & map editor
vchar64-commodore-asset-editor.notes: Cross-platform Commodore 64/128 graphics-development editor supporting character, tile and map editing; CharPad, Koala and VICE snapshot import; assembly/raw/PRG export; palette emulation and live preview against target tooling.

vgmplay-bbc.title: vgmplay — early BBC Micro VGM player
vgmplay-bbc.display_title: vgmplay — early BBC Micro VGM player
vgmplay-bbc.notes: Early 6502 VGM playback source and BBC disk image. README dates the experiments to 2015–2016 and says simondotm's newer converter/packer superseded them. Historical audio development reference, not the present successor's implementation.

vice-cartconv-c64-bank-extractor.title: VICE cartconv
vice-cartconv-c64-bank-extractor.display_title: VICE cartconv — C64 cartridge bank extraction
vice-cartconv-c64-bank-extractor.notes: Small stand-alone adaptation of VICE's cartconv with -f extraction of CRT CHIP banks into header-plus-payload chunks; README says EasyFlash and GMOD/2 tested but other cartridges uncertain. main.c retains VICE author credits and adds extraction behavior.

virtualjaguar-libretro.title: Virtual Jaguar libretro
virtualjaguar-libretro.notes: Maintained Jaguar and Jaguar CD libretro emulator. Repository documents processor/peripheral models and hardware-behavior test suite; no claim of new reverse engineering of a particular game.

vlm-jaguar-reconstruction.title: Virtual Light Machine
vlm-jaguar-reconstruction.display_title: Virtual Light Machine — Atari Jaguar core reconstruction
vlm-jaguar-reconstruction.notes: Reconstructed source for Jeff Minter's Virtual Light Machine. The core existed only as vlm.abs in an otherwise surviving source dump; it was reverse engineered with the surviving symbol file and reintegrated into a buildable Jaguar source tree.

virushistory-historical-analysis-tools.title: Virus History
virushistory-historical-analysis-tools.display_title: Virus History — historical malware archive and analysis tools
virushistory-historical-analysis-tools.notes: Repository-level museum of historical malicious software, built from a recovered 1990s collection and extended with documentation and research utilities. The tools/ directory includes an Amiga bootblock analyzer and a decoder for a 68000 copy/XOR loop; these are components of the same preservation and analysis project. Other platforms and samples have not been individually verified.

visicalc-apple-ii-buildable-disassembly.title: VisiCalc
visicalc-apple-ii-buildable-disassembly.notes: Buildable Merlin32/ca65 adaptation of the Brutal Deluxe VisiCalc disassembly. Recovers two regions left undecoded in the earlier listing, corrects code/data boundaries, and generates a DOS 3.3 disk image. README says source-only corrections retain byte-identical binaries; this is credited follow-on analysis, not the original disassembly. Whole-program match against the source binary is not claimed.

voidrunner-c16.title: Voidrunner
voidrunner-c16.notes: Disassembled and commented source for Jeff Minter's 1987 Commodore 16/Plus/4 Gridrunner-series game Voidrunner; the repository provides a reproducible 64tass build.

volamos-amiga-cli-runtime.title: volamos

runtime_profiles.name: Linux x86-64 command-line runtime
runtime_profiles.notes: Current CI builds the release executable on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and executes vamos comparison and interpreter/JIT fixtures. No minimum RAM or Linux release is established.

runtime_profiles.name: Apple Silicon command-line runtime
runtime_profiles.notes: Current CI log identifies aarch64-apple-darwin and passes unit/end-to-end guest fixture execution. No minimum RAM or macOS release is established.

volamos-amiga-cli-runtime.notes: Wine-style host runtime for classic AmigaOS m68k command-line tools: interprets guest instructions (optional m68k-crate trace JIT) and reimplements OS library calls in Rust. No Kickstart ROM is needed for normal use. It is generic development/analysis tooling, not a native reconstruction of a specific game; graphics, custom chips, Workbench GUI and games are explicitly out of scope. Linux/macOS build and guest execution are corroborated by current CI logs; published Windows x86-64 binaries compile but Windows/Wine runtime remains unverified. Interpreter/JIT parity covers six fixtures; comparison with vamos includes three documented known divergences, so it is not universal compatibility proof.

voltmace-delta14b-bbc-disassembly.title: voltmace-delta14b-driver
voltmace-delta14b-bbc-disassembly.display_title: Voltmace Delta 14B drivers — BBC byte-reproducing disassembly
voltmace-delta14b-bbc-disassembly.notes: Annotated KEYPAD and JOYSTIK driver/loader disassemblies recreate the original files byte-for-byte, including BASIC tokenization and rotated payload encoding.

vs64-c64-vscode-development.title: vs64
vs64-c64-vscode-development.display_title: VS64 — C64 IDE, compiler and debugger extension
source_language: C64 program code and disk/tape/resource formats
vs64-c64-vscode-development.notes: VS Code C64 development suite with toolchain, resource compilers, VICE debugging, embedded 6502 emulation and disassembly; Atari ST search origin was incidental.

vscode-amiga-assembly-debugger.title: vscode-amiga-assembly
vscode-amiga-assembly-debugger.display_title: Amiga Assembly for VS Code — build and disassembly debugger
vscode-amiga-assembly-debugger.notes: VS Code extension integrating VASM/VLINK, FS-UAE/WinUAE run/debug and Capstone disassembly for stack selection and source-less debugging.

jotd-vulgus-amiga.title: Vulgus — Amiga arcade transcode

runtime_profiles.name: AGA build
runtime_profiles.notes: README identifies the port as AGA; the linked main game, Amiga and VBR objects are assembled with -m68020. No complete RAM minimum is stated outside build-specific WHDLoad allocations.

jotd-vulgus-amiga.notes: AGA Amiga Vulgus port; README credits tcdev's full Z80 reverse engineering and jotd's 68000 transcode plus graphics/sound conversion.

monty-mole-spectrum-ritchie.title: Wanted: Monty Mole — Spectrum disassembly
monty-mole-spectrum-ritchie.notes: Separate annotated Wanted: Monty Mole Spectrum source with build script; short README and src tree establish work, not independently verified exactness.

warhawk-nintendo-ds-remake.title: Warhawk DS — C64 shooter reimagined in Nintendo DS ARM code
warhawk-nintendo-ds-remake.display_title: Warhawk DS — C64 shooter reimagined in Nintendo DS ARM code
warhawk-nintendo-ds-remake.status: Upstream v1.02 Nintendo DS release with 16 normal and 16 additional hard levels.
warhawk-nintendo-ds-remake.notes: Author calls this a reimagining of the 1986 C64 Warhawk. Gameplay collision and movement are direct ARM assembly; C support is used for libfat/EFS audio and storage. README documents native DS installation, playtesting and completion levels. Its mention of the DS 4 MB limitation explains external music storage and is not an explicit minimum-RAM requirement. Reviewed 2026-10-05. Build/run/play statements are upstream reports; no candidate code was compiled or executed in this review. Evidence: https://github.com/benbaker76/WarhawkDS/blob/master/README.md https://github.com/benbaker76/WarhawkDS/blob/master/WarhawkDS/arm9/source/collisiondetect.s https://github.com/benbaker76/WarhawkDS/blob/master/WarhawkDS/arm9/Makefile

warlord-spectrum.title: Warlord
warlord-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

watford-ddfs-154t-seddon.title: Watford 1770 DDFS 1.54T — ROM disassembly
watford-ddfs-154t-seddon.notes: A focused, partially annotated disassembly of Watford DDFS 1.54T created to investigate one fault. README provides a 64tass/Make build and explicitly calls out uncertain constants; it does not claim full understanding of the ROM.

wcdatool-watcom-dos-disassembler.title: wcdatool
wcdatool-watcom-dos-disassembler.display_title: wcdatool — Watcom DOS executable disassembly workbench
wcdatool-watcom-dos-disassembler.notes: Python workbench for disassembling Watcom-built DOS applications. It combines Open Watcom wdump and GNU objdump, applies per-executable hints, formats and deduplicates disassembly, and can reconstruct original module boundaries when debug symbols survive. The README documents Mortal Kombat origins and successful use on other games while explicitly bounding current control-flow limitations.

werner-mach-hin-st-reconstruction.title: Werner — mach hin!
werner-mach-hin-st-reconstruction.notes: Reconstructed the shipped game in Alcyon C, including all 238 game functions, and documents a make link step that compares its complete WERNER.PRG byte for byte with the original. Separate bug-fixed build deliberately differs; normal build retains original behavior.

west-bank-spectrum.title: West Bank
west-bank-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

wheelie-spectrum.title: Wheelie
wheelie-spectrum.notes: Pobtastic annotated ZX Spectrum disassembly created with SkoolKit.

where-time-stood-still-spectrum-analyser.title: Where Time Stood Still
where-time-stood-still-spectrum-analyser.display_title: Where Time Stood Still — ZX Spectrum analyser project
where-time-stood-still-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The directory contains a ~1.52 MB Analysis.json annotation database with project configuration; tracked as an analysis-state project rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

wikinger2-amiga-rust-port.title: Wikinger II — Amiga game reconstruction
wikinger2-amiga-rust-port.notes: Author analyzed the original ADF with Ghidra, IRA and FS-UAE and used AI to extract rules. Desktop port documents deviations; original save and highscores formats are byte-compatible, which does not imply a byte-exact game binary. README provides cargo run/install instructions.

bartmanabyss-winuae-amiga-debug.title: WinUAE
bartmanabyss-winuae-amiga-debug.notes: Fork of tracked tonioni/WinUAE for vscode-amiga-debug. Author commits add barto_gdbserver initialization protection, GDB acknowledgement handling, SR capture and CPU profiling hooks. Credit upstream emulation; distinct debugger integration is the promoted divergence.

winuae-amiga-emulator.title: WinUAE
winuae-amiga-emulator.notes: Actively maintained Windows Amiga emulator and a key compatibility/debugging tool for Amiga reverse engineering and retro development. Tracked as adjacent tooling rather than as a source-reconstruction target.

axewater-winuae-gdb-monitor.title: WinUAE — axewater GDB monitor extension
axewater-winuae-gdb-monitor.notes: Fork of BartmanAbyss/WinUAE; GitHub's compare against its parent shows one additional commit changing od-win32/barto_gdbserver.cpp to add monitor screenshot and disassembly commands. Credit tonioni/WinUAE as original emulator and BartmanAbyss's tracked GDB integration as direct parent. One 94-line file change is the distinct reviewed contribution.

wizard-of-wor-c64-disassembly.title: Wizard of Wor
wizard-of-wor-c64-disassembly.display_title: Wizard of Wor — C64 extensively documented disassembly
wizard-of-wor-c64-disassembly.notes: Extensively commented reverse-engineered C64 Wizard of Wor source. The README documents 64tass compilation to a cartridge binary and explains game initialization, graphics, audio, actor logic, timing, Magic Voice support and other internals.

wizball-c64-analyser.title: Wizball
wizball-c64-analyser.notes: Title-specific C64 binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Wizball directory contains a large Analysis.json annotation database (~736 KB) plus saved analyser/emulator state and configuration. This is tracked as an analysis-state project, not as a reconstructed source tree.

wizball-spectrum-analyser.title: Wizball
wizball-spectrum-analyser.notes: Title-specific ZX Spectrum binary-analysis state for 8-Bit Analysers. The Wizball directory contains an approximately 541 KiB Analysis.json annotation database; tracked as analysis-state work rather than a reconstructed-source claim.

wonder-boy-monsterland-st.title: Wonder Boy in Monsterland
wonder-boy-monsterland-st.notes: 330 functions verified; reconstructed game boots a real STE from its own floppy.

woods-rescue-amstrad-cpc.title: Woods Rescue — Amstrad CPC native game source
woods-rescue-amstrad-cpc.display_title: Woods Rescue — Amstrad CPC native game source
woods-rescue-amstrad-cpc.status: Substantial original source with a missing-Makefile build gap; reproducibility and playability unverified.
woods-rescue-amstrad-cpc.notes: Wodzaholic’s original native CPC game credits Mónica Rampérez Andrés, María Sánchez Tenías and Martín Quirante Berná. Source contains native game, entity, system and level code; disk, tape and snapshot files accompany it. Root README is only a title. One creator/team source release with ancillary artifacts; no original commercial subject or source reconstruction is asserted. Source/Compilation pins CPCtelera commit 2cff69fa0936714597a036da94b3d9db2bf5b2e7 and says make, but the complete recursive repository tree contains no Makefile. The source and prebuilt artifacts do not establish a clean rebuild. Compilation remains unknown and needs recovery; run/play/byte matching were not tested. Reviewed on 2026-10-05; no independent build or execution was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/monineun/Woods-Rescue/blob/master/Docs/Authors.txt https://github.com/monineun/Woods-Rescue/blob/master/Source/Compilation https://github.com/monineun/Woods-Rescue/blob/master/Source/src/man/game.s https://github.com/monineun/Woods-Rescue/blob/master/Source/cfg/build_config.mk. Latest upstream commit: https://github.com/monineun/Woods-Rescue/commit/dae2a52999394196268e1ce8d6c3520efd5ec895

xdebug-amplink-st-archival-tools.title: X-Debug / AmpLink — recovered Atari ST tool sources
xdebug-amplink-st-archival-tools.upstream_name: X-Debug / AmpLink — recovered Atari ST tool sources
xdebug-amplink-st-archival-tools.display_title: X-Debug / AmpLink — recovered Atari ST tool sources
xdebug-amplink-st-archival-tools.notes: Original author recovered early-1990s X-Debug debugger and AmpLink linker source from an old hard drive, with smaller utilities. AmpLink can emit Amiga images. README explicitly says the author can no longer build or verify these historical Lattice C/HiSoft GenST sources. Original source preservation is distinguished from a newly disassembled binary.

commander-x16-emulator.title: x16-emulator
commander-x16-emulator.notes: Open-source Commander X16 hardware emulator with VERA, storage and ROM support, useful for reproducible X16 development.

x68000-converters-hitchhikr.title: X68000 converters
x68000-converters-hitchhikr.notes: Python scripts convert X68000 ADPCM samples to WAV or signed PCM and chunky, planar and tile graphics to PNG. Scope is file-format conversion, not reconstruction of a particular program.

x68k2amiga-hitchhikr.title: x68k2amiga
x68k2amiga-hitchhikr.display_title: x68k2amiga — X68000-to-Amiga executable conversion & depacking tool
x68k2amiga-hitchhikr.notes: Amiga-hosted reverse-engineering utility for converting Sharp X68000 executables into Amiga executables for subsequent analysis. It reconstructs code/data/BSS hunks and relocations, handles packed X68000 executables and can depack/extract several X68000 archive, executable and sample formats.

xdms-rs-amiga-dms.title: xdms-rs
xdms-rs-amiga-dms.notes: Rust port of xDMS providing CLI and library to unpack Amiga DMS disks to ADF. Implements all seven compression modes; README notes DEEP lacks an end-to-end fixture, while HEAVY modes were compared byte for byte with reference C xDMS on public-domain images. Byte exact here concerns decoded fixtures, not historical executable reconstruction.

xevious-68k-jotd-tcdev.title: Xevious
xevious-68k-jotd-tcdev.notes: 68k transcode of the original Xevious arcade game. The README explicitly states that multiple Z80 GAME/SUB CPU ROMs were disassembled/reverse engineered and transcoded line-by-line to platform-agnostic 68k core code, with playable Neo Geo and Amiga targets.

xfdmaster-amiga-decrunch.title: XFDMaster — Amiga packed file decruncher

runtime_profiles.name: m68k AmigaOS library
runtime_profiles.notes: Aminet classifies the package as m68k-amigaos and the package description requires Kickstart V33+. It gives no exact 680x0 model or RAM minimum.

xfdmaster-amiga-decrunch.notes: Canonical Aminet XFD system for detecting and decompressing packed files, executables and data. Release 1.38/39.15 is an m68k-amigaos library for Kickstart V33+; the inputs span many packer formats and therefore do not have one source CPU. The later AmigaOS 4.1 C port retains most slaves as 680x0 and is related rather than a separate original research subject.

xpack-linux-xpk.title: xPack — Linux port
xpack-linux-xpk.display_title: xPack — Amiga XPK unpacker for Linux
xpack-linux-xpk.notes: Linux port of historical xPack 1.5, with bundled XPK format implementation and NUKE/DUKE decompression. It reads XPK files and packs with the NONE method; not a reconstruction of the original xPack binary.

xpk-nuke-duke-decompressor.title: XPK NUKE/DUKE — Amiga decompressor
xpk-nuke-duke-decompressor.notes: Agent-facing Python decompressor for Amiga XPK NUKE and DUKE archives. README identifies codec as a port from temisu/ancient, not an independent reverse engineering of the original compressor; includes recursive file discovery and validation.

xrick-rick-dangerous-reimplementation.title: xrick
xrick-rick-dangerous-reimplementation.notes: README identifies the original IBM PC x86 and Atari ST 68k executables as the reverse-engineering inputs for the C reimplementation. The current build script produces Windows x64 and WebAssembly builds and runs PC/ST test paths; no byte-exact reconstruction or minimum host RAM is claimed.

xrick-rick-dangerous-knowledge-base.title: xrick-kb
xrick-rick-dangerous-knowledge-base.display_title: xrick-kb — Rick Dangerous reverse-engineering knowledge base
xrick-rick-dangerous-knowledge-base.notes: Independent research corpus embedded alongside xrick as a submodule. The Rick Dangerous Atari ST knowledge base reports every function reversed, 47 rooms rendered and extensive byte-identity/live-Hatari audits; the separate Rick Dangerous II corpus documents game logic, formats, gaps and a verified SNDH sound artifact.

xsdk-x68000-windows-toolchain.title: XSDK
xsdk-x68000-windows-toolchain.notes: Updated Windows X68000 SDK derived from Lyderic Maillet's human68k toolchain, with GCC 13.4.1, vasm/vlink, examples and includes. A development kit; upstream calls it work in progress.

xspeccy-mcp-agent-debugger.title: xspeccy-mcp ZX Spectrum emulator control
xspeccy-mcp-agent-debugger.notes: Headless Xpeccy-based MCP server exposes stepping, breakpoints, memory, screen/raster digests, profiling and capture for agent-controlled Spectrum debugging; README reports 53 tools. AI-assisted label is explicit.

yawi-sg1000-sc3000.title: Yawi
yawi-sg1000-sc3000.display_title: Yawi — native SG-1000 / SC-3000 Enigma remake
yawi-sg1000-sc3000.notes: Substantial native C gameplay has levels, movement, tile collisions, gold and teleport handling; SDCC -mz80 script links SGlib/PSGlib and emits .sg/.sc ROMs. Release describes Enigma-inspired Boulderdash/Sokoban/XOR game with keyboard and pad. No independent build/run. Published release guarantees only first two of twelve levels; cut levels and missing elements may prevent later completion. Script references external crt0 components. No guest game-CPU interpreter path. SMS Power publishes a playable SG release and original code. Only the first two of twelve levels are stated completable; absent mechanics may block others. Source rebuild was not repeated and its external crt0 setup is not fully established.

yoshi-nes-mstan-recomp.title: YoshiNESRecomp

execution_paths.name: native PC build
execution_paths.notes: Runs generated native host code while the shared NESRecomp runner simulates NES hardware; it is not a guest-CPU emulator path.

yoshi-nes-mstan-recomp.notes: Independent game project built on NESRecomp. The primary README states that original 6502 ROM machine code is translated to C and compiled to native x64. Single-player, two-player and demo paths are documented as running end-to-end. User supplies the matching ROM; no ROM is distributed.

yoshis-cookie-nes-mstan-recomp.title: YoshisCookieRecomp

execution_paths.name: native PC build
execution_paths.notes: Runs generated native host code while the shared NESRecomp runner simulates NES hardware; it is not a guest-CPU emulator path.

yoshis-cookie-nes-mstan-recomp.notes: Independent game project built on NESRecomp. The primary README states that original 6502 ROM machine code is translated to C and compiled to native x64. README reports full 1P and VS play with zero oracle divergence against Nestopia. User supplies the matching ROM; no ROM is distributed.

z80-smart-disassembler-cormacj.title: z80-smart-disassembler
z80-smart-disassembler-cormacj.display_title: Z80 Smart Disassembler — CPC ROM analysis and assembler output
z80-smart-disassembler-cormacj.notes: Python Z80 disassembler developed to analyse Amstrad CPC ROMs; heuristically identifies strings/data and supports template and label files, cross references, and assembly output for several assemblers. The README documents a usable command-line interface, not a verified byte-exact source reconstruction.

z88dk-z80-development-kit.title: z88dk — Z80 development kit
z88dk-z80-development-kit.notes: Long-running C/assembly compiler, assembler, linker and machine libraries targeting over a hundred Z80-family machines, including CPC; one coherent toolkit at repository root.

zanac-msx-cleanroom-re.title: zanac-re
zanac-msx-cleanroom-re.display_title: Zanac — MSX clean-room AI reconstruction and disassembly
zanac-msx-cleanroom-re.notes: Clean-room investigation of Zanac's AI plus a full MSX1 Z80 disassembly and structured symbol/data/subsystem knowledge base. The documented workflow scopes Claude Code sprints, validates generated knowledge and requires operator review; no byte-exact or playable-reconstruction claim is made.

zany-kong-bbc-fizgog.title: Zany Kong BBC disassembly
zany-kong-bbc-fizgog.notes: BBC Micro Zany Kong assembly listing plus original disk material and imagery, credited to Christopher Hyde and Solar Soft; source completeness and byte matching untested.

zaxxon-c64-mikroman.title: Zaxxon
zaxxon-c64-mikroman.notes: Uncommented KickAssembler source splits banked C64 Zaxxon cartridge into four CHIP sections; build scripts reassemble a 20 KB CRT while accommodating a mirrored $9000 debug bank. Documentation describes a launchable result but exact matching was not verified.

dos-zeliard-masm.title: Zeliard
dos-zeliard-masm.display_title: Zeliard — bit-perfect MASM reconstruction and web port
dos-zeliard-masm.notes: Author reports release builds reproduce original DOS binaries and all three SAR archives bit for bit via build_masm.py --verify; the C/WebAssembly port is playable to the ending. Separate from awkto's independent Zeliard study and SDL port.

zerotape-great-escape-serialization-dpt.title: zerotape
source_language: The Great Escape C model state
zerotape-great-escape-serialization-dpt.notes: Structured-text C serializer built for saving and loading state in the tracked The Great Escape in C reconstruction. Uses ZT field macros and a Lemon-generated grammar; README documents integer-focused syntax and limitations. General-purpose library serving that project, not an original Spectrum tape format parser or binary-derived reconstruction.

zippy-race-amiga-ocs-lantus.title: ZippyRace-OCS
zippy-race-amiga-ocs-lantus.display_title: Zippy Race — OCS Amiga fan conversion

runtime_profiles.name: OCS Amiga
runtime_profiles.notes: README states 50/60 fps on any Amiga with 1 Meg; the Makefile explicitly compiles and assembles for 68000.

evidence.excerpt: runs at 50/60fps on any Amiga with 1Meg

zippy-race-amiga-ocs-lantus.notes: Hand-written fan conversion of Irem's 1983 arcade Zippy Race for OCS Amiga. The README explicitly states that no reverse engineering or transcoding was performed; the game was recreated by hand in C with some assembly to match the arcade original as closely as possible. It is tracked under the broader retro-development/homebrew scope rather than as an RE-derived port.

znax-amstrad-cpc-shinra.title: ZNAX — Amstrad CPC native puzzle-game source
znax-amstrad-cpc-shinra.display_title: ZNAX — Amstrad CPC native puzzle-game source
znax-amstrad-cpc-shinra.status: Original native source release; no independent compilation or execution in this review.
znax-amstrad-cpc-shinra.notes: Shinra’s Adrien Destugues and Cédric Quetier provide an original native CPC implementation of the credited ZNAX concept/rules. Code covers gameplay, scoring, keyboard and CPC hardware. The repository reports fifth place at CPCRetroDev 2015 and includes older development history. README credits original concept and rules to Nick Kouvaris/Lightforce, with this code/music by Adrien Destugues and graphics by Cédric Quetier. This attribution is preserved without claiming a binary-derived port or decompilation. Some source predates the 2015 competition, so no development start is inferred from repository creation. README documents vasm/vlink, CPCSDK utilities, Exomizer and make producing DSK/CDT, plus an emulator target. Arkos Tracker music relocation is explicitly manual. These instructions were not executed, so current compilability and playability remain unverified. Reviewed on 2026-10-05; no independent build or execution was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/CPCRetroDev/znax/blob/master/README.md https://github.com/CPCRetroDev/znax/blob/master/code/Makefile https://github.com/CPCRetroDev/znax/blob/master/code/src/GAME.z80. Latest upstream commit: https://github.com/CPCRetroDev/znax/commit/f192cdd1021466a2b76d68c467584daef98bad5f

zollowers-amstrad-cpc.title: Zollowers — Amstrad CPC native game source
zollowers-amstrad-cpc.display_title: Zollowers — Amstrad CPC native game source
zollowers-amstrad-cpc.status: Author-reported runnable on real CPC or emulator; build and complete playability unverified.
zollowers-amstrad-cpc.notes: Original assembly/CPCtelera game entered in CPCRetroDev 2022 by Adrian Marco Bru, Luis Ángel Sánchez Tomás and Jose Luis Boix Camarasa. Source implements game/entity management, physics, enemy behavior, collisions and level templates. README explicitly reports running on a real CPC or WinAPE. One original CPC title; Android export support is ancillary. Root GPLv3 and source LGPLv3 notices differ and require reconciliation. The reviewed README names the CPC family without establishing an exact CPC 464 minimum. The creator explicitly states real-CPC/emulator operation, supporting attributed runnable=true. compilation.txt gives make, but no current source build or complete-play verification was performed.
